verse-maat-pita-bandhu-sabke-wo.roman: Māt pitā bandhu sabake vo, jag ke pālanahār
verse-maat-pita-bandhu-sabke-wo.grammarNote: Compound list `Māt pitā bandhu` functioning as a predicate complement; `pālanahār` is an agentive noun formed with the suffix `-hār`.

verse3-4.source: ख़ुदा की क़सम दे दे दर्शन आके
verse3-4.roman: ḵẖudā kī qasam de de darśan āke
verse3-4.grammarNote: de de is a compound imperative (stem de + auxiliary de); ḵẖudā kī qasam functions as a solemn vocative/oath modifier.

verse2-3.source: मगर मेरे बस की ये बात नहीं है
verse2-3.roman: magar mere bas kī ye bāt nahī̃ hai
verse2-3.grammarNote: kī agrees in feminine gender with bāt; bas is a masculine noun borrowed from Persian meaning control/reach.

verse4-4.source: गले से लगा ले समाधि से उठ के
verse4-4.roman: gale se lagā le samādhi se uṭh ke

words.gloss: tomb; here Sāī Bābā’s burial shrine

verse4-4.grammarNote: Uṭh ke is a conjunctive participle: having risen. Samādhi se identifies the tomb from which the singer asks Baba to rise. Galē se lagā lē is an imperative asking to be embraced.

jehi-sumirat.grammarNote: Awadhi soraṭhā opening. 'Jēhi' is oblique relative pronoun functioning with the absolute present participle 'sumirata' ('upon remembering whom'). 'Sidhi' (Sanskrit siddhi) is the subject of intransitive 'hōī'.

muka-hoi.grammarNote: Subject 'mūka', copular verb 'hōi', predicate adjective 'bācāla'. Opening pāda of the second soraṭhā.

pangu-charhai.grammarNote: Subject 'paṅgu', verb 'caṛhai', direct object 'girivara' modified by postpositive adjective 'gahanā'.

words.gloss: bearing boons / holding the boon-bestowing gesture

verse-2-line-2.grammarNote: 'kara' functions in a locative sense ('in hand/hands'); 'varadhārē' is a compound adjective/participle (vara + dhārī/dhārē) in Braj masculine form.

refrain-ganapat-vighna-haran.english: {0:O Lord of the Ganas, }{1,2:remover of obstacles, }{3:O elephant-faced Lord,}
refrain-ganapat-vighna-haran.grammarNote: gaṇapata and gajānana are vocative nouns in Hindi/Braj; vighna harana is an agentive compound noun phrase functioning as an epithet.

prasanna-vadanam-dhyayet.english: {1:of }{0:serene }{1:countenance, }{2:one should meditate upon Him }{5:for the pacification }{3:of all }{4:obstacles.}

words.gloss: one with a countenance, face: accusative

prasanna-vadanam-dhyayet.grammarNote: prasannavadanam is an accusative singular masculine Bahuvrīhi compound; dhyāyet is a 3rd person singular optative (vidhiliṅ) from root dhyā; sarvavighnopaśāntaye is a dative singular feminine tatpuruṣa compound of purpose.

chanchala-shashi-prabhu-stuti.source: चञ्चल शशि प्रभु स्तुति करत हैं
chanchala-shashi-prabhu-stuti.roman: cañcala śaśi prabhu stuti karata haiṁ
chanchala-shashi-prabhu-stuti.grammarNote: cañcala is an adjective modifying the masculine subject śaśi; stuti karata haiṁ is a compound verb construction with honorific/plural auxiliary haiṁ.

sphatika-rachita-pithe.grammarNote: Two locative singular compound nominals: 'sphaṭika-racita-pīṭhe' (tatpuruṣa) and 'ramya-kailāsa-śṛṅge' (karmadhāraya/tatpuruṣa).

vikacha-kamala-patrair.english: {3:worshipping }{4:the Great Lord }{2:with the petals }{0:of fully blossomed }{1:lotuses,}
vikacha-kamala-patrair.grammarNote: Sandhi merger: instrumental plural 'patraiḥ' + accusative feminine singular present active participle 'arcayantīm' (√arc); 'maheśam' is accusative masculine singular.

words.gloss: solid, the cymbal class of instrument

kara-dhruta-ghana-vadya.grammarNote: Feminine nominative singular bahuvrīhi compound: kara (hand) + dhṛta (held) + ghana-vādya (solid musical instrument).

pita-varna-yatakshi.grammarNote: Feminine nominative singular compound combining bahuvrīhi elements: pīta-varṇā (yellow-complexioned) and āyata-akṣī (having elongated eyes).

sukavibhir-iyam-ukta.grammarNote: Sandhi combination: 'sukavibhiḥ' (instrumental plural masculine) + 'iyam' (nominative feminine singular demonstrative pronoun) + 'uktā' (nominative feminine singular past passive participle of √vac).

words.gloss: fierce feminine form or consort of Bhairava

bhairavi-bhairava-stri.grammarNote: Nominative feminine singular proper noun 'Bhairavī' with genitive tatpuruṣa compound 'bhairava-strī' (nominative feminine singular).

main-dharun-tiharo-dhyan.grammarNote: Braj/Hindi first-person singular indicative: 'maĩ' (subject) + 'dharū̃' (verb from dharnā) governing the direct object phrase 'tihāro dhyān'.

dhyan-main-dharun.grammarNote: Fronted direct object 'dhyān' preceding the full clause 'maĩ dharū̃ tihāro dhyān'.

han-main-dharun.grammarNote: Affirmative particle 'hā̃' introducing the standard 1st person singular clause 'maĩ dharū̃ tihāro dhyān'.

bhava-bhava-vibhava-parabhava-karini.grammarNote: Feminine agent noun 'kārini' (Sanskrit kāriṇī) governing the compound direct object 'bhava-bhava-bibhava-parābhava' in vocative/nominative epithet form.

words.gloss: self-governed; autonomous; under her own will

visva-vimohani-svabasa-biharini.grammarNote: Two coordinated feminine agent nouns ending in '-ini': 'bisva-bimohani' (vimohanī) and 'bihārini' (vihāriṇī), the latter modified by the adjectival/adverbial 'svabasa' (Sanskrit svavaśā).

v1-1.source: ऐसी भूल भई क्या करनी संकट टारो ना
v1-1.roman: Aisī bhūl bhaī kyā karanī saṅkaṭ ṭāro nā
v1-1.grammarNote: Braj bhaī is feminine singular past tense agreeing with bhūl; karanī is feminine noun ('actions/deeds'); ṭāro nā is 2nd-person respectful imperative with entreating particle.

v1-2.source: बिगड़ गई कछु रही न बाकी
v1-2.roman: Bigaṛ gaī kachu rahī na bākī
v1-2.grammarNote: Compound verb bigaṛ gaī (intransitive change of state, feminine singular). Braj indefinite kachu paired with negative na and bākī forms a total negative.

v3-1.source: कारन कौन भयो जग जननी सो दुःख जारो ना
v3-1.roman: Kāran kaun bhayo jag jananī so duḥkh jāro nā
v3-1.english: {1:What }{0:cause }{2:has arisen, }{3,4:O Mother of the World? }{8:Please }{7:burn away }{5:that }{6:sorrow.}
v3-1.grammarNote: Interrogative clause Kāran kaun bhayo; jag jananī is vocative compound noun; so duḥkh is direct object of imperative jāro (Braj form of jalānā) with particle nā.

v3-1-part.grammarNote: Interrogative sentence fragment with vocative compound jag jananī.

v3-3.grammarNote: Direct object pronoun Sab; niravāro is Braj 2nd-person respectful imperative from niravārnā (cognate to nivārnā/nibaṛnā) with entreating particle nā.

sikhi-atai-sangti-parbrahm-kar-namaskari.source: ਸਿਖੀ ਅਤੈ ਸੰਗਤੀ ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮੁ ਕਰਿ ਨਮਸਕਾਰਿਆ
sikhi-atai-sangti-parbrahm-kar-namaskari.roman: Sikhī atai saṅgatī pārbrahmu kari namaskāriā
sikhi-atai-sangti-parbrahm-kar-namaskari.english: {0:The disciples }{1:and }{2:the congregations }{5:have bowed to You, }{4:recognizing You as }{3:Pārbrahm.}

words.gloss: by the disciples; by the Sikhs
by the congregations; by the spiritual gatherings
Supreme Brahman, the highest divine reality; para means supreme, and Brahman the great
having recognized as; considering; regarding as

sikhi-atai-sangti-parbrahm-kar-namaskari.grammarNote: Ergative plural subjects `sikhī` and `saṅgatī` govern the transitive perfective verb `namaskāriā`. The conjunctive participle `kari` ('having regarded/treated as') takes `pārbrahmu` (with nominative/accusative short -u) as its complement.

parbrahm-kar-namaskari-a.english: {1:Recognizing You as }{0:Pārbrahm, }{2:they have bowed to You.}

words.gloss: Supreme Brahman, the highest divine reality; para means supreme, and Brahman the great
having recognized as; considering; regarding as

parbrahm-kar-namaskari-a.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle `kari` functions adverbially to denote the mental attitude/recognition with which the main verbal action `namaskāriā` is performed.

jini-tu-sevi-a-bhao-kar-se-tudh-paar-uta.source: ਜਿਨੀ ਤੂ ਸੇਵਿਆ ਭਾਉ ਕਰਿ ਸੇ ਤੁਧੁ ਪਾਰਿ ਉਤਾਰਿਆ
jini-tu-sevi-a-bhao-kar-se-tudh-paar-uta.roman: Jinī tū seviā bhāu kari se tudhu pāri utāriā
jini-tu-sevi-a-bhao-kar-se-tudh-paar-uta.english: {0:Those who }{2:have served }{1:You }{4:with }{3:loving devotion, }{5:them }{6:You }{8:have carried across }{7:to the other shore.}
jini-tu-sevi-a-bhao-kar-se-tudh-paar-uta.grammarNote: Relative-correlative structure: `jinī` (rel. erg. pl.) corresponds to `se` (correl. pl. direct object of `utāriā`). `Tudhu` is the agentive/instrumental form of the 2nd person pronoun. `Pāri` acts as a directional preverb with causal/transitive `utāriā`.

verse-1c.source: ਉਪਦੇਸਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪੁ ਜਾਪੈ
verse-1c.roman: upadesi gurū hari hari japu jāpai
verse-1c.english: {0:Following the instruction }{1:of the Guru, }{5:they chant }{4:the recitation }{2:“Hari, }{3:Hari”;}

words.gloss: through the teaching; by the instruction
The one who takes away—the remover; a divine name of Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa.
The one who takes away—the remover; a divine name of Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa.

verse-1c.grammarNote: upadēsi carries the instrumental/locative inflection -i; japu jāpai is a cognate internal accusative-verb construction.

dhoop-malianlo.source: ਧੂਪੁ ਮਲਆਨਲੋ ਪਵਣੁ ਚਵਰੋ ਕਰੇ ਸਗਲ ਬਨਰਾਇ ਫੂਲੰਤ ਜੋਤੀ ॥
dhoop-malianlo.roman: dhūpu malaānalo pavaṇu cavaro kare sagala banarāi phūlanta jotī ॥
dhoop-malianlo.english: {1:The sandalwood breeze }{0:is incense, }{2:the wind }{4:waves }{3:the fly-whisk, }{5:and all }{6:vegetation }{7:bears flowers }{8:for the divine Light.}
dhoop-malianlo.grammarNote: Malaānalo names the breeze from the sandalwood-bearing Malaya mountains. Pavaṇu is the subject of kare, with cavaro as its object. Phūlanta describes the vegetation bearing flowers; jotī names the divine Light for whom those flowers are offered.

line-002.source: ਸੁਖ ਸਨੇਹੁ ਅਰੁ ਭੈ ਨਹੀ ਜਾ ਕੈ
line-002.roman: sukh sanehu aru bhai nahī jā kai
line-002.grammarNote: Sukha sanehu means attachment to pleasure: sukha qualifies sanehu rather than forming a separate item in the list. The relative possessive phrase jā kai locates the absence of that attachment and of fear in the person described.

line-014.source: ਸੁਖ ਸਨੇਹੁ ਅਰੁ ਭੈ ਨਹੀ ਜਾ ਕੈ
line-014.roman: sukh sanehu ar bhai nahī jā kai
line-014.grammarNote: Sukha sanehu means attachment to pleasure: sukha qualifies sanehu rather than forming a separate item in the list. The relative possessive phrase jā kai locates the absence of that attachment and of fear in the person described.

line-025.source: ਸੁਖ ਸਨੇਹੁ ਅਰੁ ਭੈ ਨਹੀ ਜਾ ਕੈ
line-025.roman: sukha sanehu aru bhai nahī jā kai
line-025.grammarNote: Sukha sanehu means attachment to pleasure: sukha qualifies sanehu rather than forming a separate item in the list. The relative possessive phrase jā kai locates the absence of that attachment and of fear in the person described.

line-040.english: {0,1:With eyes brimming with tears, }{2:she draws }{3:deep sighs.}
line-040.grammarNote: locana bharī is a participial clause describing state; le is a conjunctive/present participle governing the direct object usāsā.

line-021.source: ਸੇਵ ਕਰੀ ਪਲੁ ਚਸਾ ਨ ਵਿਛੁੜਾ
line-021.roman: sev karī palu casā na vichuṛā
line-021.english: {0,1:I shall render service }{4,5:and not part }{2:for a moment }{3:or an instant,}
line-021.grammarNote: sev karī is a 1st person singular present/future conjunct verb; palu casā are adverbial accusatives of duration; vichuṛā is a 1st person singular present/subjunctive verb with negative particle na.

line-000.source: ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਲੋਚੈ ਗੁਰ ਦਰਸਨ ਤਾਈ ॥
line-000.roman: merā manu locai gur darasana tāī ॥
line-000.grammarNote: merā manu is masculine singular nominative; locai is a 3rd person singular present indicative verb; tāī is a postposition governing the compound/genitive phrase gur darasana.

line-003.source: ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ ਨ ਉਤਰੈ ਸਾਂਤਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ਬਿਨੁ ਦਰਸਨ ਸੰਤ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥
line-003.roman: trikhā na utarai sānti na āvai binu darasana santa piāre jīu ॥
line-003.english: {0:Thirst }{1,2:does not subside }{3:and peace }{4,5:does not come }{6:without }{7:the sight }{9:of the beloved }{10:and revered }{8:Saint.}
line-003.grammarNote: Compound coordinate clause with two negated 3rd person singular present verbs (utarai, āvai); binu acts as a preposition governing the oblique noun phrase darasana santa piāre; jīu is an honorific particle.

line-012.source: ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਲੋਚੈ ਗੁਰ ਦਰਸਨ ਤਾਈ ॥
line-012.roman: merā manu locai gur darasana tāī ॥
line-012.grammarNote: merā manu is the subject; locai is a third-person singular present verb. tāī marks the purpose or object of longing: the sight of the Guru.

line-023.source: ਗੁਰ ਦਰਸਨ ਤਾਈ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਲੋਚੈ
line-023.roman: gur darasana tāī merā manu locai
line-023.grammarNote: Syntactic permutation of the opening line with the postpositional phrase fronted for lyrical emphasis.

line-024.source: ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ ਨ ਉਤਰੈ ਸਾਂਤਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ
line-024.roman: trikhā na utarai sānti na āvai
line-024.grammarNote: Coordinate negated clauses with parallel 3rd person singular present indicative verbs (utarai, āvai).

line-028.source: ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ ਨ ਉਤਰੈ ਸਾਂਤਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ਬਿਨੁ ਦਰਸਨ ਸੰਤ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥
line-028.roman: trikhā na utarai sānti na āvai binu darasana santa piāre jīu
line-028.english: {0:Thirst }{1,2:does not subside }{3:and peace }{4,5:does not come }{6:without }{7:the sight }{9:of the beloved }{10:and revered }{8:Saint.}
line-028.grammarNote: Full verse line repeated with phonetic transcription variants (piāre, jīu).

line-037.grammarNote: Incomplete melodic line; manu is nominative subject with negated 3rd person singular present verb rahai.

line-038.source: ਮਨੁ ਨ ਰਹੈ ਬਹੁ ਬਿਧਿ ਉਮਕਾਈ ॥
line-038.roman: manu na rahai bahu bidhi umakāī
line-038.english: {0:The mind }{1,2:does not stay still; }{3:in so many }{4:ways }{5:it surges with longing.}

words.gloss: surges up; leaps with eager yearning

line-038.grammarNote: bahu bidhi is an adverbial phrase of manner ('in many ways'); umakāī is a 3rd person singular present/perfective verb expressing enthusiastic swelling of emotion.

words.gloss: woman; bride, here the yearning devotee

line-039.grammarNote: panthu has the masculine nominative/accusative -u ending; kāmanī is a feminine singular subject with 3rd person singular present indicative verb nihārai.

line-044.english: {0:I think of that sight }{1:day after day, }{2:without cease.}
line-044.grammarNote: citavau is first-person: I think of or remember. The object, the longed-for sight, is carried over from the preceding line. anadinu and nīta reinforce the continuity of this longing.

editorialAdjustments.reason: The expansive speaker is Tuka; the inner lamp supports awakening, but neither establishes divine pervasion under this controlled definition. The finite-verb correction does not add that evidence.

verse-3b.english: {0:I have remained}{1: solely for doing good.”}
verse-3b.grammarNote: Uraloṁ is 1st person singular past/perfect of uraṇe ('to remain'); upakārāpuratā is a compound of upakāra (dative/oblique upakārā-) + puratā ('sufficient for / restricted only to').

refrain-beet-gaye.source: बीत गये दिन भजन बिना रे
refrain-beet-gaye.roman: Bīt gaye din bhajan binā re
refrain-beet-gaye.grammarNote: Compound verb bīt gaye (bītnā + jānā) in perfective aspect, agreeing with masculine plural subject din. Binā is a postposition governing the preceding noun bhajan.

words.gloss: for the sake of / cause / reason

v2-lahe-karan.grammarNote: Lāhe is the oblique form of lāhā (Braj/Old Hindi for profit). Gavāyo is masculine singular perfective agreeing with mūl.

closing-bhajan-bina.grammarNote: Elliptical postpositional phrase echoing the coda of the refrain.

v3-line2.grammarNote: 'gumānī' is used vocatively / as the agent descriptor; 'vahām̐ kī' has an implicit feminine noun head like 'bāt' or 'cintā'; copula 'hai' is elided after participle 'karatā'.

v2-line3.source: ये तो पलक पीछे उड़ जावे
v2-line3.roman: Ye to palak pīche uṛ jāve

words.gloss: goes / vanishes [3rd sg. present/subjunctive of jānā]

v2-line3.grammarNote: Compound verb 'uṛ jāve' (polar verb stem 'uṛ' + vector 'jāve'). 'palak pīche' functions as a temporal adverbial phrase.

words.gloss: I speak / I say [1st person singular present/subjunctive]

v3-line1.grammarNote: 'sun' is an imperative; 'kahūm̐' is a 1st person singular verb; 'paramānī' is a postnominal adjective modifying feminine noun 'bāt'.

ref-1.grammarNote: Elided present copula (hain). 'paisā ke' is oblique genitive modifying the plural predicate nominative 'bhāī'.

ref-2.grammarNote: Initial 'Bhāī' is vocative singular; final 'bhāī' is plural predicate noun. Copula is elided.

verse1-line2.source: प्राणी इसका हित कछु कर ले
verse1-line2.roman: Prāṇī iskā hit kachu kar le
verse1-line2.grammarNote: Vocative `prāṇī`; pronoun `iskā` refers back to `nar deh`; compound imperative `kar le`.

verse3-line3.source: जब लग पल्लो में पैसा भाई
verse3-line3.roman: Jab lag pallo mẽ paisā bhāī
verse3-line3.english: {0,1:As long as }{4:there is money }{2,3:in the hem of your garment, }{5:brother,}

words.gloss: hem of the garment / fold of cloth / pocket

verse3-line3.grammarNote: Temporal subordinator `jab lag` + locative phrase `pallo mẽ` (pallo is dialectal locative/oblique of pallā) + subject `paisā` + vocative `bhāī`.

words.gloss: yoga / ascetic discipline (masculine noun, Skt. yoga)
skill / contrivance / technique (feminine noun, Skt. yukti)
attains / obtains / reaches (3rd person singular present/habitual)

verse1-3.grammarNote: Alliterative paired nominals 'joga jugata' functioning as instrumental means or topic; transitive verb 'pāve' negated by 'nahiṁ' with elided divine object.

words.gloss: King Rāma / Sovereign Lord Rāma (compound noun); Rāma means “pleasing” or “delightful”

refrain-raja-ram.grammarNote: Compound proper noun 'rājārāma' as direct object of the repeated honorific imperative verb 'kaho'.

words.gloss: King Rāma / Sovereign Lord Rāma (compound noun); Rāma means “pleasing” or “delightful”

refrain-raja-ram-end.grammarNote: Direct object plus imperative verb with honorific clitic.

words.gloss: mystical diagrams / amulets / occult devices (masculine noun, Skt. yantra)
incantations / spells / mantras (masculine noun, Skt. mantra)
becomes / turns out (3rd person singular/plural present verb)

verse3-4.grammarNote: Rhyming dvandva pair 'jantara mantara' acting as subject to the intransitive verb 'hove' with predicate adjective 'laṭapaṭa'.

v1-l3a.grammarNote: Indefinite pronoun 'Koī' modifying masculine noun 'bakhat' (tadbhava of waqt); demonstrative 'aisā'; 3rd person masculine singular future verb 'āvegā'.

nayan-diye-darshan-karne-ko.grammarNote: Ergative/passive alignment with implied agent; plural direct object 'nayana' agrees with plural perfective verb 'diye'; purposive infinitive construction 'karane ko'.

words.gloss: vocative/emphatic particle calling the listener’s attention

hari-bhajan-ko-maan-re.grammarNote: Simple imperative 'māna' with direct object marked by 'ko' and closing vocative enclitic 're'.

words.gloss: do / give / perform [imperative / truncated purposive infinitive]

haath-diye-kar-daan-re.grammarNote: Masculine plural noun 'hātha' agrees with 'diye'; 'kara dāna' functions as an elliptical purposive or direct imperative command followed by vocative 're'.

words.gloss: is produced / arises / is yielded [imperfective participle / habitual verb]

kanchan-nipjat-khaan-re.grammarNote: Habitual/present participle 'nipajata' with subject 'kañcana' and bare locative/ablative noun 'khāna' (in/from the mine), typical of Braj/Old Hindi syntax lacking an explicit postposition.

refrain-2.grammarNote: Perfective participle paṛe functions as a finite resultant verb agreeing with masculine plural subject hama. Appositional noun phrase dāsa tumhāre modifies hama.

verse-4-karma.grammarNote: yaha karma gati is the subject noun phrase; balavānā is predicate adjective modifying the feminine noun gati (adapted masculine/tatsama inflection in Braj/Hindi verse).

verse-4-bhoge.source: भोगे बिन होय न हाना जी
verse-4-bhoge.roman: bhoge bina hoya na hānā jī
verse-4-bhoge.grammarNote: bhoge is oblique verbal noun from bhoganā governed by bina; hoya is 3rd person singular present; hānā (Sanskrit hāni) is nominative subject noun meaning destruction or loss; na is pre-verbal negation.

verse1-line2.grammarNote: Compound verb 'miṭa gaī' (miṭnā + jānā) in feminine singular perfective agreeing with 'khaiñcātānī'.

words.gloss: the Master; the inner Lord; the Sovereign

verse2-line2.grammarNote: 'lāyā' is used here in the sense of 'lagāyā' (joined/fastened), taking 'dhyāna' as direct object and 'dhanī se' as postpositional complement.

words.gloss: the complete one; the perfect master

pickup-pura.grammarNote: Incomplete conditional protasis clause functioning as a musical pickup.

verse-4.grammarNote: Inverted poetic word order (Object-Verb-Subject: `bhāva` [O] `karata` [V] `śūlapānī` [S]); `śūlapānī` is a bahuvrīhi compound (`śūla` + `pāṇi`, 'having a trident in hand').

verse-2b.grammarNote: Nominal predicate sentence with elided copula; feminine noun dhvani takes the feminine adjective piyārī.

aankh-jo-bhaaye.source: आँख जो भाये वो कोरा सपना
aankh-jo-bhaaye.roman: Ā̃kha jō bhāyē vō kōrā sapanā
aankh-jo-bhaaye.grammarNote: Relative-correlative construction 'jō ... vō'; 'ā̃kha' takes experiential dative sense with verb 'bhāyē'; copula 'hai' is elided after 'sapanā'.

man-sun-meri.source: मन सुन मेरी कान लगा के
man-sun-meri.roman: Mana suna mērī kāna lagā kē
man-sun-meri.grammarNote: 'Mana' is vocative; 'suna' is the informal 2nd person singular imperative; 'mērī' (feminine possessive) modifies an elided feminine noun such as 'bāt' (word/counsel); 'kāna lagā kē' is a conjunctive participial clause functioning adverbially.

jin-charno-mein-tirath-base-hain.source: जिन चरणों में तीरथ बसे हैं
jin-charno-mein-tirath-base-hain.roman: jin caraṇõ mẽ tīrath base haĩ
jin-charno-mein-tirath-base-hain.grammarNote: `jin caraṇõ mẽ` is a locative phrase formed with the oblique relative pronoun `jin`; `tīrath` functions as masculine plural subject agreeing with `base haĩ`.

jin-pairon-ko-muni-dhote-hain.source: जिन पैरों को मुनि धोते हैं
jin-pairon-ko-muni-dhote-hain.roman: jin pairõ ko muni dhote haĩ
jin-pairon-ko-muni-dhote-hain.grammarNote: `jin pairõ ko` is the marked direct object; `muni` is plural subject agreeing with habitual present verb `dhote haĩ`.

jin-charno-mein-mera-jeevan-basa-hai.source: जिन चरणों में मेरा जीवन बसा है
jin-charno-mein-mera-jeevan-basa-hai.roman: jin caraṇõ mẽ merā jīvan basā hai
jin-charno-mein-mera-jeevan-basa-hai.grammarNote: `merā jīvan` is masculine singular subject agreeing with `basā hai`; `jin caraṇõ mẽ` is locative complement.

refrain-3.source: ये मन न जाने क्या-क्या कराए
refrain-3.roman: ye mana na jāne kyā-kyā karāye
refrain-3.grammarNote: mana functions as the subject of causative verb karāye (3rd person singular present/habitual subjunctive); na jāne acts as a parenthetical idiom.

words.gloss: desireless; unselfish; free of personal motive
may I make; may I transform

verse2-2.grammarNote: Reflexive pronoun apane with accusative postposition ko; banāūṁ is 1st person singular subjunctive of causative banānā.

man-me-khayal-leke.source: मन में ख़याल लेके साईं को पुकार ले
man-me-khayal-leke.roman: man mẽ khayāl leke sāī̃ ko pukār le
man-me-khayal-leke.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle 'leke' coordinates the prior mental preparation with the compound imperative 'pukār le' (stem 'pukār' + reflexive auxiliary 'lenā').

bandhan-ka-prem-dhaga.source: बंधन का प्रेम धागा पार लगाए ना
bandhan-ka-prem-dhaga.roman: bandhan kā prem dhāgā pār lagāe nā

jeevan-ki-reet-ko.source: जीवन की रीत को तू थोड़ा सा सुधार ले
jeevan-ki-reet-ko.roman: jīvan kī rīt ko tū thoṛā sā sudhār le
jeevan-ki-reet-ko.grammarNote: Direct object 'jīvan kī rīt' marked by accusative 'ko'; explicit subject pronoun 'tū'; predicate is the compound imperative 'sudhār le'.

tum-pooja-phir-arpan.source: तुम पूजा फिर अर्पण हो साईं, जग माया के अंत हो

a context-dependent power or condition of worldly appearance

tum-pooja-phir-arpan.grammarNote: Compound verse with two parallel copular predicates ('pūjā phir arpaṇ ho' and 'jag māyā ke ant ho') sharing subject 'tum'.

prem-gyan-bhakti-ka-saath-ho.source: प्रेम ज्ञान भक्ति का साथ हो
prem-gyan-bhakti-ka-saath-ho.roman: Prem jñān bhakti kā sāth ho

prem-gyan-bhakti-ka-saath-ho.grammarNote: Subjunctive 3rd person singular verb ho with compound nominal modifier prem jñān bhakti governing the masculine head noun sāth.

akhil-vishwa-ke-bhakta.source: अखिल विश्व के भक्त तुम्हारा ध्यान सदा धरते

akhil-vishwa-ke-bhakta.grammarNote: Masculine plural subject 'bhakta' with genitive dependent 'akhil viśva ke'; conjunct verb 'dhyān dharate'.

mandir-me-baj-uthi-ghantiya.source: मंदिर में बज उठीं घंटियाँ, शंख भी ये कहते
mandir-me-baj-uthi-ghantiya.roman: Mandira meṁ baja uṭhīṁ ghaṇṭiyāṁ, śaṅkha bhī ye kahate
mandir-me-baj-uthi-ghantiya.english: {0,1:In the temple,} {4:bells} {2,3:have burst into ringing,} {5:and conch shells} {6:also} {8:proclaim} {7:this:}

madhur-raseeli-murali-ki-dhun.roman: Madhura rasīlī muralī kī dhuna kī sudhā barasāo hama para

he-pavan-parameshwar.source: हे पावन परमेश्वर मेरे मन ही मन शरमाऊँ

nain-moond-kar.source: नैन मूंदकर हे परमेश्वर कभी न तुझको ध्याया

v7-l3.source: जाए सहाय भयो तब ही अहिरावन सैन्य समेत संहारो ।

line-115.source: पूँछिहु नाथ राम कटकाई। बदन कोटि सत बरनि न जाई॥ नाना बरन भालु कपि भारी। बिकटानन बिसाल भयकारी॥
line-115.roman: pūm̐chihu nātha rāma kaṭakāī | badana koṭi sata barani na jāī || nānā barana bhālu kapi bhārī | bikaṭānana bisāla bhayakārī ||
line-115.english: {0:You asked, }{1:O lord, }{2:about Rama’s }{3:army; }{7,8,9:it cannot be described }{6:even with a hundred }{5:crore }{4:mouths! }{14:There are massive }{12:bears }{13:and monkeys }{10,11:of manifold hues, }{15:fierce-faced, }{16:colossal, }{17:and terrifying.}

words.gloss: Rāma, the delightful one; Viṣṇu’s avatāra and husband of Sītā

line-115.grammarNote: badana koṭi sata is an instrumental phrase of means. barani na jāī is a passive potential construction.

line-118.source: ए कपि सब सुग्रीव समाना। इन्ह सम कोटिन्ह गनइ को नाना॥ राम कृपाँ अतुलित बल तिन्हहीं। तृन समान त्रैलोकहि गनहीं॥
line-118.roman: e kapi saba sugrīva samānā | inha sama koṭinha ganai ko nānā || rāma kṛpām̐ atulita bala tinhahīṃ | tṛna samāna trailokahi ganahīṃ ||
line-118.english: {2:All }{0:these }{1:monkeys }{3,4:are equal to Sugriva; }{9:who }{8:can count }{10:the manifold }{7:crores }{6:like }{5:them? }{11:By Rama’s }{12:grace, }{13,15:unto them is incomparable }{14:strength; }{19:they deem }{18:the three worlds }{17:as equal to }{16:a blade of grass.}

words.gloss: of Rāma, the delightful Lord of Ayodhyā, Sītā’s husband

line-118.grammarNote: kṛpām̐ has an instrumental nasalization. trailokahi carries the accusative marker -hi. ko ganai forms a rhetorical question signifying infinite numbers.

line-122.source: सहज सूर कपि भालु सब पुनि सिर पर प्रभु राम
line-122.roman: sahaja sūra kapi bhālu saba puni sira para prabhu rāma
line-122.english: {0:By nature, }{4:all }{2:the monkeys }{3:and bears }{1:are heroic, }{5:and moreover, }{8:Lord }{9:Rama }{7:stands over }{6:their heads.}

words.gloss: Rāma, the delightful one; Viṣṇu’s avatāra and husband of Sītā

line-122.grammarNote: Nominal clause without explicit copula. 'sira para' is a postpositional locative phrase indicating protection and sovereignty.

words.gloss: Rāma, the delightful one; Viṣṇu’s avatāra and husband of Sītā

line-124.grammarNote: rāma is in genitive relation to the compound/series of nouns teja, bala, budhi, bipulāī.

line-127.grammarNote: pūcheu is 3sg past indicative in Awadhi. bhrātahi has the accusative/dative inflection -hi ('to the brother'). naya nāgara is an appositive epithet of Rama.

words.gloss: having relied upon; taking as firm

line-132.grammarNote: kar is genitive postposition equivalent to modern kā. dṛṛhāī is a conjunctive participle / absolutive in Awadhi.

words.gloss: do you make; do you do

line-134.grammarNote: mūṛha is vocative. kā is interrogative adverb ('why'). karasi is Awadhi 2sg present indicative.

words.gloss: having caused to read; having had read

line-141.grammarNote: Bacāi is an absolutive form of the causative verb bacānā (to cause to read / vācana). Juṛāvahu is a second-person plural/polite imperative.

line-143.english: and {1:summoning }{0:a minister, }{2:the fool }{3:began }{4:to have it read aloud:}

words.gloss: to have read aloud; to cause to read

line-143.grammarNote: Boli is an absolutive participle (bolāi / having summoned). Lāga + inflected infinitive bacāvana forms an inceptive aspect construction.

line-148.source: सुनत सभय मन मुख मुसुकाई। कहत दसानन सबहि सुनाई॥
line-148.roman: sunata sabhaya mana mukha musukāī. kahata dasānana sabahi sunāī.
line-148.english: {0:Hearing it, }{1:fearful }{2:in mind }{4:but smiling }{3:on his face, }{6:the ten-headed one }{5:spoke }{7:aloud for all }{8:to hear:}

words.gloss: upon hearing; as soon as he heard

line-148.grammarNote: Sunata is an imperfective temporal participle ('on hearing'). Mukha musukāī is an adverbial participial phrase of manner.

line-155.source: जब तेहिं कहा देन बैदेही। चरन प्रहार कीन्ह सठ तेही॥
line-155.roman: jaba tēhiṁ kahā dēna baidēhī. carana prahāra kīnha saṭha tēhī.
line-155.english: {0:When }{1:he }{2:spoke of }{3:giving up }{4:Vaidehī, }{8:the wretch }{7:struck }{9:him }{6:with a blow }{5:of his foot.}
line-155.grammarNote: Tēhiṁ is ergative singular ('by him'). Dēna is an inflected verbal noun / infinitive governing the object baidēhī.

line-156.source: नाइ चरन सिरु चला सो तहां। कृपासिंधु रघुनायक जहां॥
line-156.roman: nāi carana siru calā sō tahāṁ. kṛpāsiṁdhu raghunāyaka jahāṁ.
line-156.english: {0:Bowing }{2:his head }{1:at his feet, }{4:he }{3:departed }{5:there, }{8:where }{7:the Lord of the Raghus, }{6:the ocean of mercy, was.}
line-156.grammarNote: Nāi is an absolutive participle (from nāvanā / namana). Tahāṁ... jahāṁ forms a relative-correlative spatial clause.

line-169.source: कनक थार भरि मनि गन नाना। बिप्र रूप आयउ तजि माना॥
line-169.roman: kanaka thāra bhari mani gana nānā. bipra rūpa āyau taji mānā.
line-169.english: {2:filling }{0:a golden }{1:platter }{4:with heaps }{5:of manifold }{3:jewels, }{9:he set aside }{10:pride }{8:and came }{7:in the guise }{6:of a brāhmaṇa.}
line-169.grammarNote: 'kanaka thāra bhari' is an adverbial participial phrase of manner. 'bipra rūpa' is an adverbial noun phrase of assumed form.

line-170.source: काटहिं पइ कदरी फरइ कोटि जतन कउ सींच
line-170.roman: kāṭahiṁ pai kadarī pharai kōṭi jatana kau sīñca
line-170.english: {1:Only }{0:upon being cut }{2:does the plantain }{3:bear fruit, }{6:though }{7:watered }{4:with ten million }{5:efforts;}

words.gloss: upon being cut; only when cut

line-170.grammarNote: 'kāṭahiṁ pai' is an emphatic locative of condition (only upon being hewn). 'kau' acts as a concessive particle modifying 'sīñca'.

line-178.source: प्रभु आयसु जेहि कहँ जस अहई
line-178.roman: prabhu āyasu jēhi kaham̐ jasa ahaī
line-178.grammarNote: 'āyasu' is the Awadhi tadbhava of Sanskrit ājñā / āyāsa (order/mandate). 'jēhi kaham̐ jasa' introduces the relative condition.

line-179.source: सो तेहि भाँति रहें सुख लहई
line-179.roman: sō tēhi bhām̐ti rahēṁ sukha lahaī
line-179.grammarNote: 'rahēṁ' is an Awadhi locative/conditional participle (upon abiding). 'sō ... sukha lahaī' forms the correlative resolution to 'jēhi ... jasa ahaī'.

line-189.source: जेहि बिधि उतरै कपि कटकु तात सो कहहु उपाइ
line-189.roman: jēhi bidhi utarai kapi kaṭaku tāta sō kahahu upāi
line-189.grammarNote: Correlative structure 'jēhi bidhi ... sō upāi' with 2nd person plural/respectful imperative 'kahahu'; vocative 'tāta'.

line-200.english: {0:Hearing}{4: the distress}{2: of the ocean's}{3: mind,}{1: the compassionate Lord,}
line-200.grammarNote: suni is an absolutive participle (having heard); sāgara mana pīrā forms a genitive-noun phrase functioning as the direct object.

line-204.english: {2,4:He recounted}{0: the entire}{1: account}{3: to the Lord,}
line-204.grammarNote: kahi sunāvā is a compound verbal construction; prabhuhi carries the Awadhi dative/accusative marker -hi.

line-210.source: सकल सुमंगल दायक रघुनायक गुन गान
line-210.roman: sakala sumaṅgala dāyaka raghunāyaka guna gāna
line-210.english: {5:Singing}{4: the virtues}{3: of the leader of the Raghus}{2: is the bestower}{0: of all}{1: auspicious blessings;}

words.gloss: of the leader of the Raghus [Rama]

line-210.grammarNote: sakala sumaṅgala dāyaka is a compound adjective modifying raghunāyaka guna gāna.

line-001.english: {0:Tranquil, }{1:eternal, immeasurable, stainless, }{2:bestowing the peace of liberation,}
line-001.grammarNote: Sanskrit accusative singular masculine adjectives: 'śāntaṁ', 'śāśvatam' + 'aprameyam' + 'anagham' joined by continuous sandhi, and 'nirvāṇa-śānti-pradam' (upapada compound).

line-002.english: {0:unceasingly served by Brahmā, Śambhu, and the serpent-king, }{1:knowable through Vedānta, }{2:the all-pervading Lord,}

words.gloss: incessantly served by Brahmā, Śiva, and the serpent-king Śeṣa
knowable through the culmination of Vedic wisdom (Vedānta)

line-002.grammarNote: Accusative singular masculine forms: 'brahmā-śambhu-phaṇīndra-sevyam' (dvandva inside an upapada compound) combined with adverb 'aniśam' ('unceasingly'), 'vedānta-vedyam' (tatpuruṣa), and 'vibhum' (substantive adjective from vi-√bhū).

line-003.english: {0:known by the name of Rāma, }{1:sovereign of the universe, }{2:spiritual teacher of the gods, }{3:human through māyā, }{4:Hari—}

words.gloss: known by the name of Rāma; Rāma means “pleasing” or “delightful”
appearing as human through worldly creative power (māyā)
Lord Viṣṇu; Hari is “the remover” of evil and suffering

line-003.grammarNote: Accusative singular masculine nouns and tatpuruṣa/karmadhāraya compounds ('rāma-ākhyam', 'jagat-īśvaram', 'sura-gurum', 'māyā-manuṣyam', 'harim'), all acting as direct objects of 'vande'.

line-004.english: {0:I bow to Him, }{1:the mine of compassion, }{2:the foremost of the Raghus, }{3:the crest-jewel among kings}

words.gloss: mine of compassion / ocean of mercy
foremost among the Raghus / best of Raghu's line

line-004.grammarNote: 'vande'haṁ' contains 'vande' (1st sg. present Ātmanepada of √vand) and 'aham' (1st sg. nom. pronoun) with avagraha elision. 'karuṇā-ākaram' (tatpuruṣa), 'raghu-varam', and 'bhūpāla-cūḍāmaṇim' are accusative singular masculine epithets.

line-005.english: {0:There is no other }{1:longing, }{2:O guardian of the Raghu lineage, }{3:in my heart;}

words.gloss: O guardian of the Raghu lineage

line-005.grammarNote: 'na' + 'anyā' merge via dīrgha sandhi into 'nānyā' (nom. sg. fem.). 'spṛhā' is nom. sg. fem. 'raghupate' is vocative sg. masc. of 'raghupati' (guardian/protector of Raghu's line). 'hṛdaye'smadīye' shows pūrvarūpa sandhi of 'hṛdaye' (loc. sg. neuter) and 'asmadīye' (loc. sg. neuter pronominal adjective, 'in my/our heart').

line-006.english: {1:I speak }{0:the truth, }{2:and }{3:You are the inner Self of all beings.}

words.gloss: You [are] the inner Self of all beings

line-006.grammarNote: 'satyaṁ' is used adverbially/cognate accusative with 'vadāmi' (1st sg. present active of √vad). 'bhavān' (nom. sg. masc. honorific 2nd person pronoun) sandhies with 'akhila-antar-ātmā' (karmadhāraya/bahuvrīhi compound, nom. sg. masc. from ātman). Copula is omitted.

line-007.english: {1:grant }{4:unto me, }{2:O eminent leader among the Raghus, }{3:unwavering }{0:devotion,}

words.gloss: O eminent leader among the Raghus

line-007.grammarNote: 'bhaktiṁ' (acc. sg. fem.) is modified by 'nirbharāṁ' (acc. sg. fem.), both direct objects of 'prayaccha' (2nd sg. imperative active of pra-√yam). 'raghupuṅgava' is a vocative compound (Raghu + puṅgava, literally 'bull among the Raghus', an honorific for foremost leader). 'me' is enclitic dative/genitive singular.

line-008.english: {3:and }{1:render }{2:my mind }{0:devoid of faults such as lust}

words.gloss: devoid of blemishes such as lust and desire

line-008.grammarNote: 'kāmādidoṣarahitaṁ' is a compound adjective (kāma + ādi + doṣa + rahita, acc. sg. neuter) functioning as a secondary predicate complement to 'mānasaṁ' (acc. sg. neuter direct object). 'kuru' is 2nd sg. imperative active of √kṛ.

line-009.english: {0:Abode of matchless strength, }{1:whose body has the luster of a golden mountain,}

words.gloss: abode of incomparable strength / storehouse of matchless might
whose body has the luster of a golden mountain

line-009.grammarNote: Accusative singular masculine bahuvrīhi/tatpuruṣa compounds: 'atulita-bala-dhāmam' (atulita 'incomparable' + bala 'might' + dhāma 'abode') and 'hema-śaila-ābha-deham' (hema 'gold' + śaila 'mountain' + ābhā 'radiance/luster' + deha 'body').

line-010.english: {0:fire to the forest of demons, }{1:foremost among the wise,}

words.gloss: fire to the forest of demons

line-010.grammarNote: Sanskrit compound accusatives in the masculine singular (danuja-vana-kṛśānum and jñāninām-agra-gaṇyam) modifying the implicit object of namāmi.

line-011.english: {0:receptacle of all virtues, }{1:sovereign master of the monkeys,}
line-011.grammarNote: Sanskrit compound accusatives: sakala-guṇa-nidhānam and vānarāṇām-adhīśam (tatpuruṣa compound governed by genitive plural vānarāṇām).

line-012.english: {0:beloved devotee of the guardian of Raghu's line, }{1:son of the wind—}{2:I bow to him.}

words.gloss: beloved devotee of the guardian of Raghu's line

line-012.grammarNote: namāmi is first-person singular present active from √nam; raghupati designates Rama as the guardian/protector of Raghu's line; vātajātam is accusative masculine singular.

line-015.source: सिंधु तीर एक भूधर सुंदर। कौतुक कूदि चढ़ेउ ता ऊपर ॥
line-015.roman: siṃdhu tīra eka bhūdhara suṃdara। kautuka kūdi caṛheu tā ūpara ॥
line-015.english: {0:On the ocean }{1:shore }{2:was a }{4:splendid }{3:mountain; }{5:in play, }{6:having leapt, }{7:he mounted }{9:on top of }{8:it.}
line-015.grammarNote: siṃdhu tīra is an unmarked locative phrase; kautuka functions adverbially; caṛheu is 3rd sg. past tense.

line-018.source: जिमि अमोघ रघुपति कर बाना। एही भाँति चलेउ हनुमाना ॥
line-018.roman: jimi amogha raghupati kara bānā। ehī bhā~ti caleu hanumānā ॥
line-018.english: {0:Just like }{1:the unerring }{4:arrow }{2,3:of the guardian of Raghu's line, }{5:in this very }{6:manner }{8:Hanumān }{7:sped forth.}

words.gloss: of the guardian of Raghu's line
monkey-god; son of the Wind; Hanumān means “having prominent jaws”

line-018.grammarNote: Simile structure with comparative particle jimi ('just as') and correlative ehī bhā~ti ('in this very manner'); kara is the Awadhi genitive marker following raghupati (guardian of Raghu's line).

line-019.source: जलनिधि रघुपति दूत बिचारी। तैं मैनाक होहि श्रमहारी ॥
line-019.roman: jalanidhi raghupati dūta bicārī। taiṃ maināka hohi śramahārī ॥
line-019.english: {0:The ocean, }{3:having recognized }{2:the messenger }{1:of the guardian of Raghu's line, said: }{4:“You, }{5:Maināka, }{6:be }{7:the reliever of fatigue.”}

words.gloss: of the guardian of Raghu's line
the mountain who rises from the sea to offer Hanumān rest

line-019.grammarNote: bicārī is a conjunctive participle ('having recognized'); direct speech follows with 2nd sg. pronoun taiṃ, vocative maināka, and 2nd sg. imperative hohi.

line-027.source: कबनेहुँ जतन देइ नहिं जाना। ग्रससि न मोहि कहेउ हनुमाना ॥
line-027.roman: kabanehu~ jatana dei nahiṃ jānā। grasasi na mohi kaheu hanumānā ॥
line-027.english: {0,3:By no }{1:effort }{2:would she allow }{4:him passage. }{6:“Why then do you not }{5:devour }{7:me?” }{8:said }{9:Hanumān.}

words.gloss: monkey-god; son of the Wind; Hanumān means “having prominent jaws”

line-027.grammarNote: 'kabanehu~ jatana' is an instrumental/manner phrase ('by any effort'). 'grasasi na' functions as an ironic or daring imperative ('then why don't you swallow?'). Verb 'kaheu' has postposed nominal agent 'hanumānā'.

line-044.source: उमा न कछु कपि कै अधिकाई। प्रभु प्रताप जो कालहि खाई ॥
line-044.roman: umā na kachu kapi kai adhikāī. prabhu pratāpa jo kālahi khāī.
line-044.english: {0:O Uma,}{1: there is not}{2: any}{5: greatness}{3,4: of the monkey;}{6: it is the Lord's}{7: majesty,}{8: which}{10: devours}{9: Time itself.}

words.gloss: Umā (Pārvatī), Śiva’s consort and listener in this narration

line-044.grammarNote: Vocative 'umā'. 'Kapi kai adhikāī' contains the feminine genitive postposition 'kai'. 'Kālahi' has the Awadhi objective suffix '-hi'.

line-046.source: अति उतंग जलनिधि चहु पासा। कनक कोट कर परम प्रकासा ॥
line-046.roman: ati utaṅga jalanidhi cahu pāsā. kanaka koṭa kara parama prakāsā.
line-046.english: {0:Exceedingly}{1: lofty,}{2: with the ocean}{3: on all four}{4: sides,}{8: and the supreme}{9: radiance}{5,7: of the golden}{6: rampart.}
line-046.grammarNote: 'Cahu pāsā' functions adverbially. 'Kanaka koṭa kara' uses the masculine genitive postposition 'kara'.

line-058.source: रघुबीर सर तीरथ सरीरन्हि त्यागि गति पैहहिं सही
line-058.roman: raghubīra sara tīratha sarīranhi tyāgi gati paihahi~ sahī.
line-058.english: {4:relinquishing}{3: their bodies}{2: at the sacred ford}{0: of the Hero of Raghu's line's}{1: arrows,}{7: they will truly}{6: attain}{5: liberation.}

words.gloss: they will attain; they will receive

line-058.grammarNote: 'raghubīra sara tīratha' is a metaphorical compound (rūpaka alaṅkāra: the arrow as tīrtha). 'tyāgi' is an absolutive participle with direct object 'sarīranhi' (plural). 'paihahi~' is 3rd person plural future.

line-062.source: नाम लंकिनी एक निसिचरी। सो कह चलेसि मोहि निंदरी ॥
line-062.roman: nāma laṅkinī eka nisicarī. so kaha calesi mohi niṁdarī ||
line-062.grammarNote: Nāma laṅkinī eka nisicarī is a descriptive nominal phrase identifying the subject. So is the correlative pronoun governing kaha. Calesi is a 2nd person singular verb form in Awadhi. Niṁdarī is an absolutive form of √nind.

line-067.source: बिकल होसि तैं कपि कें मारे। तब जानेसु निसिचर संघारे ॥
line-067.roman: bikala hosi taiṁ kapi keṁ māre. taba jānesu nisicara saṁghāre ||
line-067.english: {2:‘When you }{1:become }{0:distressed }{4,5:by the striking }{3:of a monkey, }{6:then }{7:know }{8:that the demons }{9:are destroyed.’"}
line-067.grammarNote: Kapi keṁ māre is an instrumental-causal participial phrase ('by the striking of a monkey'). Jānesu is an Awadhi 2nd person future imperative ('you shall know / know then'). Nisicara saṁghāre functions as an objective clause with a passive participle ('that demons are slain').

line-076.source: गयउ दसानन मंदिर माहीं। अति बिचित्र कहि जात सो नाहीं ॥
line-076.roman: gayau dasānana maṁdira māhīṁ. ati bicitra kahi jāta so nāhīṁ ||
line-076.english: {0:He went }{3:inside }{2:the palace }{1:of the Ten-Headed one; }{4:it was exceedingly }{5:wondrous, }{8:that }{7,9:cannot }{6:be described.}
line-076.grammarNote: 'gayau' is a masculine singular simple past verb. 'dasānana' functions as an uninflected genitive modifier to 'maṁdira'. 'kahi jāta ... nāhīṁ' is a passive potential construction.

line-081.source: लंका निसिचर निकर निवासा। इहाँ कहाँ सज्जन कर बासा ॥
line-081.roman: laṁkā nisicara nikara nivāsā. ihām̐ kahām̐ sajjana kara bāsā ॥
line-081.english: {0:Lanka is }{3:the abode }{2:of a host }{1:of night-wanderers; }{5:how is there }{4:here }{8:the dwelling }{6,7:of a virtuous person?}
line-081.grammarNote: ‘nisicara nikara nivāsā’ is a genitive compound phrase in apposition to ‘laṁkā’. ‘kara’ marks the genitive relation between ‘sajjana’ and ‘bāsā’.

line-090.source: सुनत जुगल तन पुलक मन मगन सुमिरि गुन ग्राम
line-090.roman: sunata jugala tana pulaka mana magana sumiri guna grāma
line-090.english: {0:Upon hearing, }{2:the bodies }{1:of both }{3:thrilled with bristling hair }{4:and their minds }{5:became immersed, }{6:remembering }{8:the multitude }{7:of virtues.}
line-090.grammarNote: sunata is an imperfective participle functioning adverbially ('upon hearing'). jugala functions as the collective subject governing both the nominal predicate of physical thrill (tana pulaka) and mental absorption (mana magana). sumiri is an absolutive participle modifying magana.

line-098.source: प्रात लेइ जो नाम हमारा। तेहि दिन ताहि न मिलै अहारा ॥
line-098.roman: prāta lei jo nāma hamārā. tehi dina tāhi na milai ahārā ॥
line-098.grammarNote: Relative-correlative conditional construction: jo ... tāhi. lei is 3rd singular present/subjunctive. milai is 3rd singular present/subjunctive with dative experiencer tāhi. tehi dina is an oblique temporal modifier.

line-101.source: जानतहूँ अस स्वामि बिसारी। फिरहिं ते काहे न होहिं दुखारी ॥
line-101.roman: jānatahūm̐ asa svāmi bisārī. phirahiṁ te kāhe na hohiṁ dukhārī.
line-101.grammarNote: Participle with emphatic suffix 'jānata-hūm̐'; absolutive 'bisārī'; 3rd person plural present/subjunctive verbs 'phirahiṁ' and 'hohiṁ'.

line-123.source: नाहिं त सपदि मानु मम बानी। सुमुखि होति न त जीवन हानी ॥
line-123.roman: nāhiṁ ta sapadi mānu mama bānī | sumukhi hoti na ta jīvana hānī ||
line-123.english: {0,1:Otherwise, }{3:heed }{4:my }{5:words }{2:at once, }{6:O fair-faced one, }{8,9:or else }{7:there will be }{11:the loss }{10:of life.”}

words.gloss: O fair-faced one; O woman of beautiful countenance (vocative)

line-123.grammarNote: nāhiṁ ta and na ta function as conditional disjunctive particles ('otherwise'). mānu is 2nd person singular imperative. sumukhi is a vocative bahuvrīhi compound (su-mukha).

line-144.source: तजौं देह करु बेगि उपाई। दुसहु बिरहु अब नहिं सहि जाई ॥
line-144.roman: tajaũ deha karu begi upāī. dusahu birahu aba nahĩ sahi jāī ..
line-144.english: {3:Quickly }{2:devise }{4:a means }{0:that I may give up }{1:my body; }{5:unbearable }{6:separation }{7,8,10:can no longer }{9:be endured.}

words.gloss: may I give up / let me abandon

line-144.grammarNote: `tajaũ` is 1st singular optative/subjunctive; `karu` is 2nd singular imperative; `nahĩ sahi jāī` is a passive modal construction expressing impossibility.

line-149.source: कह सीता बिधि भा प्रतिकूला। मिलहि न पावक मिटिहि न सूला ॥
line-149.roman: kaha sītā bidhi bhā pratikūlā. milahi na pāvaka miṭihi na sūlā ..

words.gloss: Rāma’s wife and heroine of the Rāmāyaṇa; Sītā means “furrow”

line-149.grammarNote: `bidhi` (Skt. vidhi) is the masculine subject of `bhā`; `milahi` and `miṭihi` are 3rd person singular future/potential forms in Avadhi paired with `na` in correlative negation.

line-165.source: राम दूत मैं मातु जानकी। सत्य सपथ करुनानिधान की ॥
line-165.roman: rāma dūta maĩ mātu jānakī. satya sapatha karunānidhāna kī ..
line-165.english: {2:“I am }{0:Rama’s }{1:messenger, }{3:O Mother }{4:Janaki; }{5,6:true is the oath }{7,8:by the Treasury of Compassion.”}

words.gloss: of Rāma, the delightful Lord of Ayodhyā, Sītā’s husband

line-165.grammarNote: First clause is nominal with elided copula ('maĩ rāma dūta [āhaũ]'). 'mātu jānakī' is a vocative compound/phrase. 'karunānidhāna kī' is a genitive postpositional phrase modifying the feminine noun 'sapatha'.

line-173.source: कोमलचित कृपाल रघुराई। कपि केहि हेतु धरी निठुराई ॥
line-173.roman: kōmalacita kṛpāla raghurāī. kapi kēhi hētu dharī niṭhurāī.
line-173.english: {0:“Tender-hearted }{1:and compassionate }{2:is the Lord of the Raghus; }{3:O monkey, }{4:for what }{5:reason }{6:has he assumed }{7:harshness?”}
line-173.grammarNote: kōmalacita and kṛpāla stand in apposition to raghurāī; raghurāī is a title denoting ruler/chief of Raghu's line (raghu + rāya); dharī is a feminine perfective verb agreeing with niṭhurāī.

line-174.source: सहज बानि सेवक सुख दायक। कबहुँक सुरति करत रघुनायक ॥
line-174.roman: sahaja bāni sēvaka sukha dāyaka. kabahum̐ka surati karata raghunāyaka.
line-174.english: {0:“By innate }{1:nature }{4:a giver }{3:of joy }{2:to servants—}{8:does the Leader of the Raghus }{5:ever }{6,7:bring me to mind?”}
line-174.grammarNote: sahaja bāni functions as an adverbial or adjectival descriptor of Rama's character; surati karata is a conjunct verb (surati, from Skt. smṛti, 'memory/remembrance' + karana).

line-178.source: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता। तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा निकेता ॥
line-178.roman: mātu kusala prabhu anuja samētā. tava dukha dukhī sukṛpā nikētā.
line-178.english: {0:“O Mother, }{2:the Lord }{1:is well }{4:together with }{3:his younger brother; }{7:grieved }{5:by your }{6:grief }{9:is the abode }{8:of gracious compassion.”}
line-178.grammarNote: mātu is an affectionate vocative singular; sukṛpā nikētā is a bahuvrīhi/tatpuruṣa compound ('abode of gracious kindness') in apposition to prabhu; dukha dukhī uses cognate noun and adjective to express empathetic distress.

line-179.source: जनि जननी मानहु जियँ ऊना। तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना ॥
line-179.roman: jani jananī mānahu jiyaṁ ūnā. tumha tē prēmu rāma kēṁ dūnā.
line-179.english: {0:“Do not, }{1:O Mother, }{2:deem it }{4:diminished }{3:in your heart: }{8,9:Rama’s }{7:love }{10:is double }{5,6:yours.”}

words.gloss: in the heart; in the mind
hero of the Rāmāyaṇa and Viṣṇu’s avatāra; Rāma means “pleasing” or “delightful”

line-179.grammarNote: jani is the standard Awadhi prohibitive particle preceding the imperative mānahu; jiyaṁ is a locative singular ('in the heart'); tē is an ablative/comparative postposition ('than you').

line-187.source: तत्त्व प्रेम कर मम अरु तोरा। जानत प्रिया एकु मनु मोरा ॥
line-187.roman: tattva prēma kara mama aru tōrā. jānata priyā ēku manu mōrā.
line-187.grammarNote: tattva prēma kar mama aru tōrā is the topicalized direct object phrase. jānata is a 3rd person singular present habitual verb agreeing with the masculine singular subject ēku manu mōrā. manu matches registry entry manas.

line-189.source: प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥
line-189.roman: prabhu sandēsu sunata baidēhī. magana prēma tana sudhi nahiṁ tēhī.
line-189.english: {2:Upon hearing }{0:the Lord's }{1:message, }{3:Vaidehi }{4:was immersed }{5:in love; }{8:no }{7:consciousness }{6:of her body }{9:remained to her.}
line-189.grammarNote: sunata is an imperfective/present participle denoting contemporaneous action ('as she heard'). magana is a past participle used adjectivally. tana sudhi nahiṁ tēhī is an experiencer dative construction ('to her there was no awareness of the body').

line-208.source: करहुँ कृपा प्रभु अस सुनि काना। निर्भर प्रेम मगन हनुमाना ॥
line-208.roman: karahuṁ kṛpā prabhu asa suni kānā. nirbhara prema magana hanumānā.
line-208.english: {4:Hearing }{5:with his ears }{3:these words, }{2:“May the Lord }{0:bestow }{1:grace,” }{9:Hanumān }{8:was immersed }{6:in boundless }{7:love.}

words.gloss: monkey-god; son of the Wind; Hanumān means “having prominent jaws”

line-208.grammarNote: kānā is an instrumental/locative singular ('with the ear'). magana is a past participle used predicatively ('immersed / absorbed').

line-210.source: अब कृतकृत्य भयउँ मैं माता। आसिष तव अमोघ बिख्याता ॥
line-210.roman: aba kṛtakṛtya bhayauṁ maiṁ mātā. āsiṣa tava amogha bikhyātā.
line-210.english: {0:“Now }{3:I }{1,2:have become fulfilled in purpose, }{4:O Mother; }{6:your }{5:blessing }{8:is renowned }{7:as unfailing.}
line-210.grammarNote: Awadhi 1sg perfective 'bhayauṁ' agrees with 'maiṁ'. 'mātā' is in the vocative case. The second hemistich operates as a nominal copular clause: 'āsiṣa tava amogha [hai] bikhyātā'.

line-213.source: तिन्ह कर भय माता मोहि नाहीं। जौं तुम्ह सुख मानहु मन माहीं ॥
line-213.roman: tinha kara bhaya mātā mohi nāhīṁ. jauṁ tumha sukha mānahu mana māhīṁ.
line-213.grammarNote: 'tinha kara' is genitive plural governing 'bhaya'. 'mānahu' is 2pl present/subjunctive in a conditional protasis introduced by 'jauṁ'.

line-227.source: मारसि जनि सुत बांधेसु ताही। देखिअ कपिहि कहाँ कर आही ॥
line-227.roman: mārasi jani suta bā~dhesu tāhī. dekhia kapihi kahā~ kara āhī.
line-227.english: {2:“O son, }{1:do not }{0:kill }{4:him, }{3:bind him; }{5:let us see }{6:the monkey, }{7:whence }{8,9:he is.”}
line-227.grammarNote: jani is the prohibitive negation particle used with the subjunctive/imperative mārasi. bā~dhesu is a 2nd person singular imperative with suffix -su. dekhia is an impersonal/hortative form.

line-230.source: अति बिसाल तरु एक उपारा। बिरथ कीन्ह लंकेस कुमारा ॥
line-230.roman: ati bisāla taru eka upārā. biratha kīnha laṅkesa kumārā.
line-230.english: {4:He uprooted }{3:a single }{0:exceedingly }{1:colossal }{2:tree }{6:and rendered }{8:the son }{7:of the ruler of Laṅkā }{5:chariotless.}
line-230.grammarNote: Tadbhavas: upārā < Skt. utpāṭayati; biratha < Skt. viratha (bahuvrīhi compound: vi- + ratha). laṅkesa is a tatpuruṣa compound (laṅkā + īśa).

line-263.source: मोहि न कछु बाँधे कइ लाजा। कीन्ह चहउँ निज प्रभु कर काजा ॥
line-263.roman: mōhi na kachu bām̐dhē kaï lājā. kīnha cahaum̐ nija prabhu kara kājā .
line-263.english: {0:To me }{1:there is no }{5:shame }{2:at all }{3,4:of being bound; }{7:I wish }{6:to do }{8:my own }{9,10:Lord's }{11:work.}
line-263.grammarNote: Dative-experiencer construction mōhi ... lājā ('to me there is shame'). kīnha cahaum̐ is a desiderative verb construction (infinitive/participle + cahaum̐).

line-265.source: देखहु तुम्ह निज कुलहि बिचारी। भ्रम तजि भजहु भगत भय हारी ॥
line-265.roman: dēkhahu tumha nija kulahi bicārī. bhrama taji bhajahu bhagata bhaya hārī .
line-265.english: {0:Look, }{1:you, }{4:having reflected }{2:upon your own }{3:clan; }{6:having abandoned }{5:delusion, }{7:worship }{10:the dispeller }{8:of devotees' }{9:fear.}
line-265.grammarNote: kulahi has the accusative case ending -hi. bhagata bhaya hārī is a compound functioning as the accusative object of bhajahu.

line-267.source: तासों बयरु कबहुँ नहिं कीजै। मोरे कहें जानकी दीजै ॥
line-267.roman: tāsōṁ bayaru kabahum̐ nahiṁ kījai. mōrē kahēṁ jānakī dījai .
line-267.english: {0:With Him }{1:enmity }{2,3:must never }{4:be made; }{5:at my }{6:word, }{7:let Janaki }{8:be given back.}
line-267.grammarNote: kījai and dījai are Awadhi polite passive/optative imperatives. mōrē kahēṁ is a locative/instrumental participial clause.

line-269.source: गएँ सरन प्रभु राखिहैं तव अपराध बिसारि
line-269.roman: gaēm̐ sarana prabhu rākhihaiṁ tava aparādha bisāri .
line-269.grammarNote: gaēm̐ sarana is a conditional/locative absolute construction ('upon going into shelter'). rākhihaiṁ is an Awadhi 3rd person honorific future form.

line-275.source: सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गए पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥
line-275.roman: sajala mūla jinha saritanha nāhīṁ. baraṣi gaē puni tabahiṁ sukhāhīṁ .
line-275.english: {3:Rivers }{2:which }{4:have no }{0:water-filled }{1:source, }{5:once the rains have }{6:passed, }{7:subsequently }{9:dry up }{8:right then.}
line-275.grammarNote: 'jinha saritanha' is an oblique relative plural. 'baraṣi gaē' is an absolute participial construction indicating completed temporal condition. 'sukhāhīṁ' is third-person plural present.

line-284.source: सुनि कपि बचन बहुत खिसिआना। बेगि न हरहुँ मूढ़ कर प्राना ॥
line-284.roman: suni kapi bacana bahuta khisiānā. bēgi na harahuṁ mūṛha kara prānā ||
line-284.english: {0:Hearing }{1:the monkey’s }{2:words, }{3:he became greatly }{4:enraged: }{6:“Why do you not }{5:swiftly }{7:take away }{8,9:the fool’s }{10:life-breaths?”}
line-284.grammarNote: suni is an absolutive participle. harahuṁ is a 2nd person plural imperative (Awadhi variant of harahu). kara functions as a genitive postposition connecting mūṛha and prānā.

line-289.source: कपि कें ममता पूँछ पर सबहि कहउँ समुझाइ।
line-289.roman: kapi kēṁ mamatā pūm̐cha para sabahi kahauṁ samujhāi.
line-289.english: {0,1:“A monkey }{2:has attachment }{3,4:to its tail; }{7:I explain }{6:and say }{5:to all:}
line-289.grammarNote: dō. marks the dohā metric section. kapi kēṁ uses the genitive postposition kēṁ. kahauṁ is 1st person singular present indicative. samujhāi is an absolutive participle compounding with the main verb.

line-292.source: जिन्ह कै कीन्हसि बहुत बड़ाई। देखेउँमैं तिन्ह कै प्रभुताई ॥
line-292.roman: jinha kai kīnhasi bahuta baṛāī. dēkhēuṁ maiṁ tinha kai prabhutāī ||

words.gloss: let me see; I shall see

line-292.grammarNote: 'kīnhasi' is a transitive past verb with 2nd person singular agentive enclitic '-si' ('you did'). 'dēkhēuṁ' functions modal-optatively as 1st person singular ('let me see'). 'jinha kai' correlatively balances 'tinha kai'.

line-296.source: कौतुक कहँ आए पुरबासी। मारहिं चरन करहिं बहु हाँसी ॥
line-296.roman: kautuka kaham̐ āē purabāsī. mārahiṁ carana karahiṁ bahu hām̐sī ||
line-296.english: {3:The citizens }{2:came }{1:for }{0:the spectacle; }{4:they struck him }{5:with their feet }{6:and made }{7:much }{8:mockery.}
line-296.grammarNote: 'kautuka kaham̐' functions as a purposive dative ('for the sake of the spectacle'). 'purabāsī' is the common plural subject of 'āē', 'mārahiṁ', and 'karahiṁ'. 'carana' is used instrumentally/adverbially as '[with] feet'.

line-318.source: कहु कपि केहि बिधि राखौं प्राना। तुम्हहू तात कहत अब जाना ॥
line-318.roman: kahu kapi kēhi bidhi rākhauṁ prānā. tumhahū tāta kahata aba jānā.
line-318.english: {0:“Tell me, }{1:O monkey, }{2,3:how can I }{4:keep }{5:my life-breaths? }{7:Dear child, }{6:you too }{8,9:now speak }{10:of departing.”}
line-318.grammarNote: `rākhauṁ` is first person singular present subjunctive. `tumhahū` is an emphatic pronoun (`tumha` + `-hū`). `jānā` functions as a verbal noun.

line-319.source: तोहि देखि सीतलि भइ छाती। पुनि मो कहुँ सोइ दिनु सो राती ॥
line-319.roman: tōhi dēkhi sītali bhai chātī. puni mō kahuṁ sōi dinu sō rātī.
line-319.english: {1:Having seen }{0:you, }{4:my chest }{3:became }{2:cool; }{5:now again }{7:for }{6:me }{8:there will be that same }{9:day }{10:and that same }{11:night.”}
line-319.grammarNote: `dēkhi` is an absolutive participle. `sītali bhai chātī` exhibits feminine agreement (`chātī` is feminine in Awadhi). `mō kahuṁ` is a postpositional experiencer dative.

line-343.source: ताहि सदा सुभ कुसल निरंतर। सुर नर मुनि प्रसन्न ता ऊपर ॥
line-343.roman: tāhi sadā subha kusala niraṃtara. sura nara muni prasanna tā ūpara ॥
line-343.english: {0:for that person there is }{1:always }{2:auspicious }{3:well-being }{4:unceasingly; }{5:gods, }{6:mortals, }{7:and sages }{8:are pleased }{10:with }{9:him.}
line-343.grammarNote: 'tāhi' is dative correlative pronoun ('to that one'). Dvandva compound 'sura nara muni' functions as plural grammatical subject for the predicate adjective 'prasanna'.

line-349.source: कहहु तात केहि भाँति जानकी। रहति करति रच्छा स्वप्रान की ॥
line-349.roman: kahahu tāta kehi bhāomti jānakī. rahati karati racchā svaprāna kī ॥
line-349.english: {0:“Tell me, }{1:O dear one, }{2:in what }{3:manner }{4:does Janaki }{5:live }{6:and maintain }{7:the protection }{9:of }{8:her own life-breaths?”}
line-349.grammarNote: 'kahahu' is 2nd person honorific imperative. 'kehi bhāomti' is an interrogative adverbial phrase. 'rahati' and 'karati' are feminine imperfective habitual verbs agreeing with 'jānakī'.

line-356.source: अवगुन एक मोर मैं माना। बिछुरत प्रान न कीन्ह पयाना ॥
line-356.roman: avaguna eka mora maiṃ mānā. bichurata prāna na kīnha payānā ॥
line-356.grammarNote: 'maiṃ mānā' is an ergative-type past transitive construction ('I acknowledged'). 'bichurata' is an imperfective participle functioning adverbially of time.

line-363.source: सुनि सीता दुख प्रभु सुख अयना। भरि आए जल राजिव नयना ॥
line-363.roman: suni sītā dukha prabhu sukha ayanā. bhari āe jala rājiva nayanā ॥
line-363.english: {0:Hearing}{1: Sītā’s}{2: sorrow,}{3: the Lord,}{5: the abode}{4: of bliss,}{9: had His lotus}{10: eyes}{6,7: fill}{8: with tears.}

words.gloss: Rāma’s wife and heroine of the Rāmāyaṇa; Sītā means “furrow”

line-363.grammarNote: suni is a conjunctive participle indicating prior action. sukha ayanā is a tatpuruṣa compound in apposition to prabhu. bhari āe is a compound verb (bharnā + ānā 3pl masculine) agreeing with plural rājiva nayanā.

line-365.source: कह हनुमंत बिपति प्रभु सोई। जब तव सुमिरन भजन न होई ॥
line-365.roman: kaha hanumaṁta bipati prabhu soī. jaba tava sumirana bhajana na hoī ॥
line-365.english: {1:Hanumān}{0: said:}{3: “O revered one,}{4: that alone}{2: is adversity,}{5: when}{7: remembrance}{8: and worship}{6: of You}{9,10: do not occur.”}

words.gloss: Hanumān; Rāma’s monkey devotee; Hanumān means “having prominent jaws”

line-365.grammarNote: kaha hanumaṁta places verb before subject. bipati prabhu soī is an equational nominal clause ('O lord, distress is that alone'). jaba ... na hoī forms the temporal subordinate clause.

line-368.source: प्रति उपकार करौं का तोरा। सनमुख होइ न सकत मन मोरा ॥
line-368.roman: prati upakāra karauṁ kā torā. sanamukha hoi na sakata mana morā ॥
line-368.english: {3:What}{0: return}{1: favor}{2: can I do}{4: for you?}{10: My}{9: mind}{7,8: cannot}{6: even stand}{5: face-to-face.}

words.gloss: can I do; shall I do

line-368.grammarNote: prati upakāra is segmented across two tokens. karauṁ kā is a 1sg deliberative subjunctive. sanamukha hoi na sakata uses the modal auxiliary sakanā with root/infinitive hoi, agreeing with masculine subject mana morā.

line-370.source: पुनि पुनि कपिहि चितव सुरत्राता। लोचन नीर पुलक अति गाता ॥
line-370.roman: puni puni kapihi citava suratrātā. locana nīra pulaka ati gātā ॥
line-370.english: {0,1:Again and again}{4: the protector of the gods}{3: gazes}{2: upon the monkey;}{6: tears}{5: are in His eyes}{8: and immense}{7: thrilling}{9: is upon His limbs.}
line-370.grammarNote: Awadhi imperfective/present verb citava with compound agent suratrātā (sura + trātā). Accusative/dative enclitic -hi in kapihi. The second hemistich uses parataxis with unexpressed locative markers: locana [maham̐] nīra, gātā [par] ati pulaka.

line-373.source: बार बार प्रभु चहइ उठावा। प्रेम मगन तेहि उठब न भावा ॥
line-373.roman: bāra bāra prabhu cahai uṭhāvā. prema magana tehi uṭhaba na bhāvā ॥
line-373.english: {0,1:Time and again}{2: the Lord}{3: sought}{4: to raise him up,}{6: but immersed}{5: in love,}{8: rising}{9: did not}{7,10: please him.}
line-373.grammarNote: Reduplicated bāra bāra expresses iterative aspect. The verbal phrase cahai uṭhāvā combines finite verb with causative verbal noun. The second hemistich tehi uṭhaba na bhāvā is an experiencer-dative construction with the verbal noun uṭhaba as grammatical subject.

line-386.source: उमा राम सुभाउ जेहिं जाना। ताहि भजनु तजि भाव न आना ॥
line-386.roman: umā rāma subhāu jehiṃ jānā. tāhi bhajanu taji bhāva na ānā.
line-386.english: {0:O Umā, }{3,5:to whoever }{4:has known }{1:Rāma’s }{2:nature, }{7:leaving aside }{6:His worship, }{9,10:nothing else }{8:appeals.}

words.gloss: O Umā, Pārvatī, Śiva’s consort and listener in this narration
of Rāma, the delightful Lord of Ayodhyā, Sītā’s husband

line-386.grammarNote: Relative-correlative structure: 'jehiṃ... tāhi'. 'taji' is an absolutive participle. 'bhāva' functions as 3rd person singular present of 'bhānā' (to please/appeal) with subject 'ānā' (other/anything else). 'umā' is vocative.

line-387.source: यह संवाद जासु उर आवा। रघुपति चरन भगति सोइ पावा ॥
line-387.roman: yaha saṃvāda jāsu ura āvā. raghupati carana bhagati soi pāvā.
line-387.english: {2:Into whose }{3:heart }{0:this }{1:dialogue }{4:enters, }{8:that very person }{9:attains }{7:devotion }{6:to the feet }{5:of the guardian of Raghu’s line.}
line-387.grammarNote: Relative-correlative: 'jāsu... soi'. 'raghupati carana bhagati' is a head-final genitive chain. 'āvā' and 'pāvā' form the rhyming past-tense couplet endings.

line-390.source: अब बिलंबु केहि कारन कीजे। तुरत कपिन्ह कहुँ आयसु दीजे ॥
line-390.roman: aba bilaṃbu kehi kārana kīje. turata kapinha kahu~ āyasu dīje.
line-390.english: {0:Now }{2:for what }{3:reason }{1:should delay }{4:be made? }{9:Give }{8:the order }{6,7:to the monkeys }{5:at once.}
line-390.grammarNote: 'kīje' and 'dīje' are polite/passive optative-imperative forms in rhyming couplet position. 'kapinha' is oblique plural of 'kapi' with postposition 'kahu~'.

line-423.source: सुनहु नाथ सीता बिनु दीन्हें। हित न तुम्हार संभु अज कीन्हें ॥
line-423.roman: sunahu nātha sītā binu dīnhēm̐. hita na tumhāra sambhu aja kīnhēm̐.
line-423.english: {0:Listen,}{1: O lord,}{3: without}{4: giving back}{2: Sītā,}{7: your}{5: welfare}{6: is not}{10: achieved, even if done by}{8: Śambhu}{9: and the Unborn.}

words.gloss: Rāma’s wife and heroine of the Rāmāyaṇa; Sītā means “furrow”
Śiva; Śambhu means “bringing happiness or well-being”

line-423.grammarNote: 'dīnhēm̐' and 'kīnhēm̐' are oblique past participles used adverbially with conditional/concessive sense.

line-425.source: जब लगि ग्रसत न तब लगि जतनु करहु तजि टेक
line-425.roman: jaba lagi grasata na taba lagi jatanu karahu taji ṭēka
line-425.english: {0:As}{1: long as}{3: they have not}{2: devoured them,}{5: until }{4:then}{7: make}{6: an effort,}{8: abandoning}{9: stubborn obstinacy.}
line-425.grammarNote: 'jaba lagi... na' forms an Awadhi idiom meaning 'until/before'. 'taji' is an absolutive participle.

line-429.source: कंपहिं लोकप जाकी त्रासा। तासु नारि सभीत बड़ि हासा ॥
line-429.roman: kampahim̐ lōkapa jākī trāsā. tāsu nāri sabhīta baṛi hāsā.
line-429.english: {1:The world-guardians}{0: tremble}{2: at whose}{3: dread—}{4:that his}{5: wife}{6: is terrified}{7: is a matter of great}{8: laughter.}
line-429.grammarNote: 'lōkapa' reflects Sanskrit 'lokapāla'. 'jākī trāsā' contains a feminine genitive relative pronoun agreeing with 'trāsā'.

line-434.source: जितेहु सुरासुर तब श्रम नाहीं। नर बानर केहि लेखे माही ॥
line-434.roman: jitēhu surāsura taba śrama nāhīm̐. nara bānara kēhi lēkhē māhī.
line-434.english: {0:“You conquered}{1: gods and demons,}{2: and at that time}{4: there was no}{3: strain;}{9: in }{7:what}{8: reckoning}{5: are mortal men}{6: and monkeys?”}
line-434.grammarNote: 'jitēhu' is 2nd person honorific past. 'surāsura' is a dvandva compound (sura + asura). 'kēhi lēkhē māhī' is a rhetorical locative idiom expressing complete insignificance.

line-436.source: राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास
line-436.roman: rāja dharma tana tīni kara hoi begihīṁ nāsa
line-436.english: {3,4:for these three—}{0:realm,}{1: righteous conduct,}{2: and the body—}{7:destruction}{6: swiftly}{5: occurs.}
line-436.grammarNote: 'rāja dharma tana' corresponds respectively to minister, guru, and physician from line-435. 'tīni kara' is the genitive modifying 'nāsa'. 'begihīṁ' contains the emphatic suffix '-hīṁ'.

line-440.source: जौ कृपाल पूँछिहु मोहि बाता। मति अनुरुप कहउँ हित ताता ॥
line-440.roman: jau kṛpāla pūm̐chihu mohi bātā. mati anurupa kahauṁ hita tātā ॥
line-440.english: {0:“Since}{2: you have asked}{3: of me}{4: the matter,}{1: O gracious one,}{7: I speak}{8: what is beneficial}{6: according to my}{5: understanding,}{9: O brother.”}
line-440.grammarNote: 'pūm̐chihu' is 2nd person honorific past. 'kahauṁ' is 1st person singular present indicative/subjunctive. 'kṛpāla' and 'tātā' function as vocative titles.

line-441.source: जो आपन चाहै कल्याना। सुजसु सुमति सुभ गति सुख नाना ॥
line-441.roman: jo āpana cāhai kalyānā. sujasu sumati subha gati sukha nānā ॥
line-441.grammarNote: Relative pronoun 'jo' governs the 3sg present/optative verb 'cāhai'. The accusative objects are listed in asyndeton ('kalyānā', 'sujasu', 'sumati', 'subha gati', 'sukha nānā').

line-470.source: जिअसि सदा सठ मोर जिआवा। रिपु कर पच्छ मूढ़ तोहि भावा ॥
line-470.roman: jiasi sadā saṭha mōra jiāvā. ripu kara paccha mūḍha tōhi bhāvā.
line-470.english: {1:You always }{0:live, }{2:O rogue, }{4:kept alive }{3:by me, }{5,6:yet the enemy’s }{7:side }{10:pleases }{9:you, }{8:O fool!}
line-470.grammarNote: 'jiasi' is 2nd person singular present indicative. 'jiāvā' is a causative past participle used adverbially/substantively with genitive agent 'mōra' ('by my sustaining'). 'bhāvā' takes a dative/experiencer pronoun 'tōhi' with nominative subject 'ripu kara paccha'.

line-482.source: चलेउ हरषि रघुनायक पाहीं। करत मनोरथ बहु मन माहीं ॥
line-482.roman: caleu haraṣi raghunāyaka pāhīṁ. karata manōratha bahu mana māhīṁ ॥
line-482.english: {1:Rejoicing,}{0: he set out}{3: toward}{2: the Lord of the Raghus,}{4: making}{6: many}{5: heartfelt longings}{8: within}{7: his heart.}
line-482.grammarNote: Absolutive 'haraṣi' ('having rejoiced') qualifies the 3rd person past verb 'caleu'. 'karata' is an imperfective participle functioning adverbially.

line-488.source: ते पद आजु बिलोकिहउँ इन्ह नयनन्हि अब जाइ
line-488.roman: tē pada āju bilōkihauṁ inha nayananhi aba jāi
line-488.english: {0:those}{1: feet}{3: I shall behold}{2: today}{4: with these}{5: eyes,}{7: going}{6: now.}
line-488.grammarNote: 'tē pada' is demonstrative object phrase of 'bilōkihauṁ'. 'nayananhi' is an instrumental plural noun governed by the proximal demonstrative 'inha'. '42' represents the verse number.

line-489.source: एहि बिधि करत सप्रेम बिचारा। आयउ सपदि सिंधु एहिं पारा ॥
line-489.roman: ēhi bidhi karata saprēma bicārā. āyau sapadi sindhu ēhiṁ pārā ॥
line-489.english: {0:In this}{1: manner,}{2: making}{3: loving}{4: reflections,}{6: he swiftly}{5: arrived}{8: on this}{9: shore}{7: of the ocean.}
line-489.grammarNote: 'karata' is a present participle modifying the subject of 'āyau'. 'sapadi' is an adverb of speed. 'sindhu ēhiṁ pārā' functions as a locative goal.

line-515.source: नयन नीर पुलकित अति गाता। मन धरि धीर कही मृदु बाता ॥
line-515.roman: nayana nīra pulakita ati gātā. mana dhari dhīra kahī mṛdu bātā ..
line-515.english: {1:With tears }{0:in his eyes }{4:and his body }{3:exceedingly }{2:thrilled, }{6:holding }{7:composure }{5:in his mind, }{8:he spoke }{9:soft }{10:words:}

words.gloss: thrilled with hair standing on end

line-515.grammarNote: nayana and mana function in locative sense without explicit postpositions. dhari is an absolutive participle in -i. kahī agrees with the feminine object bātā in perfective aspect.

line-520.source: अस कहि करत दंडवत देखा। तुरत उठे प्रभु हरष बिसेषा ॥
line-520.roman: asa kahi karata daṁḍavata dēkhā. turata uṭhē prabhu haraṣa bisēṣā.
line-520.english: {1:Having spoken }{0:thus, }{2:Vibhīṣaṇa was performing }{3:full prostration like a staff; }{4:seeing him, }{7:the sovereign guardian }{5:instantly }{6:rose }{9:with immense }{8:joy.}
line-520.grammarNote: kahi is an absolutive participle in -i. karata is a present participle functioning adverbially/attributively with daṁḍavata. uṭhē is an honorific/plural past tense verb agreeing with prabhu.

line-523.source: कहु लंकेस सहित परिवारा। कुसल कुठाहर बास तुम्हारा ॥
line-523.roman: kahu laṁkēsa sahita parivārā. kusala kuṭhāhara bāsa tumhārā.
line-523.english: {0:“Tell me, }{1:O Lord of Laṅkā, }{4:is there well-being }{7:for you }{2:together with }{3:your family, }{6:when your dwelling }{5:is in an unfit place?}

words.gloss: in an unfit place; in a foul abode

line-523.grammarNote: kahu is 2sg imperative. laṁkēsa is a vocative compound (Laṅkā + īśa). kuṭhāhara is ku- (bad/unworthy) + ṭhāhara (place/dwelling).

line-538.source: अहोभाग्य मम अमित अति राम कृपा सुख पुंज।
line-538.roman: -ahōbhāgya mama amita ati rāma kṛpā sukha puñja.
line-538.english: {3:Exceedingly }{2:boundless }{1:is my }{0:supreme fortune, }{4:O Rāma, }{5,7:embodiment of grace }{6:and bliss,}

words.gloss: O Rāma, the delightful Lord of Ayodhyā, Sītā’s husband
mass of; treasury of; embodiment of

line-538.grammarNote: 'dō.' is a metrical section header abbreviation for dohā. 'kṛpā sukha puñja' is a vocative or nominative compound modifying Rāma.

refrain-tumhari-yaad.grammarNote: Feminine singular agreement: tumharī (fem. poss. pron.) agrees with yāda (fem. noun) and bhalī (fem. adj.).

verse2-line-1.grammarNote: Predicate adjective compound: mahā-sukhadāī (supremely bliss-giving) modifying śaraṇa.

vrindavan-ki-kunj.source: वृन्दावन की कुञ्ज गलिन में सबको नाच नचाये
vrindavan-ki-kunj.roman: Vṛndāvana kī kuñja galina mēṁ sabakō nāca nacāyē

words.gloss: Vṛndāvana, the woodland by the Yamunā associated with Kṛṣṇa’s youth

vrindavan-ki-kunj.grammarNote: Braj/Hindi causative verb 'nacāyē' taking the direct object 'sabakō' and internal cognate accusative 'nāca'.

refrain-1.source: आरती कुंजबिहारी की, श्री गिरिधर कृष्ण मुरारी की
refrain-1.roman: āratī kuñjabihārī kī, śrī giridhara kṛṣṇa murārī kī

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
Krishna; the divine cowherd; Kṛṣṇa means “dark” or “dark-hued”

refrain-1.grammarNote: Feminine head noun āratī governing coordinated genitive postpositions (kī) linked to Krishna's titles.

verse1-4.source: नन्द के नन्द, श्री आनन्दकन्द, मोहन बृजचन्द
verse1-4.roman: nanda ke nanda, śrī ānandakanda, mohana brijacanda
verse1-4.grammarNote: A series of rhyming nominative epithets and compounds placed in apposition.

v1-gunjenge-raag-bankar.grammarNote: Finite future 1st person plural verb 'gūñjeṅge' modified by the conjunctive participle 'bankar' with masculine noun 'rāg'.

words.gloss: melodic mode; traditionally the feminine counterpart of a rāga

v1-har-ragini-ki-dhun-par.grammarNote: Feminine genitive 'rāginī kī' modifying 'dhun', enclosed by quantifier 'har' and postposition 'par'.

v3-tum-soham-shabd-bankar.grammarNote: 2nd person pronoun 'tum' as subject of the conjunctive clause 'soham śabd bankar', introducing the non-dual mantra 'soham' as an appositive modifier to 'śabd'.

v1-veena-ki-taar-banke.grammarNote: Feminine genitive construction 'vīṇā kī tār' followed by conjunctive participle 'banke' (variant of bankar).

v1-hriday-me-pyar-banke.grammarNote: Locative phrase 'hṛday meṁ' modifying the nominal predicate 'pyār' combined with conjunctive participle 'banke'.

v1-svar-banke-utha-karna.grammarNote: Compound verb 'uṭhā karnā' (perfective participle + habitual auxiliary) preceded by conjunctive phrase 'svar banke'.

v2-nachenge-mor-bankar.grammarNote: 1st person plural future verb 'nāceṅge' combined with conjunctive participle 'bankar' and masculine noun 'mor'.

words.gloss: Ghanshyam; Krishna dark as a monsoon cloud

v2-ghanshyam-chhaye-rahna.grammarNote: Vocative compound 'ghanaśyām' with compound continuous verb 'chāye rahnā' (participle of chānā + rahnā as infinitive imperative).

v2-bankar-ke-megh-kare.grammarNote: Conjunctive verbal particle sequence 'bankar ke' governing the inverted noun-adjective phrase 'megh kāre' (Braj/poetic form for kāle megh).

v2-amrit-ki-dhar-bankar.grammarNote: Feminine genitive phrase 'amṛt kī dhār' with conjunctive participle 'bankar'.

v3-pranon-me-rama-karna.grammarNote: Plural oblique noun 'prāṇoṁ' with postposition 'meṁ' modifying the compound habitual verb 'ramā karnā' (participle of ramnā + auxiliary karnā).

v2-l3.source: प्रेम प्यार से सींच ले जीवन, ये अवसर फिर ना आए
v2-l3.roman: Prema pyāra se sīñca le jīvana, ye avasara phira nā āe
v2-l3.grammarNote: Compound verb imperative (sīñca le) with instrumental phrase (prema pyāra se), followed by a paratactic clause of warning (ye avasara phira nā āe).

v3-l4.source: मन की कही पे चलने वाले, फिर पीछे पछताएगा
v3-l4.roman: Mana kī kahī pe calane vāle, phira pīche pachatāegā
v3-l4.english: {4,5:O you who walk }{3:according to }{1,2:the bidding of }{0:the mind, }{8:you will regret it }{6,7:afterwards.}
v3-l4.grammarNote: Vocative agentive phrase (mana kī kahī pe calane vāle) with postposition pe (= par), followed by a future indicative main verb (pachatāegā) with adverbial reinforcement (phira pīche).

param-kripa-de-apni.source: परम कृपा दे अपनी भव से उबारता
param-kripa-de-apni.roman: Parama kṛpā dē apanī bhava sē ubāratā

words.gloss: worldly existence; the ocean of birth and death

param-kripa-de-apni.grammarNote: 'dē' is a truncated conjunctive participle ('dēkar' / giving); 'apanī' is reflexive feminine singular modifying 'kṛpā'; 'ubāratā' is the imperfective habitual verb agreeing with the elided masculine singular subject.

mil-jayega-param-sahara.source: मिल जायेगा, मिल जायेगा, परम सहारा मिल जायेगा
mil-jayega-param-sahara.roman: mila jāyegā, mila jāyegā, parama sahārā mila jāyegā
mil-jayega-param-sahara.english: {0,1:It will be found, }{2,3:it will be found, }{4:supreme }{5:support }{6,7:will be found}
mil-jayega-param-sahara.grammarNote: Inverted word order (verb mila jāyegā fronted before subject parama sahārā) for musical emphasis.

sahaj-kinara-mil-jayega-full.source: सहज किनारा मिल जायेगा, परम सहारा मिल जायेगा
sahaj-kinara-mil-jayega-full.roman: sahaja kinārā mila jāyegā, parama sahārā mila jāyegā
sahaj-kinara-mil-jayega-full.english: {1:The shore }{2,3:will be found }{0:with ease, }{4:supreme }{5:support }{6,7:will be found}
sahaj-kinara-mil-jayega-full.grammarNote: Parallel compound verb constructions (mila jāyegā) balancing two hemistichs.

v1-bheetar-se-man.source: भीतर से मन साफ़ किया ना बाहर माँजे गगरिया
v1-bheetar-se-man.roman: bhītar se man sāf kiyā nā bāhar mām̐je gagariyā
v1-bheetar-se-man.english: {0,1:from within,}{5: you did not}{3,4: clean}{2: the mind,}{6: yet outside}{7: you scour}{8: the pitcher.}
v1-bheetar-se-man.grammarNote: Parallel antithetical clauses: bhītar se man sāf kiyā nā (inner mind was not cleansed) vs bāhar mām̐je gagariyā ([yet] outside you scour the pot). kiyā nā features postposed negation. gagariyā is the poetic diminutive of gāgar.

v2-sukh-paane-tu.source: सुख पाने तू दर-दर भटके जनम हुआ दुखदाई
v2-sukh-paane-tu.roman: sukh pāne tū dar-dar bhaṭke janam huā dukhadāī
v2-sukh-paane-tu.english: {0,1:To find happiness,}{2: you}{4: wander}{3: from door to door,}{5: and life}{6: became}{7: full of sorrow.}

words.gloss: to obtain; in order to get

v2-sukh-paane-tu.grammarNote: Two coordinate clauses: (1) sukh pāne tū dar-dar bhaṭke (infinitival purpose clause + present verb bhaṭke); (2) janam huā dukhadāī (stative result clause with predicate adjective dukhadāī). janam is tadbhava of janma.

v3-swanso-ka.source: श्वासों का अनमोल ख़ज़ाना दिन-दिन लुटता जाए
v3-swanso-ka.roman: śvāsom̐ kā anamol khazānā din-din luṭatā jāe
v3-swanso-ka.english: {2:The priceless}{3: treasure}{1: of }{0:breaths}{4: day by day}{5,6: continues to be plundered;}

words.gloss: day by day; with each passing day
being plundered; being robbed; being squandered

v3-swanso-ka.grammarNote: Continuous passive-intransitive construction: luṭatā (participle of luṭnā) + jāe (auxiliary of progressive aspect). Reduplicated din-din acts as a temporal adverb.

v3-moti-lene.source: मोती लेने आया तट पे सीप से मन बहलाए
v3-moti-lene.roman: motī lene āyā taṭ pe sīp se man bahalāe
v3-moti-lene.english: {2:You came}{3,4: to the shore}{0,1: to gather pearls,}{8: yet amuse}{7: the mind}{5,6: with shells.}
v3-moti-lene.grammarNote: Two coordinate clauses: motī lene āyā taṭ pe (purpose infinitive lene + motion verb āyā) and sīp se man bahalāe (instrumental sīp se + transitive causative verb bahalāe).

v2d.roman: De aisā vardān he maiyā, sumiran terā gāūṅ main
v2d.source: दे ऐसा वरदान हे मैया, सुमिरन तेरा गाऊँ मैं

v1a.roman: Jag meṅ ākar jag ko maiyā, ab tak na pahchān sakā
v1a.english: {2:Having come }{0,1:into the world, }{5:Mother, }{9:I have }{7:not }{6:yet }{9:been able to }{8:recognize }{4:the }{3:world.}
v1a.source: जग में आकर जग को मैया, अब तक न पहचान सका

v1c.roman: Ye bhī na main jān sakā
v1c.source: ये भी न मैं जान सका

v1-lead.source: तू ही सत् चित् सुखमय शुद्ध ब्रह्म रूपा
v1-lead.roman: Tū hī sat cit sukhamaya śuddha brahma rūpā
v1-lead.grammarNote: Tū hī functions as the subject pronoun with emphatic particle; śuddha-brahma-rūpā is a feminine possessive/bahuvrīhi compound in predicate position.

v1-chorus-resp.grammarNote: Maiyā is the vocative of affection; śuddha-brahma-rūpā is in apposition.

v10-lead.source: मूलाधार निवासिनि इह पर सिद्धि प्रदे
v10-lead.roman: Mūlādhāra nivāsini iha para siddhi prade
v10-lead.english: {1:O dweller in the }{0:Muladhara, }{5:bestower of }{4:attainments }{2:in this world }{3:and the beyond.}

words.gloss: “root support”; yogic centre at the base of the spine
