naad-bindu-se.roman: Nād bindu sē pīchē jamāyā pānī pānī ho jī
naad-bindu-se.grammarNote: Ablative compound 'Nād bindu sē'. Transitive causative perfective verb 'jamāyā' taking 'pānī' as direct object; 'ho jī' serves as a respectful refrain tag.

sab-ghat-pooran.source: सब घट पूरन पूरु रह्या है अलख पुरुष निरबानी हो जी बानी हो जी
sab-ghat-pooran.roman: Sab ghaṭ pūran pūru rahyā hai alakh puruṣa nirbānī ho jī bānī ho jī
sab-ghat-pooran.english: {0:In every }{1:vessel, }{2:fully }{3,4:pervading }{5:is }{6:the imperceptible, }{7:Supreme Person, }{8:silent, }{9:O }{10:honored one, }{11:the Word, }{12:O }{13:honored one}
sab-ghat-pooran.grammarNote: Locative sense implied in uninflected noun 'sab ghaṭ' (Braj/Sant Bhasha syntax). 'pūru rahyā hai' is a compound stative verb phrase with masculine singular agreement with 'puruṣa'.

gagan-mein-aawaz-outro.source: गगन में आवाज़ हो रही झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी झीनी
gagan-mein-aawaz-outro.roman: Gagan mē̃ āvāz ho rahī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī jhīnī
gagan-mein-aawaz-outro.grammarNote: Continuous aspect verb 'ho rahī' with feminine singular agreement with 'āvāz'. Twelve consecutive occurrences of adjective 'jhīnī' serving as meditative fade-out/outro.

puri-bhari-phir-kya-tole.grammarNote: Absolute participial phrase 'Pūrī bharī' ('[once] completely filled') followed by the 3rd person potential/habitual rhetorical question 'phira kyā tōlē'.

aaj-badra-utha.grammarNote: Direct Braj/Hindi verse syntax with inverted genitive phrase: temporal adverb (Āja) + subject (badarā) + intransitive perfective verb (uṭhā) + genitive modifier (prēma kā).

eji-badra-utha.source: ए जी बदरा उठा प्रेम का रे हम पर बरसा होय
eji-badra-utha.roman: Ē jī badarā uṭhā prēma kā rē hama para barasā hōya
eji-badra-utha.grammarNote: Compound participial construction 'barasā hōya' expressing the sudden, complete onset of rain upon the 1st person plural pronoun 'hama' used in singular devotional reference.

harsheeli-ho-gayi.source: हर्षीली हो गई आतमा और हरी भरी बनराई
harsheeli-ho-gayi.roman: Harṣīlī hō gaī ātamā aura harī bharī banarāī
harsheeli-ho-gayi.grammarNote: Feminine singular completive verb 'hō gaī' governing feminine singular predicate adjective 'Harṣīlī' and subjects 'ātamā' and 'banarāī'; paired adjectives 'harī bharī' form a rhyming echoic compound.

mann-mast-hua.source: मन मस्त हुआ फिर क्या बोले
mann-mast-hua.roman: Mana masta huā phira kyā bōlē
mann-mast-hua.grammarNote: Paratactic conditional: '[jaba] mana masta huā, phira [vaha] kyā bōlē'; 3rd person potential/habitual verb 'bōlē' functions as a rhetorical negative statement.

mast-hua-phir-kya-bole.grammarNote: Ellipsis of explicit subject noun 'mana', retaining the participial state 'masta huā' and rhetorical predicate 'phira kyā bōlē'.

heera-paaya.grammarNote: Transitive perfective verb 'pāyā' with direct object 'Hīrā', combined with the conjunctive/absolutive verb stem 'bā̃ndha' governing the locative/accusative diminutive noun 'gaṭhariyā'.

words.gloss: swan; the bird in the lake image
Lake Manasarovar; the lake in which the swan bathes

hansa-naahave.grammarNote: Subject noun 'Haṁsā' with Braj 3rd person singular present/habitual verb 'nāhāvē' governing the unmarked locative proper noun 'mānasarōvara'.

sahib-mil-gaya.english: {0:The Master }{1,2:was found }{4:behind the veil of }{3:a sesame seed}
sahib-mil-gaya.grammarNote: Compound completive verb 'mila gayā' with masculine singular subject 'Sāhiba' and postpositional locative phrase 'tila ōlē' ('ōlē' being the oblique of Braj/Rajasthani 'ōlā', meaning veil/screen/shelter).

line-04.source: आवागमन मिट जाय म्हारी हेली रे, चालो म्हारा देश
line-04.roman: Āvāgaman miṭ jāy mhārī helī re, cālo mhārā deś
line-04.english: {0:Coming and going }{1,2:is erased, }{5:O }{3:my }{4:companion, }{6:let us go }{7:to my }{8:country.}

words.gloss: O; a particle of direct address

line-04.grammarNote: Compound verb 'miṭ jāy' (intensifier/completive aspect). 'cālo' is first-person plural / second-person polite hortative imperative.

line-05.source: ल्यो तो आवागमन मिट जाय म्हारी हेली रे, चालो म्हारा देश
line-05.roman: Lyo to āvāgaman miṭ jāy mhārī helī re, cālo mhārā deś
line-05.english: {0:Behold }{1:then, }{2:coming and going }{3,4:is erased, }{7:O }{5:my }{6:companion, }{8:let us go }{9:to my }{10:country.}

words.gloss: O; a particle of direct address

line-05.grammarNote: 'Lyo to' functions as a Rajasthani discourse marker drawing immediate experiential attention ('behold', 'see then').

line-16.source: निर्गुण का बाजार में म्हारी हेली, हीरों को होवे व्यापार
line-16.roman: Nirguṇ kā bājār mẽ mhārī helī, hīrõ ko hove vyāpār
line-16.english: {3:In }{2:the marketplace }{0,1:of the formless Divine, }{4:my }{5:companion, }{9:trade }{6,7:in diamonds }{8:takes place.}
line-16.grammarNote: Rajasthani genitive 'ko' agreeing with 'vyāpār' (hīrõ ko vyāpār = trade of diamonds).

line-17.source: हाँ निर्गुण का बाजार में म्हारी हेली, हीरों को होवे व्यापार
line-17.roman: Hā̃ nirguṇ kā bājār mẽ mhārī helī, hīrõ ko hove vyāpār
line-17.english: {0:Yes, }{4:in }{3:the marketplace }{1,2:of the formless Divine, }{5:my }{6:companion, }{10:trade }{7,8:in diamonds }{9:takes place.}

line-01.source: निर्गुण गलियाँ सांकरी म्हारी हेली, वहाँ चढ़्यो नहीं जाय
line-01.roman: Nirguṇ galiyā̃ sāṅkarī mhārī helī, vahā̃ caṛhyo nahī̃ jāy
line-01.english: {1:The lanes }{0:of the formless Divine }{2:are narrow, }{3:my }{4:companion, }{5:there }{7,8:one cannot }{6:climb.}
line-01.grammarNote: Rajasthani impersonal passive potential construction 'caṛhyo nahī̃ jāy' (cannot be climbed). 'helī' is the standard feminine vocative for a close female companion or the seeker's own soul.

line-02.source: हाँ वहाँ चढ़े तो पिया मिले म्हारी हेली
line-02.roman: Hā̃ vahā̃ caṛhe to piyā mile mhārī helī
line-02.grammarNote: Conditional construction with subjunctive/presumptive verb 'caṛhe' and correlative 'to'. 'piyā mile' uses the passive/ergative meeting construction.

line-03.source: वहाँ चढ़े तो पिया मिले म्हारी हेली
line-03.roman: Vahā̃ caṛhe to piyā mile mhārī helī
line-03.grammarNote: Direct repetition of line 02 without the opening affirmative particle 'Hā̃'.

line-06.source: कहाँ उगे कहाँ आसते म्हारी हेली, कहाँ उजाला होय
line-06.roman: Kahā̃ uge kahā̃ āsate mhārī helī, kahā̃ ujālā hoy
line-06.grammarNote: 'āsate' is derived from Sanskrit 'asta' (setting of heavenly bodies). Triple interrogative structure establishing a devotional riddle.

line-07.source: हाँ यहीं उगे यहीं आसते म्हारी हेली
line-07.roman: Hā̃ yahī̃ uge yahī̃ āsate mhārī helī

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
right here; in this very place

line-07.grammarNote: 'yahī̃' contains the emphatic enclitic '-hī̃' appended to the proximal locative 'yahā̃' ('in this very place / within oneself').

line-08.source: यहीं उगे यहीं आसते म्हारी हेली
line-08.roman: Yahī̃ uge yahī̃ āsate mhārī helī

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
right here; in this very place

line-08.grammarNote: Repetition for musical cadence and devotional emphasis.

line-09.source: यहीं उजाला होय म्हारी हेली रे, चालो म्हारा देश
line-09.roman: Yahī̃ ujālā hoy mhārī helī re, cālo mhārā deś

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
O; a particle of direct address

line-09.grammarNote: Syntactically links the realization of internal light with the journey refrain.

line-10.source: ल्यो तो यहीं उजाला होय म्हारी हेली रे, चालो म्हारा देश
line-10.roman: Lyo to yahī̃ ujālā hoy mhārī helī re, cālo mhārā deś

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
O; a particle of direct address

line-10.grammarNote: 'Lyo to' introduces emphatic direct experience before the refrain clause.

line-11.source: कहाँ को गरजे कहाँ बरसै म्हारी हेली, कहाँ सूखा का हरिया होय
line-11.roman: Kahā̃ ko garje kahā̃ barasai mhārī helī, kahā̃ sūkhā kā hariyā hoy
line-11.english: {0,1:Where }{2:does it thunder, }{3:where }{4:does it rain, }{5:my }{6:companion, }{7:where }{8:does the withered }{9,11:turn }{10:green?}
line-11.grammarNote: 'ko' functions as a dialectal interrogative/emphatic particle with 'kahā̃' ('kahā̃ ko garje' = what thunders where). 'sūkhā kā hariyā hoy' uses 'kā' to mark state transformation from dry to green.

line-12.source: हाँ यहीं गरजे यहीं बरसै म्हारी हेली
line-12.roman: Hā̃ yahī̃ garje yahī̃ barasai mhārī helī

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
right here; in this very place

line-12.grammarNote: Parallel present-tense 3rd person singular verbs 'garje' and 'barasai' denoting internal yogic phenomena.

line-13.source: यहीं गरजे यहीं बरसै म्हारी हेली
line-13.roman: Yahī̃ garje yahī̃ barasai mhārī helī

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
right here; in this very place

line-14.source: यहीं सूखा का हरिया होय म्हारी हेली ओ, चालो म्हारा देश
line-14.roman: Yahī̃ sūkhā kā hariyā hoy mhārī helī o, cālo mhārā deś

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
O; a particle of direct address

line-14.grammarNote: 'o,' is an affectionate vocative exclamation modifying 'helī'.

line-15.source: ल्यो तो लाग्या भजन वाला बाण म्हारी हेली ओ, चालो म्हारा देश
line-15.roman: Lyo to lāgyā bhajan vālā bāṇ mhārī helī o, cālo mhārā deś
line-15.english: {0:Behold }{1:then, }{5:the arrow }{3,4:of devotion }{2:has struck, }{8:O }{6:my }{7:companion, }{9:let us go }{10:to my }{11:country.}

words.gloss: O; a particle of direct address

line-15.grammarNote: 'bhajan vālā bāṇ' is a possessive noun phrase functioning as the grammatical subject of the intransitive/passive verb 'lāgyā'.

line-18.source: हाँ सुगुरा मानव तो सौदो करै म्हारी हेली
line-18.roman: Hā̃ sugurā mānav to saudo karai mhārī helī
line-18.english: {0:Yes, }{2:a person }{1:with a spiritual teacher }{3:indeed }{4,5:makes the trade, }{6:my }{7:companion.}

words.gloss: one who has a spiritual teacher

line-18.grammarNote: 'sugurā' (su- + guru + -ā) is the Sant tradition term for a seeker who has a Guru, paired antonymously with 'nugurā'.

line-19.source: सुगुरा मानव तो सौदो करै म्हारी हेली, ई तो नुगुरा मूल गँवाय म्हारी हेली ओ, चालो म्हारा देश
line-19.roman: Sugurā mānav to saudo karai mhārī helī, ī to nugurā mūl gam̐vāy mhārī helī o, cālo mhārā deś
line-19.english: {1:A person }{0:with a spiritual teacher }{2:indeed }{3,4:makes the trade, }{5:my }{6:companion; }{8:but }{7:the one }{9:without a spiritual teacher }{11:loses }{10:their capital. }{14:O }{12:my }{13:companion, }{15:let us go }{16:to my }{17:country.}

words.gloss: one who has a spiritual teacher
O; a particle of direct address

line-19.grammarNote: 'nugurā' (na- + guru + -ā) is the person devoid of a guru. 'mūl' denotes financial principal as a metaphor for the breath/life-capital of human embodiment.

line-20.source: ओ हो अनहद का मैदान में म्हारी हेली, म्हारा साहिब जी की सेज
line-20.roman: O ho anhad kā maidān mẽ mhārī helī, mhārā sāhib jī kī sej
line-20.english: {0,1:O, }{5:in }{4:the vast expanse }{2,3:of the unstruck sound, }{6:my }{7:companion, }{12:is the bed }{11:of }{8:my }{9,10:Lord.}
line-20.grammarNote: 'anhad' (< Skt. 'anāhata', unstruck vibration). Nominal sentence with omitted present copula 'hai'.

line-21.source: हाँ अनहद का मैदान में म्हारी हेली, म्हारा साहिब जी की सेज
line-21.roman: Hā̃ anhad kā maidān mẽ mhārī helī, mhārā sāhib jī kī sej
line-21.english: {0:Yes, }{4:in }{3:the vast expanse }{1,2:of the unstruck sound, }{5:my }{6:companion, }{11:is the bed }{10:of }{7:my }{8,9:Lord.}

line-22.source: हाँ कहै कबीर धर्मदास से म्हारी हेली
line-22.roman: Hā̃ kahai Kabīr Dharmadās se mhārī helī
line-22.grammarNote: Standard Sant bhanita formula where Kabir addresses his primary disciple Dharmadas.

line-23.source: हाँ कहै कबीर धर्मदास से म्हारी हेली, न तो मरे न बूढ़ा होय म्हारी हेली ओ, चालो म्हारा देश
line-23.roman: Hā̃ kahai Kabīr Dharmadās se mhārī helī, na to mare na būṛhā hoy mhārī helī o, cālo mhārā deś

words.gloss: one whose service is to dharma; Kabīr’s disciple and named addressee
O; a particle of direct address

line-23.grammarNote: na ... na coordinates the two negations: neither dying nor growing old. hoy supplies becoming/growing with būṛhā. The subject is implicit; the English supplies one without naming a realm absent from this line.

line-24.source: ल्यो तो यहीं उजाला होय म्हारी हेली ओ, चालो म्हारा देश
line-24.roman: Lyo to yahī̃ ujālā hoy mhārī helī o, cālo mhārā deś

words.gloss: right here; in this very place
O; a particle of direct address

line-24.grammarNote: Identical structure to line 10 with vocative 'o,'.

line-25.source: या तो लाग्या भजन वाला बाण म्हारी हेली ओ, चालो गुरुजी रे देश
line-25.roman: Yā to lāgyā bhajan vālā bāṇ mhārī helī o, cālo gurujī re deś
line-25.english: {0,1:Truly }{5:the arrow }{3,4:of devotion }{2:has struck, }{8:O }{6:my }{7:companion, }{9:let us go }{10,11:to the revered Guru's }{12:country.}

words.gloss: O; a particle of direct address

line-25.grammarNote: 'gurujī re deś' uses the Rajasthani masculine oblique genitive postposition 're' ('of the revered Guru'). 'Yā to' is an emphatic proximal particle.

line-26.grammarNote: Condensed refrain phrase stripped of vocative addresses.

line-27.grammarNote: Final truncated hortative with attention-calling discourse marker 'Lyo to'.

line-1.source: मैं मेरा घर जाळिया रे जोगिया जियो, दीया पलीता हाथ
line-1.roman: maiṁ mērā ghara jāḷiyā rē jōgiyā jiyō, dīyā palītā hātha
line-1.grammarNote: First-person Rajasthani transitive past construction with subject maiṁ, direct object mērā ghara, and verb phrase jāḷiyā ... dīyā palītā hātha. The vocative address rē jōgiyā jiyō is parenthetical.

line-2.source: कोई जाळो घर आपणो रे जोगिया जियो, चलो हमारे साथ
line-2.roman: kōī jāḷō ghara āpaṇō rē jōgiyā jiyō, calō hamārē sātha
line-2.grammarNote: An open invitation addressed to an unspecified listener: burn your own house and walk with us. The two verbs jāḷō and calō address that listener.

words.gloss: Rāma, the delightful Lord invoked here as the supreme divine reality; the name is also that of Rāma of Ayodhyā
juice; here, the sweetness of devotion pictured as a drink

refrain-1.grammarNote: Nominal phrase headed by the compound rāma rasa preceded by the exclamatory/emphatic particle kai.

refrain-2.source: मीठो घणो रे जोगिया जियो, पीये अमर होय जाय
refrain-2.roman: mīṭhō ghaṇō rē jōgiyā jiyō, pīyē amara hōya jāya
refrain-2.grammarNote: Adjectival clause mīṭhō ghaṇō describing rāma rasa, followed by the participial conditional clause pīyē and compound verb hōya jāya with complement amara.

line-3.source: घर जाळ्यो घर ऊभरे रे जोगिया जियो, घर राखो घर जाय
line-3.roman: ghara jāḷyō ghara ūbharē rē jōgiyā jiyō, ghara rākhō ghara jāya
line-3.english: {0:If the house }{1:is burned, }{2:the home }{3:is saved, }{4:O }{6:noble }{5:ascetic; }{7:if the house }{8:is kept, }{9:the home }{10:is lost.}
line-3.grammarNote: Balanced antithetical couplet with polysemous ghara (first outer house, then inner true home). Each half consists of an absolute conditional participle (jāḷyō / rākhō) and an intransitive present verb (ūbharē / jāya).

line-4.source: एक अचम्भो मैं देखियो रे जोगिया जियो, मढ़ो काल ने खाय
line-4.roman: ēka acambhō maiṁ dēkhiyō rē jōgiyā jiyō, maḍhō kāla nē khāya
line-4.grammarNote: Transitive main clause ēka acambhō maiṁ dēkhiyō followed by the subordinate content clause maḍhō kāla nē khāya with maḍhō as subject and kāla marked with the postposition nē.

line-5.source: आगे आगे धाव जळे रे जोगिया जियो, पीछे हरिया होय
line-5.roman: āgē āgē dhāva jaḷē rē jōgiyā jiyō, pīchē hariyā hōya
line-5.grammarNote: Reduplicated spatial adverb āgē āgē with subject dhāva and intransitive verb jaḷē, contrasted with the adverbial phrase pīchē hariyā hōya.

line-6.source: बलिहारी उन रूखड़ी रे जोगिया जियो, जड़ काटो फल होय
line-6.roman: balihārī una rūkhaṛī rē jōgiyā jiyō, jaṛa kāṭō phala hōya
line-6.english: {0:I offer myself }{1:to that }{2:little tree, }{3:O }{5:noble }{4:ascetic: }{6,7:cut its root, }{9:and it bears }{8:fruit.}

words.gloss: I offer myself in devotion; an expression of self-surrender

line-6.grammarNote: Devotional noun balihārī governing oblique demonstrative and diminutive noun una rūkhaṛī, followed by absolute participial clause jaṛa kāṭō and result phala hōya.

line-7.source: ध्रुव पियो प्रह्लाद पियो रे जोगिया जियो, पीये रह्यो रविदास
line-7.roman: dhruva piyō prahlāda piyō rē jōgiyā jiyō, pīyē rahyō ravidāsa
line-7.grammarNote: Compound declarative line with simple past clauses dhruva piyō and prahlāda piyō, combined with the continuous aspectual construction pīyē rahyō ravidāsa.

line-8.source: भगत कबीर रस पीये रह्यो रे जोगिया जियो, फेर पीवण री आस
line-8.roman: bhagata kabīra rasa pīyē rahyō rē jōgiyā jiyō, phēra pīvaṇa rī āsa

words.gloss: juice; here, the sweetness of devotion pictured as a drink

line-8.grammarNote: Subject bhagata kabīra with continuous verb pīyē rahyō taking direct object rasa, followed by the Rajasthani genitive nominal phrase phēra pīvaṇa rī āsa.

words.gloss: Rāma, the delightful Lord invoked here as the supreme divine reality; the name is also that of Rāma of Ayodhyā
juice; here, the sweetness of devotion pictured as a drink

line-closing.grammarNote: Final repetition of the refrain's opening nominal phrase kai rāma rasa.

tera-hoga-bada-ehsan.source: तेरा होगा बड़ा एहसान कि जुग-जुग तेरी रहेगी शान, भगत भर दे रे झोली
tera-hoga-bada-ehsan.roman: terā hogā baṛā ehasān ki jug-jug terī rahegī śān, bhagat bhar de re jholī
tera-hoga-bada-ehsan.english: {2:Great }{1:will be }{0:your }{3:favor, }{4:so that }{5:age after age }{6:your }{8:glory }{7:will endure; }{9:devotee, }{10,11:fill }{13:the alms bag, }{12:O}

words.gloss: for ages and ages; age after age

tera-hoga-bada-ehsan.grammarNote: 'ki' introduces a result/consequence clause. 'jug-jug' is an emphatic reduplicated noun functioning adverbially. 'rahegī' agrees in gender (fem. sg.) with 'śān'.

ki-us-waqt-hamein.english: {0:when}{1: at that}{2: moment,}{4: Sāīṁ}{5: met}{3: us}{6: before departing}
ki-us-waqt-hamein.grammarNote: 'milke gae' combines the conjunctive participle 'milke' with the honorific/plural past verb 'gae', describing an intentional visit made by the master.

itna-hai-karza.source: इतना है कर्ज़ा मुझ पर मेरे साईं का
itna-hai-karza.roman: itnā hai karzā mujh par mere sāīṁ kā
itna-hai-karza.english: {0:So great}{1,2: is the debt}{4: upon }{3:me}{5,6,7: to my Sai,}
itna-hai-karza.grammarNote: Word order is inverted: standard would be 'mujh par mere sāīṁ kā itnā karzā hai'. 'karzā' is a masculine noun from Arabic qarz.

kitne-hain-upkaar.source: कितने हैं उपकार मुझ पर साईं के
kitne-hain-upkaar.roman: kitne haiṁ upkār mujh par sāīṁ ke
kitne-hain-upkaar.english: {0:How manifold}{1,2: are the favors}{6: of }{5:Sai}{4: upon }{3:me,}
kitne-hain-upkaar.grammarNote: 'upkār' is an unmarked masculine plural noun agreeing with plural copula 'haiṁ' and genitive postposition 'ke'.

line-01-jai.source: श्री सच्चिदानन्द सद्गुरु साईंनाथ महाराज की जय
line-01-jai.roman: Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja kī jaya
line-01-jai.grammarNote: Feminine genitive postposition kī agrees with feminine noun jaya in the conventional celebratory formula.

words.gloss: please take; please do (polite precative auxiliary)

line-03-sun-lije-arji.grammarNote: Compound verb suna līje combines main verb stem sun- with polite precative auxiliary lenā (līje); hamārī agrees in feminine singular with arajī.

line-07-daya-karo.source: दया करो दे दो बाबा कृपा की छाया
line-07-daya-karo.roman: Dayā karo de do bābā kṛpā kī chāyā
line-07-daya-karo.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative clauses: dayā karo and compound imperative de do; kī agrees in feminine singular with chāyā.

line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.source: तुका कहे सेवा मेरी भोली भावड़ी
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.roman: Tukā kahe sevā merī bholī bhāvaḍī
line-08-tuka-kahe-seva.grammarNote: Tukā kahe is the standard third-person singular signature formula; merī, bholī, and bhāvaḍī all agree in feminine singular with sevā.

line-10-utho-panduranga.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग प्रभात समय आ गया
line-10-utho-panduranga.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga prabhāta samaya ā gayā

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-10-utho-panduranga.grammarNote: Uṭho is an imperative second-person plural/honorific; ā gayā is a compound verb (ā- + gayā) expressing completed arrival with masculine subject samaya.

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.source: वैष्णवों का मेला गरुड़ पार आ गया
line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.roman: Vaiṣṇavoṁ kā melā Garuḍa Pāra ā gayā

words.gloss: of Vaishnavas; of devotees of Vishnu

line-11-vaishnavo-ka-mela.grammarNote: Garuḍa Pāra is an unmarked locative goal of motion; melā is masculine singular governing the compound verb ā gayā.

line-12-garuda-par-se.source: गरुड़ पार से महाद्वार देहरी तक
line-12-garuda-par-se.roman: Garuḍa Pāra se mahādvāra deharī taka
line-12-garuda-par-se.english: {2:From }{0:the Garuda }{1:platform }{5:up to }{4:the threshold }{3:of the main gate,}
line-12-garuda-par-se.grammarNote: Ablative se paired with inclusive postposition taka establishes a continuous spatial corridor between two temple landmarks.

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.source: शुक सनकादिक नारद तुम्बर भक्त हैं कोटि
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.roman: Śuka Sanakādika Nārada Tumbara bhakta haiṁ koṭi
line-14-shuka-sanakadik.english: {0:Shuka, }{1:Sanaka and the sages, }{2:Narada, }{3:Tumburu, }{6:and crores }{4:of devotees }{5:are present.}

words.gloss: the enlightened sage son of Vyasa

line-14-shuka-sanakadik.grammarNote: A list of proper nouns acting as plural subject governing the plural auxiliary haiṁ; koṭi functions as a post-nominal numeral quantifier modifying bhakta.

line-15-trishula-damaru.source: त्रिशूल डमरू लेकर आये गिरिजा के पति
line-15-trishula-damaru.roman: Triśūla ḍamarū lekara āye Girijā ke pati

words.gloss: small hourglass drum associated with Śiva

line-15-trishula-damaru.grammarNote: Lekara is a conjunctive participle ('having taken'); āye is plural/honorific masculine agreeing with the subject Girijā ke pati.

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.source: कलियुग का भक्त नामा बना कीर्तनी
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.roman: Kaliyuga kā bhakta Nāmā banā kīrtanī
line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.english: {3:Nama, }{2:the devotee }{0,1:of the Kali age, }{4:has become }{5:the lead singer of praise,}

words.gloss: kirtan singer; lead performer of holy song

line-16-kaliyuga-ka-bhakta.grammarNote: Kaliyuga kā bhakta modifies Nāmā in apposition; banā is a simple past/perfective verb governing predicate noun kīrtanī.

line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.source: पीठ पीछे खड़ी आके बन्दगी ये जनी
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.roman: Pīṭha pīche khaḍī āke bandagī ye Janī
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.english: {2:Standing }{0,1:right behind his back, }{5:this }{6:Jani }{3:has come }{4:in humble homage.}
line-17-pith-pichhe-khadi.grammarNote: Pīṭha pīche is a locative phrase; khaḍī is feminine singular agreeing with Janī; āke is a conjunctive participle.

line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.source: उठो उठो श्री साईंनाथ गुरु चरण कमल दिखलाओ
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.roman: Uṭho uṭho Śrī Sāīnātha guru caraṇa kamala dikhalāo
line-18-utho-utho-sainatha.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative uṭho uṭho shows heightened urgency; caraṇa kamala is a karmadhāraya compound functioning as direct object of causative imperative dikhalāo.

line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.source: फिर भी अज्ञान सी छाई है तुम्हरी योग माया
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.roman: Phira bhī ajñāna sī chāī hai tumharī yoga māyā
line-21-phir-bhi-agyana.grammarNote: Compound phrase 'yoga māyā' acts as the feminine singular subject agreeing with 'chāī hai'; 'ajñāna sī' is an adjectival modifier of state.

line-24-bho-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative structure: 'Bho' introduces the titles; 'bhavatimiranāśaka' is a Sanskrit tatpuruṣa compound (bhava + timira + nāśaka) modifying 'ravi'.

line-32-uthakar-netra.source: उठाकर नेत्र पलकें दीन बन्धु रमाकान्ता
line-32-uthakar-netra.roman: Uṭhākara netra palakeṁ dīna bandhu Ramākāntā
line-32-uthakar-netra.english: {0:Lifting }{2:the eyelids }{1:of Your eyes, }{4:O friend }{3:of the humble, }{5:O beloved of Lakshmi,}

words.gloss: beloved of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī, as fortune and splendour; Lord Viṣṇu

line-32-uthakar-netra.grammarNote: 'uṭhākara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on 'dekho' in line 33; 'dīna bandhu' and 'Ramākāntā' are vocative epithets.

line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.source: सुनाओ मधुर वाणी हरो ताप साईंनाथा
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.roman: Sunāo madhura vāṇī haro tāpa Sāīnāthā
line-34-sunao-madhur-vani.grammarNote: Two coordinate imperative verbs 'sunāo' and 'haro' addressed to the vocative 'Sāīnāthā'.

line-36-sahan-karke-aao.source: सहन करके आओ चाहे भेट कृष्ण देवा
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.roman: Sahana karake āo cāhe bheṭa Kṛṣṇa devā
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.english: {0,1:bearing it patiently, }{2:come forth; }{3:one longs for }{4:a meeting, }{6:O Lord }{5:Krishna!}
line-36-sahan-karke-aao.grammarNote: 'sahana karake' is a conjunctive participle modifying 'āo'; 'cāhe bheṭa' has an inverted word order with implied subject ('the world/devotee desires a meeting').

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.source: उठो पाण्डुरङ्ग अब तो दर्शन दो सबको
line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.roman: Uṭho Pāṇḍuraṅga aba to darśana do sabako

words.gloss: the pale/white-hued one; Viṭṭhala of Paṇḍharpur

line-37-utho-panduranga-ab-to.grammarNote: Coordinate imperatives 'uṭho' and 'do'; 'Pāṇḍuraṅga' is vocative; 'to' adds emphatic pleading.

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.source: राई रखुमाबाई मन में आने दो दया
line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.roman: Rāī Rakhumābaī mana meṁ āne do dayā

words.gloss: Rakhumābāī, Rukmiṇī the gold-adorned goddess; consort of Viṭṭhala

line-43-rai-rakhumabai-man-me.grammarNote: Vocative direct address 'Rāī Rakhumābaī' governing permissive verbal construction 'āne do' with direct object 'dayā'.

words.gloss: Hanumān, the one with prominent jaws; Rāma’s divine attendant and devotee

line-45-garuda-hanumanta-thade.grammarNote: Plural subject 'Garuḍa Hanumanta' takes the stative participle 'ṭhāḍe' and imperfective verb 'johate'; 'bāṭa' is the accusative complement of the idiom.

line-48-vishnudasa-nama-khada.grammarNote: Appositive proper noun 'Viṣṇudāsa Nāmā' is the subject of the predicate adjective 'khaḍā' with conjunctive participle phrase 'lekara kākaḍā'.

line-49-lekar-pancharati.source: लेकर पञ्चारती करूँ बाबा की आरती
line-49-lekar-pancharati.roman: Lekara pañcāratī karūṁ bābā kī āratī
line-49-lekar-pancharati.english: {0:Holding }{1:the five-flame lamp, }{2:I offer }{5:worship with lights }{3,4:to Baba.}

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-49-lekar-pancharati.grammarNote: First person singular verb 'karūṁ' taking 'āratī' as direct object; 'pañcāratī' is governed by 'lekara'.

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.source: उठो उठो हे बान्धव मनाओ ये रमाधव
line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.roman: Uṭho uṭho he bāndhava manāo ye Ramādhava

words.gloss: Ramādhava, husband of Ramā, the delightful Lakṣmī who embodies fortune and splendour; Viṣṇu

line-50-utho-utho-he-bandhava.grammarNote: Reduplicated imperative 'uṭho uṭho' for devotional emphasis; vocative 'he bāndhava'; second-person plural imperative 'manāo'.

line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.source: कृष्णनाथा दत्त साई पदों में चित्त जड़े साई
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.roman: Kṛṣṇanāthā Datta Sāī padoṁ meṁ citta jaḍe Sāī
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.english: {0:Krishnanatha }{6:fixes }{5:his consciousness }{3,4:at the feet }{1,2:of Datta Sai, }{7:O Sai.}
line-52-krishnanatha-datta-sai.grammarNote: Subject 'Kṛṣṇanāthā' with transitive verb 'jaḍe' (3rd person singular present in poetic Hindi); 'Sāī' is repeated at the end for rhythmic emphasis.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-53-kakada-arati-karata.grammarNote: Participle 'karatā' used as finite present verb with implicit first-person subject; 'Sāīnātha devā' is in the vocative case.

line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.source: साईंनाथ के भक्ति ताप से उसको जलाया
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.roman: Sāīnātha ke bhakti tāpa se usako jalāyā
line-57-sainatha-ke-bhakti.grammarNote: Causative/transitive past verb 'jalāyā' taking pronoun 'usako' as direct object; 'bhakti tāpa se' is the instrumental cause.

line-61-aise-datta-deva.source: ऐसे दत्त देव शिरडी रहकर भी मिलते
line-61-aise-datta-deva.roman: Aise Datta deva Śiraḍī rahakar bhī milate
line-61-aise-datta-deva.english: {0:In such a way} {1,2:Lord Datta} {6:meets seekers,} {4,5:even while dwelling} {3:in Shirdi.}

words.gloss: Shirdi (the sacred village of Sai Baba)

line-61-aise-datta-deva.grammarNote: Aise functions adverbially modifying milate. Rahakar is a conjunctive participle (rah- + kar) expressing simultaneous or attendant circumstance.

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.source: सगुण दर्शन पाने जन जन शिरडी आ रहा
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.roman: Saguṇa darśana pāne jana jana Śiraḍī ā rahā
line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.english: {2:To obtain} {1:the sacred vision} {0:of your embodied form,} {3,4:multitudes of people} {6,7:are coming} {5:to Shirdi.}

words.gloss: with manifest attributes; embodied divine form

line-66-saguna-darshana-pane.grammarNote: Pāne is the oblique infinitive of purpose. Jana jana is a distributive reduplication functioning as a singular collective subject with masculine singular agreement in ā rahā.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
I wave in offering; I circle

line-72-arati-utaru-mere.grammarNote: Paṇḍharīnāthā is in the vocative case (Paṇḍharīnātha + ā extension common in devotional Marathi/Hindi verse).

line-73-mere-sainatha.grammarNote: Vocative phrase standing in direct apposition to Paṇḍharīnāthā in line 72.

line-80-inta-para-khada.source: ईंट पर खड़ा हुआ है सुन्दर बाबा
line-80-inta-para-khada.roman: Ī̃ṭa para khaḍā huā hai sundara bābā

words.gloss: brick (the sacred brick thrown by Pundalik)

line-80-inta-para-khada.grammarNote: Ī̃ṭa para is a locative postpositional phrase. Khaḍā huā hai is a stative periphrastic construction agreeing with the masculine subject sundara bābā.

line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.source: उठकर भोर में बाबा खड़े हैं ईंट पे
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.roman: Uṭhakara bhora meṁ bābā khaḍe haiṁ ī̃ṭa pe
line-83-uthkar-bhor-me.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle 'uṭhakara' preceding the main predicate 'khaḍe haiṁ'. Honorific plural verb 'haiṁ' and participle 'khaḍe' with singular subject 'bābā'. Postposition 'pe' is a colloquial variant of 'par'.

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.source: केशवराज ईंट पे खड़े नामा चरण पूजते
line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.roman: Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe Nāmā caraṇa pūjate

words.gloss: King Keśava, the fine-haired lord, here Viṭṭhala

line-92-keshavaraja-inta-pe.grammarNote: Two balanced clauses combined in one line: 'Keśavarāja ī̃ṭa pe khaḍe [haiṁ]' and 'Nāmā caraṇa pūjate [haiṁ]'. 'Nāmā' refers to the Marathi saint-poet Namdev.

line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.source: साईंनाथ गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.roman: Sāīnātha guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Sainath, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sai.}
line-93-sainatha-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: Vocative titles 'Sāīnātha', 'guru merī māī', and 'Sāī'. 'De do' is a compound verb (stem 'de' + vector verb 'do') forming a polite/pleading imperative. 'Caraṇoṁ' is the oblique plural of 'caraṇa'.

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.source: दत्तराज गुरु मेरी माई चरणों में स्थान दे दो साईं
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.roman: Dattarāja guru merī māī caraṇoṁ meṁ sthāna de do Sāī
line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.english: {0:O Dattaraja, }{1:guru }{2:and my }{3:mother, }{7,8:grant }{6:a place }{4,5:at your feet, }{9:O Sai.}

words.gloss: King Datta, the given one; Lord Dattātreya

line-94-dattaraja-guru-meri-mai.grammarNote: 'Dattarāja' is a tatpuruṣa/karmadhāraya title (Datta + rāja). Syntax and verbal morphology identical to line 93.

line-20-gai-chhod-kar.source: गई छोड़ कर भव से रजनी तम ने विलय पाया
line-20-gai-chhod-kar.roman: Gaī choḍa kara bhava se rajanī tama ne vilaya pāyā

words.gloss: having done (choḍa kara = having left behind)

line-20-gai-chhod-kar.grammarNote: First clause gaī choḍa kara bhava se rajanī uses inverted word order with feminine singular subject rajanī; second clause tama ne vilaya pāyā is an ergative transitive construction where tama acts as subject of pāyā.

line-22-shakti-nahi.source: शक्ति नहीं यत्किञ्चित उसको ना सरका पाया
line-22-shakti-nahi.roman: Śakti nahīṁ yatkiñcita usako nā sarakā pāyā

words.gloss: in the least; even a little

line-22-shakti-nahi.grammarNote: Subject is elided; 'yatkiñcita' is a Sanskrit adverbial loanword ('the slightest bit'); 'sarakā pāyā' is a potential compound verb construction with negative marker 'nā'.

line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.source: तुम्ही हटा कर मुख दिखलाना जन तारो राया
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.roman: Tumhī haṭā kara mukha dikhalānā jana tāro rāyā
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.english: {0:You alone, }{1,2:having removed it, }{4:reveal Your }{3:face; }{6:deliver }{5:the devotees, }{7:O King!}
line-23-tumhi-hata-kar.grammarNote: 'haṭā kara' is a conjunctive participle dependent on polite imperative 'dikhalānā'; 'rāyā' is a Marathi-derived vocative honorific ('O Sovereign/Lord').

line-27-sakripa-hokar.source: सकृप होकर अपनी महिमा खुद ही सुनवाओ
line-27-sakripa-hokar.roman: Sakṛpa hokara apanī mahimā khuda hī sunavāo
line-27-sakripa-hokar.grammarNote: 'sunavāo' is a second-person plural/polite causative imperative of 'sunnā' (to hear); 'sakṛpa hokara' functions as a participial adjunct.

line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.source: देखो ऐसे देखे जैसे बालक को माता
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.roman: Dekho aise dekhe jaise bālaka ko mātā
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.english: {0:look }{1:in such a way }{3:as }{6:a mother }{2:looks }{4,5:upon her child!}
line-33-dekho-aise-dekhe.grammarNote: 'dekho' is a direct imperative; 'aise... jaise' introduces a correlative comparative clause with the verb 'dekhe' agreeing with singular subject 'mātā'.

line-35-hum-hi-apni.source: हम ही अपनी खातिर तुमको कष्ट देते देवा
line-35-hum-hi-apni.roman: Hama hī apanī khātira tumako kaṣṭa dete devā
line-35-hum-hi-apni.grammarNote: 'devā' is a Marathi-influenced vocative form; 'kaṣṭa dete' has an elided auxiliary 'haiṁ' typical of verse.

line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.source: त्वद्वचनामृत प्राशन कर के देहभान खो रहा
line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.roman: Tvadvacanāmṛta prāśana kara ke dehabhāna kho rahā
line-67-tvad-vachanamrita-prashana-karke.grammarNote: Tvadvacanāmṛta is a compound noun: tvad- (your) + vacana (speech) + amṛta (nectar). Prāśana kara ke is an adverbial conjunctive participial clause.

line-89-dvara-pe-baje.source: द्वार पे बाजे बजते ढोल ढमाढम गरजते
line-89-dvara-pe-baje.roman: Dvāra pe bāje bajate ḍhola ḍhamāḍhama garajate
line-89-dvara-pe-baje.grammarNote: Parallel imperfective participles 'bajate' and 'garajate' functioning as finite present tense verbs with omitted auxiliary 'haiṁ'. 'Ḍhamāḍhama' is an onomatopoeic adverb.

refrain-1.source: मैं किस्मत का मारा साईं कैसे तेरे दर्शन पाऊँ
refrain-1.roman: maĩ kismat kā mārā sāī̃ kaise tere darśan pāū̃
refrain-1.english: {0:I,}{1,2,3: struck by fate,}{4: O Sai,}{5: how}{8: may I receive}{6,7: your sacred vision?}
refrain-1.grammarNote: First-person singular pronoun maĩ modified by participial genitive phrase kismat kā mārā; optative/subjunctive 1st-person verb pāū̃.

v1-1.source: देखना चाहूँ तेरी सूरत पर आँखों से अंधा हूँ
v1-1.roman: dekhanā cāhū̃ terī sūrat par ā̃khõ se andhā hū̃
v1-1.english: {0,1:I wish to see}{2: your }{3:face,}{4: but}{7,8: I am blind}{5,6: in my eyes.}
v1-1.grammarNote: Infinitive dekhanā with finite modal cāhū̃; oblique plural ā̃khõ with ablative/instrumental postposition se indicating respect/cause of defect.

v1-3.source: दे सकते तो दे दो आँखें रूप तेरा मैं देख सकूँ
v1-3.roman: de sakate to de do ā̃khẽ rūp terā maĩ dekh sakū̃
v1-3.english: {0,1:If you can give,}{2,3,4: then give}{5: eyes,}{8,9,10: that I may see}{7: your }{6:form.}
v1-3.grammarNote: Conditional protasis with unexpressed subject/copula (āp) de sakate (ho) to; compound imperative de do; potential subjunctive dekh sakū̃.

v2-response.grammarNote: Adverbial participial phrase ās lie modifying first-person stative construction maĩ baiṭhā hū̃.

v2-3.source: दे सकते तो दो वरदान तेरी कथाएँ सुन पाऊँ
v2-3.roman: de sakate to do varadān terī kathāē̃ sun pāū̃
v2-3.english: {0,1:If you can give,}{2,3: then grant}{4: a boon,}{7,8: that I may hear}{5: your }{6:stories.}

words.gloss: may be able to; succeed in

v2-3.grammarNote: Conditional protasis de sakate to; imperative do governing direct object varadān; final purpose clause with compound potential verb sun pāū̃.

vachan-3.source: यदि गया मैं यह देह तज के तो भी दौड़ूँगा भक्त के हित में
vachan-3.roman: yadi gayā maĩ yah dēh taj kē tō bhī dauṛū̃gā bhakt kē hit mē̃
vachan-3.english: {0:Even if}{2: I}{1: depart}{5,6: having cast off}{3: this}{4: body}, {8:even }{7:then}{9: I will run}{12,13: for the welfare}{10,11: of the devotee.}

words.gloss: I will run; I will hasten

vachan-3.grammarNote: Concessive conditional yadi gayā maĩ ... tō bhī. taj kē is a conjunctive participle ('having relinquished'). Postpositional phrase kē hit mē̃ governs bhakt.

vachan-6.source: शरण मेरी आया और व्यर्थ गया दिखाओ दिखाओ जो ऐसा है कोई
vachan-6.roman: śaraṇ mērī āyā aur vyarth gayā dikhāō dikhāō jō aisā hai kōī
vachan-6.english: {6:Show,}{7: show}{8,10: if there is}{11: anyone}{9: such}{2: who came}{1: to my}{0: refuge}{3: and}{5: went away}{4: in vain.}
vachan-6.grammarNote: Reduplication of the imperative dikhāō dikhāō marks intense rhetorical challenge. Relative clause jō aisā hai kōī acts as the object of dikhāō.

vachan-7.source: मुझको भजे जो जिस भावना से वैसा ही पहुँचूँ मैं पास उसके
vachan-7.roman: mujh kō bhajē jō jis bhāvanā sē vaisā hī pahuñcū̃ maĩ pās usakē
vachan-7.english: {3:Whoever}{2: worships}{0,1: me}{6: with }{4:whatever}{5: devotional feeling}{7,8:, in that very way}{10: I}{9: reach}{11,12: near to them.}
vachan-7.grammarNote: Correlative structure jis bhāvanā sē ... vaisā hī. Subjunctive/present bhajē correlates with 1st person singular subjunctive/future pahuñcū̃.

vachan-9.source: यहाँ मिलती है मदद सभी को माँगे जो जो वही मिलता है उसको
vachan-9.roman: yahā̃ milatī hai madad sabhī kō mā̃gē jō jō vahī milatā hai usakō
vachan-9.english: {0:Here}{3: help}{2: is }{1:received}{4,5: by everyone;}{7,8: whatever}{6: one asks for,}{9: that very thing}{11: is }{10:received}{12: by them.}
vachan-9.grammarNote: Dative subject construction: sabhī kō madad milatī hai (madad agrees with feminine singular milatī hai). Reduplicated relative jō jō correlates with vahī in the dative construction usakō milatā hai.

vachan-10.source: मेरा जो हुआ है काया वाचा मन से उसका ऋणी मैं सदा सर्वदा ही
vachan-10.roman: mērā jō huā hai kāyā vācā man sē usakā ṛṇī maĩ sadā sarvadā hī
vachan-10.english: {1:Whoever}{3: has }{2:become}{0: mine}{7: through }{4:body,}{5: speech,}{6: and mind,}{8: to them}{10: I}{9: am indebted}{11: always}{12: and forever}{13: indeed.}
vachan-10.grammarNote: Adverbial triad kāyā vācā man sē (instrumental compound phrase). Ellipsis of copula hū̃ in the second clause: [maĩ] usakā ṛṇī [hū̃].

doha-2.source: बाल न बांका कर सके जो जग बैरी होय
doha-2.roman: Bāla na bāṅkā kara sake jo jaga bairī hoya
doha-2.english: {5:Even if }{6:the world }{8:becomes }{7:an enemy, }{1,4:it cannot }{2,3:bend }{0:a single hair.}
doha-2.grammarNote: jo functions conditionally as 'even if'; hoya is subjunctive 3sg; bāla bāṅkā kara sake na combines the noun bāla, adjective bāṅkā, and modal potential verb.

verse-1-line-1.source: राह तुम्हारी देख देख मेरी अखियां भर भर आईं
verse-1-line-1.roman: Rāha tumhārī dekha dekha merī akhiyāṁ bhara bhara āīṁ
verse-1-line-1.english: {2,3:Watching and watching }{1:your }{0:path, }{4:my }{5:eyes }{6,7,8:have filled and filled with tears.}
verse-1-line-1.grammarNote: dekha dekha and bhara bhara are reduplicated verb stems indicating continuous/intense action; āīṁ is feminine plural perfective agreeing with akhiyāṁ.

doha-1.source: जाको राखे साइयां मार सके ना कोय
doha-1.roman: Jāko rākhe sāiyāṁ māra sake nā koya
doha-1.grammarNote: Old Hindi/Braj relative pronoun jāko (dative/accusative) pairing with correlative in doha-2; rākhe is 3sg present/subjunctive; māra sake is modal compound with negative nā.

bas-dhool-jo-mil-jaaye.grammarNote: Compound verb 'mil jānā' in 3rd person singular feminine/masculine subjunctive form with conditional marker 'jo'.

words.gloss: one's own / my own (reflexive feminine possessive)

sach-kehta-hoon-bas-apni.grammarNote: 'Apnī' is the feminine reflexive possessive adjective modifying 'taqdīr' in the following line.

ik-boond-jo-mil-jaaye.grammarNote: 'Bū̃d' is feminine singular noun; 'mil jāe' is 3rd person singular subjunctive.

words.gloss: drop; cast down; lower (infinitive as polite imperative)

nazron-se-giraana-na.grammarNote: Infinitive 'girānā' with postposed negative 'nā' functions as a polite/habitual negative imperative.

nazron-se-jo-gir-jaaye.grammarNote: Intransitive compound verb 'gir jānā' in 3rd person singular subjunctive with relative subject 'jo'.

words.gloss: is able to / manages to (potential subjunctive auxiliary)

mushkil-wo-sambhal-paaye.grammarNote: 'Sambhal pānā' is a potential compound verb; 'muśkil' functions as a negative-leaning adverb ('hardly').

mera-dam-hi-nikal-jaaye.grammarNote: Compound verb 'nikal jānā' in 3rd person singular masculine subjunctive.

sai-teri-mandir-ki-ho.source: साईं तेरी मंदिर की मैं घंटी बन कर आऊँ, हो
sai-teri-mandir-ki-ho.roman: sāīṁ terī mandira kī maiṁ ghaṇṭī bana kara āūm̐, ho

words.gloss: O Sāī, revered master and lord
may I come / return (1st person singular subjunctive)

sai-teri-mandir-ki-ho.grammarNote: terī mandira kī shows colloquial gender agreement where terī agrees with either the postpositional phrase target (ghaṇṭī) or functions as a general possessive qualifier; bana kara is a conjunctive participle.

sai-teri-mandir-ki.source: साईं तेरी मंदिर की मैं घंटी बन कर आऊँ
sai-teri-mandir-ki.roman: sāīṁ terī mandira kī maiṁ ghaṇṭī bana kara āūm̐

words.gloss: O Sāī, revered master and lord
may I come / return (1st person singular subjunctive)

sai-teri-mandir-ki.grammarNote: maiṁ is the grammatical subject of the subjunctive verb āūm̐.

words.gloss: that much; proportionally as (feminine correlative adjective/adverb)

utni-hi-kam-hai-ho.grammarNote: utanī agrees in gender with feminine praśaṁsā in line 18.

utni-hi-kam-hai-teri-prashansa.source: उतनी ही कम है तेरी प्रशंसा जितनी करता जाऊँ
utni-hi-kam-hai-teri-prashansa.roman: utanī hī kama hai terī praśaṁsā jitanī karatā jāūm̐
utni-hi-kam-hai-teri-prashansa.english: {6:However much }{7:I praise }{4:You, }{8:on and on, }{0:that much }{5:praise }{1:still }{2,3:falls short,}

words.gloss: as much as; however much (feminine relative adjective/adverb)
I may continue to (1st person singular subjunctive)

utni-hi-kam-hai-teri-prashansa.grammarNote: Correlative pair: jitanī (relative) ... utanī (correlative), both agreeing in feminine gender with praśaṁsā; karatā jāūm̐ uses continuative aspect.

tere-naam-ki-hi-mala.source: तेरे नाम की ही माला मैं हरदम जपता जाऊँ
tere-naam-ki-hi-mala.roman: tere nāma kī hī mālā maiṁ haradama japatā jāūm̐

words.gloss: may I go on (1st person singular subjunctive)

tere-naam-ki-hi-mala.grammarNote: haradama is an adverbial compound (har + dam, 'every breath'); japatā jāūm̐ is the imperfective participle with jānā expressing continuative aspect in the 1st person subjunctive.

baba-teri-mandir-ki.source: बाबा तेरी मंदिर की मैं घंटी बन कर आऊँ
baba-teri-mandir-ki.roman: bābā terī mandira kī maiṁ ghaṇṭī bana kara āūm̐

words.gloss: may I come / return (1st person singular subjunctive)

baba-teri-mandir-ki.grammarNote: Final repetition of the central refrain with the intimate vocative bābā.

verse-3-1.source: दान धर्म से मोह है घटता यह बतलाने आये
verse-3-1.roman: dān dharm se moh hai ghaṭtā yah batlāne āye

words.gloss: right order, duty, or sustaining principle
to explain; to teach; to show

verse-3-1.grammarNote: `dān dharm se moh hai ghaṭtā` is an embedded declarative clause functioning as the antecedent of `yah`. `batlāne` is an oblique infinitive of purpose governing `āye`.

verse-1-2.source: तू दे ना दे फिर भी साईं
verse-1-2.roman: tū de nā de phir bhī sāīṁ
verse-1-2.english: {0,1:Whether you give }{2,3:or do not give, }{4,5:even so, }{6:Sai}
verse-1-2.grammarNote: `tū de nā de` is an alternative subjunctive construction expressing a concession ('whether you give or do not give'). `sāīṁ` is the subject of the verb in verse-1-3.

verse-3-2.grammarNote: `ho jāye` is a compound subjunctive verb (`ho` + `jānā`). The phrase exhibits inverted genitive placement (`uskā` at the end).

aasani-se-kat-jayega.source: आसानी से कट जाएगा कांटों भरा रास्ता
aasani-se-kat-jayega.roman: āsānī sē kaṭa jāēgā kāṇṭōṁ bharā rāstā
aasani-se-kat-jayega.grammarNote: Intransitive compound verb 'kaṭa jānā' inflected in masculine singular future ('kaṭa jāēgā') agreeing with 'rāstā'. Adjectival phrase 'kāṇṭōṁ bharā' qualifies 'rāstā'.

uske-liye-sab-ek-hain.source: उसके लिए सब एक हैं करता है सबका भला
uske-liye-sab-ek-hain.roman: usakē liē saba ēka haiṁ karatā hai sabakā bhalā
uske-liye-sab-ek-hain.grammarNote: Compound sentence: 1) equational clause 'usakē liē saba ēka haiṁ'; 2) transitive habitual clause 'karatā hai sabakā bhalā' with unexpressed third-person singular subject.

muniyon-ne-rishiyon-ne-guru-shishya-mahi.source: मुनियों ने ऋषियों ने गुरु शिष्य महिमा का
muniyon-ne-rishiyon-ne-guru-shishya-mahi.roman: muniyoṁ ne ṛṣiyoṁ ne guru śiṣya mahimā kā
muniyon-ne-rishiyon-ne-guru-shishya-mahi.grammarNote: Coordinated oblique plural nouns with ergative postposition 'ne'; 'kā' agrees in masculine singular with 'guṇgān' in line 21.

line-000.source: श्री सच्चिदानंद सद्गुरु साईनाथ महाराज की जय
line-000.roman: Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja kī jaya
line-000.grammarNote: Standard Hindi/Marathi jaikāra formula; 'kī' is the feminine genitive postposition agreeing with feminine noun 'jaya'.

line-001.source: ओवाळू आरती माझ्या सद्गुरुनाथा माझ्या साईनाथा
line-001.roman: Ovāḷū āratī mājhyā sadgurunāthā mājhyā sāīnāthā
line-001.english: {0:Let me wave }{1:the āratī }{2:before my }{3:Sadguru Lord, }{4:my }{5:Lord Sai.}

words.gloss: let me wave in circle; I wave
ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it
unto the true teacher and master

line-001.grammarNote: Ovāḷū is the 1st person singular optative/present of ovāḷaṇe; 'sadgurunāthā' and 'sāīnāthā' take the oblique/dative vocative marker -ā.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-013.grammarNote: Jñānarājā is vocative/dative formed from jñāna + rājā.

line-019.grammarNote: Brahmaci has the emphatic enclitic -ci ('verily / alone'); kēlē is neuter singular past agreeing with viśva.

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-025.grammarNote: Dhāmā is vocative singular form of dhāma.

line-031.grammarNote: Abhaṅga is neuter plural; rakṣilē is neuter plural past participle.

line-033.grammarNote: Brahma is neuter singular subject; ālē is neuter past participle; Tukāsī has the dative/objective suffix -sī.

line-037.source: आळवितो सप्रेमे तुजला आरती घेउन करी हो
line-037.roman: Āḷavitō saprēmē tujalā āratī ghēuna karī hō

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-037.grammarNote: Āḷavitō is 1st person masculine present of āḷavaṇe; ghēuna is absolutive participle ('having taken'); karī is locative singular/plural.

line-052.source: आळवितो सप्रेमे तुजला आरती घेवून करी हो
line-052.roman: āḷavito sapreme tujalā āratī gheūna karī ho

words.gloss: ritual waving of light before a deity; the hymn sung with it

line-052.grammarNote: āḷavito from āḷavaṇē ('to invoke, sing plaintively'). karī is locative singular of kara ('hand').

line-067.grammarNote: Standard Hindi/Marathi victory formula: [Name/Title] + kī jaya ('victory to...').

line-069.source: पाहे प्रसादाची वाट द्यावे धुवोनिया ताट
line-069.roman: pāhe prasādācī vāṭa dyāve dhuvoniyā tāṭa
line-069.english: {0,2:[I] await }{1:the prasad; }{4:having washed }{5:the dining plate, }{3:please give it.}
line-069.grammarNote: pāhe vāṭa is an idiomatic light verb construction ('awaits'). dhuvoniyā is an archaic Marathi conjunctive participle ('having washed').

line-073.source: पावला प्रसाद आता उठोनि जावे बाबा आता निजवे
line-073.roman: pāvalā prasāda ātā uṭhoni jāve bābā ātā nijave
line-073.english: {1:The prasad }{0:is received; }{2:now, }{3:rising, }{4:one should depart, }{5:O Baba, }{6:now }{7:please rest.}

words.gloss: one should go; we shall leave

line-073.grammarNote: jāve and nijave are impersonal potential/optative verb forms used as polite imperatives. pāvalā agrees with masculine prasāda.

line-008.grammarNote: Kheḷoniyā is the absolutive/conjunctive participle ('having played'); vistāra kelā is an ergative compound verb.

line-041.source: झाले असतील कष्ट अतिशय तुमचे या देहाला हो
line-041.roman: Jhālē astatīla kaṣṭa atiśaya tumacē yā dēhālā hō
line-041.grammarNote: Jhālē astatīla forms a compound presumptive past ('must have occurred'). dēhālā is dative/accusative marked with -lā.

line-046.source: सोडुनि जाया दुःख वाटते बाबांच्या चरणांशी हो
line-046.roman: Sōḍuni jāyā duḥkha vāṭatē Bābāñcyā caraṇāñśī hō

words.gloss: at the feet; from the feet

line-046.grammarNote: Impersonal dative/experiencer syntax: sōḍuni jāyā duḥkha vāṭatē ('leaving to go feels sorrowful'). Bābāñcyā carries honorific plural genitive -ñcyā.

line-047.source: सोडुनि जाया दुःख वाटते साईंच्या चरणांशी हो
line-047.roman: Sōḍuni jāyā duḥkha vāṭatē Sāīñcyā caraṇāñśī hō

words.gloss: at the feet; from the feet

line-047.grammarNote: Sāīñcyā has the honorific plural genitive suffix -ñcyā.

line-056.grammarNote: śiḍakāvā didhalā is a conjunct verb ('gave a sprinkling'). supremācā = su- + prēma + genitive -cā.

line-057.source: पायघड्या घातल्या सुंदर नवविधा भक्ती बाबा नवविधा भक्ती
line-057.roman: pāyaghaḍyā ghātalyā suṁdara navavidhā bhaktī bābā navavidhā bhaktī
line-057.grammarNote: pāyaghaḍyā is feminine plural (from pāyaghaḍī); ghātalyā is the agreeing feminine plural perfect participle.

line-070.source: शेष घेउनि जाइल तुमचे झालिया भोजन
line-070.roman: śeṣa gheuni jāila tumace jhāliyā bhojana
line-070.grammarNote: jhāliyā bhojana is an absolute participial construction ('when dining has occurred'). jhāliyā is oblique/locative participle.

line-175.english: {3,4:Every single day}{1: taking bath}{2: and reciting japa}{0: in Kashi,}
line-175.grammarNote: Elliptical nominal phrase describing Dattatreya's daily spiritual routine.

line-182.source: कमंडलु मृगछाला धारित है सिर पे
line-182.roman: kamaṇḍalu mṛgachālā dhārita hai sira pe
line-182.english: {0:A water-pot}{1: and deerskin}{2,3: donned,}{4,5: and on your head}
line-182.grammarNote: Passive/attributive construction with locative 'sira pe' continuing into the next line.

line-012.source: तुम्हारी उपमा तुम्हे ही शोभित है सज्जना
line-012.roman: Tumhārī upamā tumhe hī śobhit hai sajjanā
line-012.english: {0:Your }{1:praise}{5: is }{4:befitting}{2,3: to you alone,}{6: O noble one.}
line-012.grammarNote: Dative experiencer construction ('tumhe... śobhit hai'). 'Sajjanā' is a vocative form addressing the Guru.

line-015.source: अजात रिपु सद्गुरु अखिल पातक भंजना
line-015.roman: Ajāt ripu sadguru akhil pātaka bhañjanā
line-015.english: {2:O Sadguru}{0: without }{1:enemy,}{5: destroyer}{3,4: of all sins!}
line-015.grammarNote: Vocative compounds: 'ajāt-ripu' (bahuvrīhi: having no enemy / friend to all) and 'akhil-pātaka-bhañjana' (destroyer of all sins).

line-018.source: ऐसा सुहितकारी इस जगत में कोई अन्य ना
line-018.roman: Aisā suhitakārī is jagat meṁ koī anya nā
line-018.english: {0,1:Such a benefactor}{5,7: there is no}{6: other}{4: in }{2:this }{3:world.}
line-018.grammarNote: Existential sentence with negative particle 'nā' functioning as predicate and copula omitted.

line-020.source: व्यर्थ बड़बड़ करे न जाने हित स्वयं का
line-020.roman: Vyartha baṛbaṛ kare na jāne hit svayaṁ kā
line-020.english: {0,1,2:he babbles in vain}{3,4: and does not know}{5,6,7: his own welfare.}
line-020.grammarNote: Habitual 3rd-person singular verbs 'kare' and 'jāne' describing the person devoid of grace.

line-024.source: करूँ सतत सत्कृति सुमति दो जगत पावना
line-024.roman: Karūṁ satat satkṛti sumati do jagat pāvanā
line-024.english: {0,1:May I constantly do}{2: virtuous deeds;}{3,4: grant right intellect,}{5,6: O purifier of the world.}
line-024.grammarNote: 'Jagat-pāvanā' is a vocative compound ('O purifier of the world'). 'Do' is a familiar/respectful imperative.

line-027.source: ऐसा श्री साईनाथ ने कहकर बताया जैसा इस बालक से
line-027.roman: Aisā Śrī Sāīnāth ne kahakar batāyā jaisā is bālak se

line-125.grammarNote: Two first-person singular present verbs ('vandūṁ', 'dekhūṁ') expressing acts of physical surrender and devotion.

line-131.source: अच्युतं केशवं रामनारायणं कृष्णदामोदरं वासुदेवं हरिम्

line-132.source: श्रीधरं माधवं गोपिकावल्लभं जानकीनायकं रामचंद्रं भजे

line-139.source: स मे कामान् कामकामाय मह्यं कामेश्वरो वैश्रवणो दधातु

line-139.grammarNote: Optative-benedictory prayer with double dative recipient ('kāmakāmāya mahyaṁ') and 3rd-person imperative verb 'dadhātu'.

line-141.source: ॐ स्वस्ति साम्राज्यं भौज्यं स्वाराज्यं वैराज्यं पारमेष्ठ्यं राज्यं महाराज्यमाधिपत्यमयं समन्तपर्यायी स्यात्

line-141.grammarNote: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 8.15, a royal-consecration blessing. The opening Oṃ is liturgical; the Vedic formula is governed by optative syāt and enumerates forms of sovereignty.

line-151.source: बचा शेष जीवन भक्ति में ही गमावें

line-155.source: दिखे अज्ञ जन सा जन जो भी आते

line-157.source: नर देह पाया उत्तम यही है

line-158.english: {0,1:that one performs spiritual discipline—}{3:this alone}{2,4: is its true fulfillment.}

line-166.english: {4:The cowherd maiden}{0,3: beholds the sight}{1,2: of his feet,}

line-120.source: करम कराल कंस भूमिपाल के भरोसे बकी बकभगिनी काहू ते कहा डरैगी

line-148.source: देवी देव दनुज मनुज मुनि सिद्ध नाग छोटे बड़े जीव जेते चेतन अचेत हैं।

line-151.source: क्रोध कीजे कर्म को प्रबोध कीजे तुलसी को सोध कीजे तिनको जो दोष दुख देत हैं॥

line-183.source: तुलसी गोसाँई भयो भोंड़े दिन भूली गयो ताको फल पावत निदान परिपाक हौं॥

line-198.source: माया जीव काल के करम के सुभाय के करैया राम बेद कहै साँचै मन गुनिए

line-015.source: संताप पाप तेहि पुरुष पहिं सपनेहुँ नहिं आवत निकट

line-020.source: भानु सो पढ़न हनुमान गए भानु मन अनुमानि सिसुकेलि कियो फेरफार सो

semantic.reason: No named deity or spiritual figure from the controlled vocabulary appears in the text; the central subject is an allegorical/narrative ox (baḷada) enduring bondage and suffering.; The text depicts bondage, entrapment, physical suffering, and forgetting one's inner soul (ātmā) through an allegory of an ox, but none of the available controlled themes (e.g., liberation, impermanence, detachment) directly match this specific narrative without importing external doctrinal assumptions.; Supported concepts outside the current vocabulary are retained for taxonomy review.
