verse-2-line-3.grammarNote: Participial clause of manner: 'hāta ṭhāri' (noun 'hāta' + conjunctive participle 'ṭhāri' functioning adverbially with main verb 'ḍāke').

words.gloss: into the hands; at the disposal

nijaku-teki-dei-prabhunka-hatare.grammarNote: Compound participle `ṭeki de'i` governing accusative reflexive `nijaku` and genitive-locative destination `prabhuṅka hātare`.

words.gloss: unattached one; free from worldly attachment

nirmohi-atura-helure.grammarNote: Vocative epithet `nirmohī` followed by predicate adjective `ātura`, 2nd person past finite verb `helu`, and vocative clitic `re`.

bata-sarigale-khata-chhadijiba-totere.source: ବାଟ ସରିଗଲେ ଖଟ ଛାଡ଼ିଯିବ ତତେ ରେ
bata-sarigale-khata-chhadijiba-totere.roman: bāṭa sarigale khaṭa chāṛijiba tote re

words.gloss: when it ends; upon running out

bata-sarigale-khata-chhadijiba-totere.grammarNote: Compound conditional participle `sarigale` (`sari` + `gale`) followed by main clause where inanimate `khaṭa` acts as the active grammatical subject of future compound verb `chāṛijiba` (`chāṛi` + `yiba`), taking accusative object `tote`.

sheshe-deba-kie-mukhe-tope-pani.source: ଶେଷେ ଦେବ କିଏ ମୁଖେ ଟୋପେ ପାଣି
sheshe-deba-kie-mukhe-tope-pani.roman: śeṣe deba ki'e mukhe ṭope pāṇi
sheshe-deba-kie-mukhe-tope-pani.english: {0:At the end, }{2:who }{1:will give }{4:a drop of }{5:water }{3:into your mouth?}

words.gloss: at the end; in the final moment

sheshe-deba-kie-mukhe-tope-pani.grammarNote: Interrogative clause with fronted temporal locative `śeṣe`, 3rd person future verb `deba`, interrogative subject `ki'e`, locative complement `mukhe`, and quantified direct object `ṭope pāṇi`.

e-katha-bi-tora-mone-nahire.source: ଏ କଥା ବି ତୋର ମନେ ନାହିଁ ରେ
e-katha-bi-tora-mone-nahire.roman: e kathā bi tora mane nāhī̃ re
e-katha-bi-tora-mone-nahire.grammarNote: Possessive/experiencer construction where subject `e kathā bi` is negated by existential copula `nāhī̃` relative to locative `mane` and genitive `tora`.

mati-re-mati-re.grammarNote: Vocative repetition of the noun 'māṭi' with the Odia vocative clitic 're'.

words.gloss: how much; so much; how persistently

kete-dakuchi-re-tote.grammarNote: ḍākuchi is present continuous aspect (stem ḍāka- + -uchi); tote is second-person singular accusative/dative.

sneha-mamata-sathere.grammarNote: Coordinate nominal pair 'sneha mamatā' governed by postposition 'sāthere' (sāthe + locative/emphatic -re).

sneha-mamata-sathe.grammarNote: Postposition 'sāthe' appearing without the emphatic clitic '-re'.

words.gloss: in the earth; in the soil; from clay
in the earth; in the soil; upon clay

matire-janami-tu-matire-badhilu.grammarNote: janami is an Odia conjunctive participle (janam- + -i); baṛhilu is 2nd-person past indicative (-ilu); māṭire carries the locative marker -re.

words.gloss: you fashioned; you built; you shaped

matira-kolare-jibana-gadhilu.grammarNote: Māṭira is genitive singular; koḷare is locative singular of koḷa (lap); gaṛhilu is 2nd-person past indicative.

words.gloss: the physical body; the mortal lump/frame

mati-pindaku-chhari-dine.grammarNote: chāṛi is a non-finite conjunctive participle; piṇḍaku is accusative singular (piṇḍa + -ku); dine is locative of dina (day).

words.gloss: you will go; you shall depart
on the path; on the road

jibu-tu-ajana-pathe.grammarNote: jibu is 2nd-person future indicative of stem jā-/ji-; pathe is locative singular of patha.

words.gloss: you will go; you shall depart
on the path; on the road

jibu-tu-ajana-pathe-re.grammarNote: Identical to previous line with the final emphatic/vocative particle 're'.

duniyara-jete-apanara-jana.grammarNote: duniyāra is genitive singular; jete acts as a relative quantifier modifying the noun phrase 'āpaṇāra jana'.

words.gloss: they will abandon; they will leave behind

chharijibe-tote-nama-jasa-dhana.grammarNote: Chāṛijibe is a compound verb (chāṛi + jibe, 3rd person plural future); tote is accusative singular; nāma, jaśa, dhana form an asyndetic coordinate list.

words.gloss: will break down; will collapse; will shatter

bhangijiba-dine-tora.grammarNote: Bhāṅgijiba is a 3rd singular future compound verb (bhāṅgi + jiba); tora is genitive possessive qualifying 'ghara' in the next line.

balukara-ehi-ghara.grammarNote: Bālukāra is genitive singular modifying ghara; ehi is a proximal demonstrative adjective.

words.gloss: already-begun karma bearing its present result

verse-6b.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle kāṭi connects the subject Guru to the finite causative verb in verse-6c; prārabdha ṛṇa is the direct object compound.

verse-3c.grammarNote: Correlative adverb sete matches jete of verse-3b; nīti acts adverbially (Sanskrit nitya / nīti = regular, perpetual).

narara-karama-chali-sathire-1.grammarNote: Genitive noun 'narara' modifies 'karama'. 'cāli' functions here as a finite/participial motion verb with locative postposition 'sāthirē'.

narara-karama-chali-sathire-2.grammarNote: Repetition of line 5 without trailing punctuation.

words.gloss: already-begun karma bearing its present result
in the play; in the game

prarabdha-karmara-khelare-1.grammarNote: 'prārabdha' modifies genitive noun 'karmara', which in turn modifies locative noun 'khēḷarē'.

words.gloss: already-begun karma bearing its present result
in the play; in the game

prarabdha-karmara-khelare-2.grammarNote: Locative phrase concluding the first verse unit.

words.gloss: in the play; in the game

karama-runara-khelare-1.grammarNote: 'karama' functions in tatpuruṣa compound or noun phrase with genitive 'ṛṇara', modifying locative 'khēḷarē'.

words.gloss: in the play; in the game

karama-runara-khelare-2.grammarNote: Final locative cadence of the song.

jana-mili-jae.grammarNote: Collective noun 'jana' takes singular 3rd person compound verb 'miḷi jāe'.

v1-4.source: ଜ୍ଞାନ କର୍ମ ଭକ୍ତି ଦେଇ ମତେ ଯେ ଉଦ୍ଧାର
v1-4.roman: Jñāna karma bhakti dei mate je uddhāra

words.gloss: action and its moral consequences; selfless action

v1-4.grammarNote: dei is the conjunctive participle of debā (to give); uddhāra acts as a verbal noun / truncated imperative ([kara] uddhāra).

v2-1.source: ବିଶ୍ଵ ତୁମ ଅଂଶ ମାତ୍ର ତୁମେ ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣବ୍ରହ୍ମ
v2-1.roman: Biśwa tuma aṁśa mātra tume pūrṇabrahma
v2-1.grammarNote: Nominal sentence with copula omitted; pūrṇabrahma is a tatpuruṣa/karmadhāraya compound (pūrṇa + brahma).

v2-2.source: ହେ ଶୂନ୍ୟ ପୁରୁଷ ତୁମେ ଶୂନ୍ୟାତୀତ ବ୍ରହ୍ମ
v2-2.roman: He śūnya puruṣa tume śūnyātīta brahma
v2-2.grammarNote: śūnyātīta is a compound of śūnya (void) + atīta (gone beyond / transcendent); nominal predicate brahma.

v2-4.source: ପାରି ହେବା ପାଇଁ ଏଇ ମାୟାର ସଂସାର
v2-4.roman: Pāri hebā pāĩ ei māyāra saṁsāra

words.gloss: crossing across; reaching the far shore
of the power of worldly appearance

v2-4.grammarNote: pāri hebā pāĩ forms a purposive verbal compound ('in order to cross'); māyāra is genitive modifying saṁsāra.

refrain-2.source: ଅପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଜୀବନେ ମୋର ଭକ୍ତି ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ କର
refrain-2.roman: Apūrṇa jībane mora bhakti pūrṇa kara
refrain-2.grammarNote: jībane carries the locative case suffix -e; apūrṇa contrasts antithetically with pūrṇa.

v1-1.source: ମୁଁ ଯେ ଛାର ଅଣୁଟିଏ ବିଶ୍ଵ ପ୍ରାଙ୍ଗଣର
v1-1.roman: Mũ je chāra aṇuṭie biśwa prāṅgaṇara
v1-1.english: {0:I am }{1:indeed }{2:a wretched }{3:tiny particle }{5:of the courtyard }{4:of the universe,}

words.gloss: a single tiny particle; a minuscule atom

v1-1.grammarNote: aṇuṭie combines aṇu (atom/particle) + enclitic diminutive/singular marker -ṭie; prāṅgaṇara has genitive -ra.

refrain-main.grammarNote: baraṣe carries the locative suffix -e; āsiachi is present perfect third-person singular (ās- + -iachi); naba kaḷebara functions as a compound noun subject.

v3-sobha.roman: ki sundara śobhā dekha naba kaḷebara
v3-sobha.grammarNote: ki is an exclamatory modifier; sundara modifies śobhā; dekha is second-person imperative; naba kaḷebara stands as the genitive/associative thematic object of the splendor.

atuta-bhabara-sathe.source: ଅତୁଟ ଭାବର ସାଥେ ଭକ୍ତି କର୍ମ ଜ୍ଞାନ
atuta-bhabara-sathe.roman: Atuṭa bhābara sāthe bhakti karma jñāna
atuta-bhabara-sathe.grammarNote: Atuṭa is a negative tatpuruṣa (a- + tuṭa 'broken'); bhābara is genitive governed by postposition sāthe; bhakti, karma, jñāna stand in coordinate asyndeton.

agatira-gati-prabhu.grammarNote: Agatira combines privative a- + gati ('path/way/shelter') with genitive suffix -ra; kṛpābanta is formed with possessive suffix -banta (-vat).

mahodadhi-kule.source: ମହୋଦଧି କୂଳେ କଳ୍ପବଟ ମୂଳେ ବିଜଯେ କାଳିଆ ମୂରତି
mahodadhi-kule.roman: Mahodadhi kūḷe kalpabaṭa mūḷe bijaye kāḷiā mūrati
mahodadhi-kule.english: {1:On the shore }{0:of the great ocean, }{3:at the foot of }{2:the Kalpabata tree, }{4:is seated in majesty }{5:the dark }{6:divine form.}
mahodadhi-kule.grammarNote: Locative endings in -e on kūḷe and mūḷe denote location. 'Bijaye' is a stylized Odia present-tense honorific verb form used for royal and divine deities.

adikalu-bhakta.source: ଆଦିକାଳୁ ଣକ୍ତ ରକ୍ଷଣେ ମଗନ ବିରାଜିତ କୃପାମୂରତି
adikalu-bhakta.roman: Ādikāḷu bhakta rakṣaṇe magana birājita krupāmūrati
adikalu-bhakta.english: {0:From the beginning of time, }{3:absorbed }{2:in protecting }{1:devotees, }{4:seated in glory }{5:is the embodiment of mercy.}
adikalu-bhakta.grammarNote: Ablative suffix -u on Ādikāḷu indicates temporal origin ('since primordial time'). Rakṣaṇe carries locative -e marking the sphere of absorption.

ho-birajita.english: {0:O... }{1:seated in glory }{2:is the embodiment of mercy.}
ho-birajita.grammarNote: Vocative particle 'Ho...' precedes the nominative epithet compound.

koti-koti-prana.english: {0,1:Crores upon crores of }{2:living souls }{4:call out }{3:to the One alone,}
koti-koti-prana.grammarNote: Reduplication of 'koṭi' intensifies quantity. 'Goṭiku' is 'goṭi' (single/one) with dative/accusative marker '-ku'. 'Ḍākaï' has the archaic/poetic 3rd-person singular present inflection -aï.

dina-dukhi-arati.english: {0:The poor and suffering }{1:offer }{2:their prayer of distress.}
dina-dukhi-arati.grammarNote: Dīnadukhī functions as a collective nominal subject. Ārati carries the dual devotional nuance of ritual offering and distressed supplication (ārti).

ho-dina-dukhi-arati.english: {0:O... }{1:the poor and suffering }{2:offer }{3:their prayer of distress.}

jaga-mahaprana.grammarNote: Compounds in apposition to the deity. 'Jaga' and 'jagata' both represent Sanskrit 'jagat' (world/cosmos).

akhila-brahmandapati.grammarNote: 'Brahmāṇḍapati' is a tatpuruṣa compound (brahmāṇḍa + pati) modified by 'akhiḷa'. Followed by vocative particle 'ho...'.

ho-bijaye-kalia.grammarNote: Refrain reprise identical to the core clause of line 1.

kete-kete-bhakta.grammarNote: Reduplication of 'kete' denotes vast plural quantity. 'Karanti' is 3rd-person honorific present tense.

nandighosa-rathe-rahi.grammarNote: 'Nandighoṣa' is the proper name of Lord Jagannatha's chariot. 'Rathe' is locative in -e. 'Rahi' is an absolutive/conjunctive participle ('having stayed / while standing').

bhabagrahi-se-je.english: {1:He }{0:is the receiver of devotional feeling, }{2:indeed }{4:the embodiment }{3:of forgiveness,}
bhabagrahi-se-je.grammarNote: 'Bhābagrāhī' is a traditional title (bhāva-grāhin). 'Kṣamāra' is genitive in -ra qualifying 'mūrati'. 'Je' acts as an emphatic or relative marker ('verily / who is').

words.gloss: of the people of the world

jagata-jananka-pati.grammarNote: 'Jagatajanaṅka' combines 'jagata' (world) + 'jana' (people) with the honorific genitive plural suffix '-aṅka'.

bijaye-kalia-outro.grammarNote: Identical in grammar and vocabulary to the main clause of the opening refrain.

v4-5.english: {2:Beyond all qualities, }{3:Brahman }{1:in a form }{0:endowed with qualities,}

words.gloss: endowed with qualities / with manifest attributes

v4-5.grammarNote: 'Saguṇa' (sa- + guṇa) and 'nirguṇa' (nir- + guṇa) form a philosophical contrast. 'rūpare' is locative (rūpa + -re). 'brahma' is the subject.

v4-6.grammarNote: 'Brahmadārurūpī' is a compound: brahma + dāru + rūpa + -ī. 'ādi caitanya' is an appositional noun phrase (ādi + caitanya).

words.gloss: Person of the Primordial Void / Transcendent Being

v8-9.grammarNote: 'Śūnyapuruṣa' (śūnya + puruṣa) reflects the Mahima/Odia Vaishnava concept of the transcendent divine void. 'ciraśāśwata' = cira + śāśvata.

line-pahacha-8-f.source: ଅଷ୍ଟମେ ଗୁହାରି କଲି କାଟ ଅଷ୍ଟପାଶ / ମାୟାପୀଡ଼ିତ ଭକ୍ତର ଆହେ ଅବିନାଶ
line-pahacha-8-f.roman: aṣṭame guhāri kali kāṭa aṣṭapāśa / māyāpīṛita bhaktara āhe abināśa
line-pahacha-8-f.english: {0:On the eighth,}{2: I made}{1: an earnest plea:}{3: sever}{4: the eight bonds}{6: of the devotee}{5: afflicted by māyā,}{7: O}{8: Imperishable One.}
line-pahacha-8-f.grammarNote: aṣṭame is locative ordinal. kāṭa is direct 2nd person imperative. bhaktara is genitive singular. āhe abināśa is a vocative invocation ('O Imperishable One').

line-pahacha-8-m.source: ଅଷ୍ଟମେ ଗୁହାରି କଲି କାଟ ଅଷ୍ଟପାଶ / ମାୟାପୀଡ଼ିତ ଭକ୍ତର ଆହେ ଅବିନାଶ
line-pahacha-8-m.roman: aṣṭame guhāri kali kāṭa aṣṭapāśa / māyāpīṛita bhaktara āhe abināśa
line-pahacha-8-m.english: {0:On the eighth,}{2: I made}{1: an earnest plea:}{3: sever}{4: the eight bonds}{6: of the devotee}{5: afflicted by māyā,}{7: O}{8: Imperishable One.}
line-pahacha-8-m.grammarNote: Identical syntax and morphemes to line-pahacha-8-f.

line-pahacha-9.source: ନବମ ପାହାଚେ ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ନବଗ୍ରହ / ଯୋଡ଼ହସ୍ତେ ଛନ୍ତି ଠିଆ ଚାହିଁ ତୁମ ମୁହଁ
line-pahacha-9.roman: nabama pāhāce dṛśya hele nabagraha / yoṛahaste chanti ṭhiā cāhiṁ tuma muhaṁ
line-pahacha-9.english: {0:On the ninth}{1: step,}{4: the nine planets}{3: became}{2: visible;}{6: they are}{7: standing}{5: with folded hands,}{8: gazing upon}{9: your}{10: face.}
line-pahacha-9.grammarNote: nabagraha is the plural subject. hele is 3rd person plural past auxiliary. chanti ṭhiā is a present progressive verbal phrase ('are standing'). cāhiṁ is a conjunctive participle.

line-pahacha-16.source: ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ପାହାଚେ ମାତା ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ଦେବୀଙ୍କୁ / ସ୍ମରିଲି ସୃଷ୍ଟିର ମୂଳ ଷୋଡ଼ଶ ଶକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ
line-pahacha-16.roman: ṣoṛaśa pāhāce mātā ṣoṛaśa debīṅku / smarili sṛṣṭira mūḷa ṣoṛaśa śaktiṅku
line-pahacha-16.english: {0:On the sixteenth}{1: step,}{5: I remembered}{3: the sixteen}{2: Mother}{4: Goddesses,}{8: the sixteen}{7: primal}{9: Shaktis}{6: of creation.}
line-pahacha-16.grammarNote: debīṅku and śaktiṅku carry the plural/honorific accusative suffix -ṅku. sṛṣṭira is genitive singular. smarili is 1st person past indicative.

line-pahacha-19.source: ଉଣେଇଶ ପାହାଚରେ ପତିତପାବନ / ମନ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳ ଅତି ଲଭିବାକୁ ଦର୍ଶନ
line-pahacha-19.roman: uṇe'iśa pāhācare patitapābana / mana byākuḷa ati labhibāku darśana
line-pahacha-19.english: {0:On the nineteenth}{1: step}{2: is Patitapabana;}{3: my heart}{5: is exceedingly}{4: anxious}{6: to attain}{7: darshan.}

words.gloss: sacred sight / vision of the deity

line-pahacha-19.grammarNote: pāhācare is locative. patitapābana stands as the devotional focus. labhibāku is an infinitive of purpose in -bāku governing darśana.

line-pahacha-21.source: ଏକୋଇଶି ପାହାଚେ ପ୍ରଣାମି ଦେବଦେବୀ / ଡାକିଲି ଦର୍ଶନ ଦିଅ ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ ସ୍ୱାମୀ
line-pahacha-21.roman: eko'iśi pāhāce praṇāmī debadebī / ḍākili darśana di'a jagannātha swāmī
line-pahacha-21.english: {0:On the twenty-first}{1: step,}{2: having bowed to}{3: the gods and goddesses,}{4: I called out,}{6: grant}{5: darshan,}{7: O Jagannath}{8: Swami!}
line-pahacha-21.grammarNote: praṇāmī is a non-finite conjunctive participle ('having saluted'). debadebī is a dvandva compound ('gods and goddesses'). ḍākili is 1st person past. di'a is a direct 2nd person imperative.

line-pahacha-13.source: ଚଢ଼ି ତ୍ରୟୋଦଶ ପାହାଚେ କଲି ଜୁହାର / ତୁମ ଅବତାର ରୂପ ନୃସିଂହାବତାର
line-pahacha-13.roman: caṛhi trayodaśa pāhāce kali juhāra / tuma abatāra rūpa nṛsiṁhābatāra
line-pahacha-13.english: {0:Having climbed}{1: onto the thirteenth}{2: step,}{3,4: I offered salutations}{7: to the form}{5: of your}{6: descent,}{8: the Narasimha incarnation.}
line-pahacha-13.grammarNote: caṛhi is a conjunctive participle. trayodaśa pāhāce is a locative phrase. juhāra kali is a compound verbal expression with 1st person past marking.

ab-to-thodi-si-umr.source: अब तो थोड़ी सी उम्र है बाकी
ab-to-thodi-si-umr.roman: ab tō thōṛī sī umra hai bāqī

words.gloss: a little / just a bit of

ab-to-thodi-si-umr.grammarNote: thōṛī sī uses the attenuative enclitic sī agreeing with feminine noun umra; bāqī hai forms a predicative adjective construction.

kahin-aane-mein-der.source: कहीं आने में देर ना हो जाये
kahin-aane-mein-der.roman: kahīm̐ ānē mēṁ dēr nā hō jāyē
kahin-aane-mein-der.grammarNote: kahīm̐ with nā and the subjunctive compound verb hō jāyē conveys the modal sense 'lest it happen'.

zindagi-se-darta-tha.source: ज़िंदगी से डरता था मैं पहले, मौत की अब परवाह नहीं है
zindagi-se-darta-tha.roman: zindagī sē ḍaratā thā maiṁ pahalē, maut kī ab parvāh nahīṁ hai
zindagi-se-darta-tha.grammarNote: ḍaratā thā represents past habitual aspect; maut kī parvāh nahīṁ hai is a nominal negative possessive/predicative clause.

jise-aapki-sharan.grammarNote: Dative-subject construction where jisē receives the nominative noun śaraṇ with compound subjunctive mil jāyē.

words.gloss: power of worldly appearance and delusion

main-maya-mein-ghira-bechara.grammarNote: `ghirā` is a past/stative participle from intransitive/passive `ghirnā` ('to be surrounded'), agreeing in masculine singular with `Maĩ`. `bechārā` functions as an appositive descriptive adjective.

v1-2.source: तुम ना आओगे तो हम रूठ जाएंगे
v1-2.roman: Tum nā āōgē tō ham rūṭh jāēṅgē

words.gloss: sulking / turning away in loving pique

v1-2.grammarNote: Compound verb 'rūṭh jānā' (stem 'rūṭh' + future auxiliary 'jāēṅgē') expressing entrance into a state of loving pique.

v2-2.source: हमें ना सता तू बता दे इरादे
v2-2.roman: Hamēṁ nā satā tū batā dē irādē
v2-2.grammarNote: Negative intimate imperative 'nā satā' paired with compound intimate imperative 'batā dē' with direct object 'irādē'.

v2-3.source: तू ना जाने क्या हमरा मनुआ रे
v2-3.roman: Tū nā jānē kyā hamrā manuā rē
v2-3.grammarNote: Dialectal/vernacular possessive 'hamrā' and diminutive/affectionate noun 'manuā' (heart/mind). 'Kyā' marks a rhetorical query.

v2-4.grammarNote: Compound postposition 'kē saṅg' governing oblique noun phrase 'hamārē jīvan' with imperative verb 'chalō'.

v3-1.source: रात ना बीते रे दिन भी दुगना
v3-1.roman: Rāt nā bītē rē din bhī dugnā
v3-1.grammarNote: Two concise parallel clauses; the second clause has an elliptical predicate ('din bhī dugnā [lagtā hai]').

v3-3.source: मिलना नहीं था तो किसने कहा था तुम्हें
v3-3.roman: Milnā nahīṁ thā tō kisnē kahā thā tumhēṁ
v3-3.grammarNote: Infinitive of destiny/intention 'milnā nahīṁ thā' paired with past perfect ergative question 'kisnē kahā thā tumhēṁ'.

v4-3.source: प्यार जताए तू हमको रुलाए रे
v4-3.roman: Pyār jatāē tū hamkō rulāē rē
v4-3.grammarNote: Two juxtaposed coordinate vernacular verb forms 'jatāē' and 'rulāē' around pronoun 'tū' and accusative/dative 'hamkō'.

v4-4.source: कभी आ जाए कभी छुप जाए रे
v4-4.roman: Kabhī ā jāē kabhī chhup jāē rē
v4-4.grammarNote: Correlative temporal adverbs 'kabhī ... kabhī' pairing two compound verbal expressions 'ā jāē' and 'chhup jāē' with vocative 'rē'.

refrain_2.source: लगी ये कैसी लगा रहे हो
refrain_2.roman: Lagī ye kaisī lagā rahe ho
refrain_2.english: {2:What kind of }{0:longing }{1:is this }{3:that You are causing to take hold?}

words.gloss: attachment, longing, a feeling that has taken hold
You are causing to take hold, instilling

verse_1_4.source: तुम्ही को फिर क्यों तुम्ही तो मन में समा रहे हो
verse_1_4.roman: Tumhī ko phir kyoṃ tumhī to man meṃ samā rahe ho

verse_2_4.source: तुम्ही को ढूँढूँ ये कैसी रीति चला रहे हो
verse_2_4.roman: Tumhī ko ḍhūṇḍhūṃ ye kaisī rīti chalā rahe ho
verse_2_4.english: …{1:I search for }{0:You alone: }{3:what kind of }{4:practice }{2:is this }{5:You are setting in motion?}

words.gloss: You are carrying on, setting in motion

refrain-1.english: {1:Into the inner corner}{0: of the soul,}{2: You}{3: descend,}
refrain-1.grammarNote: Genitive singular noun 'ātmāra' modifies the locative compound 'antarakoṇe' (antara + koṇa + e). 'tame' is the 2nd-person pronoun governing the 2nd-person imperative verb 'abatara'.

verse1-1.english: {3,4:Stir}{2: the life-breath}{1: with the sorrow}{0: of the suffering one,}
verse1-1.grammarNote: Genitive 'duḥkhīra' qualifies locative/instrumental 'duḥkhare'. 'prāṇa' is the direct object and 'āndoḷita' is the predicative adjective governed by causative/transitive imperative 'kara'.

verse1-3.source: ଶତ୍ରୁକୁ ବି ସେବା କରିବାର ଶକ୍ତି ଦିଅ
verse1-3.roman: Śatruku bi sebā karibāra śakti dia
verse1-3.english: {5:Give}{4: the strength}{3: to do}{2: service}{1: even}{0: to an enemy,}
verse1-3.grammarNote: Dative/accusative 'śatruku' with emphatic clitic 'bi'. Verbal noun genitive 'karibāra' complements noun 'śakti', which is the direct object of 2nd-person imperative 'dia'.

verse2-6.english: {1:Make}{2: me}{0: absorbed in the Guru,}{4: make}{2: me}{3: filled with service.}
verse2-6.grammarNote: Accusative 1st-person pronoun 'mote' serves as direct object for both occurrences of 'kara'. 'gurumaya' and 'sebāmaya' are predicative adjectives.

bhanga-kudia-1.source: ଭଙ୍ଗା କୁଡ଼ିଆ ମୋ ସଜାଇ ବସିଛି ଆସିବ କି ମୋର ଦ୍ୱାରେ
bhanga-kudia-1.roman: Bhaṅgā kuṛiā mo sajāi basichi āsiba ki mora dvāre
bhanga-kudia-1.english: {3:Having decorated }{2:my }{0:broken }{1:hut, }{4:I sit; }{5,6:will you come }{7,8:to my door?}
bhanga-kudia-1.grammarNote: 'mo' is a shortened colloquial genitive pronoun for 'mora'. 'sajāi' is a conjunctive participle dependent on the finite verb 'basichi' (1st person present perfect/continuous). 'āsiba' is 2nd/3rd person future with honorific implied subject.

jhariba-tumara-krupara.grammarNote: 'jhariba' is a 3rd person singular/plural future verb agreeing with the noun 'baraṣā'. 'baraṣā' is a Tadbhava form of Sanskrit 'varṣā'.

jhariba-mo-hruda-agana.source: ଝରିବ ତୁମର କୃପାର ବରଷା ମୋ ହୃଦ ଅଗଣା ପରେ
jhariba-mo-hruda-agana.roman: Jhariba tumara kṛpāra baraṣā mo hṛda agaṇā pare
jhariba-mo-hruda-agana.grammarNote: 'hṛda agaṇā' functions as a Tatpuruṣa or Karmadhāraya compound ('heart-courtyard'). 'pare' is a locative postposition governing 'agaṇā'.

chita-katidei-muruja.source: ଚିତା କାଟିଦେଇ ମୁରୁଜ ପକାଇ ଝୋଟି ପାରିଦେଇ ଗୋବର ଲିପାଇ
chita-katidei-muruja.roman: Citā kāṭidei muruja pakāi jhoṭi pāridei gobara lipāi
chita-katidei-muruja.english: {1:Having drawn }{0:floor-patterns, }{3:scattered }{2:colored powder, }{5:spread }{4:rice-paste art, }{7:and plastered }{6:with cow dung,}
chita-katidei-muruja.grammarNote: A string of conjunctive participles ('kāṭidei', 'pakāi', 'pāridei', 'lipāi') indicating sequential preparatory actions. 'kāṭidei' and 'pāridei' employ the vector verb 'debā' (to give) marking completed action.

words.gloss: having dyed / having colored in devotion

mana-sapha-kari.grammarNote: 'saphā kari' is a conjunct verb with the participle 'kari'. 'raṅgāi' is a conjunctive participle of the causative/denominative verb 'raṅgāibā' (to dye/color).

verse2-1.source: ବାଜେ ରେ ମହୁରୀ ଖୋଳ କରତାଳ ରଣଶିଙ୍ଗା ଭେରୀ ବାଜା
verse2-1.roman: bāje re mahurī khoḷa karatāḷa raṇaśiṅgā bherī bājā
verse2-1.english: {0:There resound, }{1:O, }{2:the reed pipe, }{3:khol, }{4:cymbals, }{5:battle horn, }{6:kettledrum, }{7:and musical instruments!}
verse2-1.grammarNote: 'bāje' is 3rd person present. The subject is an asyndetic list of traditional musical instruments ending in the collective term 'bājā'.

verse3-1.source: ଯୋଗ ସମାଧିରେ ସାଇ ଯୋଗୀରାଜ ଶୋଇଛନ୍ତି ମନ୍ଦିରରେ
verse3-1.roman: yoga samādhire sāi yogīrāja śoichanti mandirare
verse3-1.english: {0:In yoga }{1:samādhi, }{2:Sai, }{3:the king of yogis, }{4:rests }{5:in the temple.}
verse3-1.grammarNote: 'yoga samādhire' forms a compound concept in the locative case -re. 'śoichanti' is honorific present continuous/stative from 'śoibā'.

verse3-2.source: ପ୍ରତିମା ରୂପରେ ବିରାଜିତ ସାଇ ସମାଧି ମନ୍ଦିର ଘରେ
verse3-2.roman: pratimā rūpare birājita sāi samādhi mandira ghare
verse3-2.english: {1:In the form }{0:of a sculpted image, }{3:Sai }{2:sits resplendent }{6:in the chamber }{4:of the samādhi }{5:temple.}

words.gloss: tomb; here Sāī Bābā’s burial shrine

verse3-2.grammarNote: 'pratimā rūpare' uses the locative of guise/form. 'samādhi mandira ghare' is a genitival compound phrase ending in locative -e.

refrain-1.source: ଚାଲ ଶିରିଡ଼ିକୁ ଯିବା ରେ ସଭିଏଁ ସେ ପରା ସାଇଙ୍କ ଘର
refrain-1.roman: cāla siriṛīku jibā re sabhieṁ se parā sāiṅka ghara
refrain-1.grammarNote: Odia cohortative construction where hortative imperative 'cāla' combines with 1st person plural future/cohortative verb 'jibā'. 'siriṛīku' takes the dative/locative inflection -ku. 'sāiṅka' is the honorific genitive in -ṅka.

mote-tume-rakhya-kara-1.source: ମୋତେ ତୁମେ ରକ୍ଷା କର କୃପାସିନ୍ଧୁ ସାଈ, କୃପାସିନ୍ଧୁ ସାଈ
mote-tume-rakhya-kara-1.roman: mote tume rakṣā kara kṛpāsindhu sāī, kṛpāsindhu sāī
mote-tume-rakhya-kara-1.grammarNote: mote is 1st person singular accusative/dative pronoun. tume is 2nd person honorific/familiar subject. rakṣā kara is a conjunct verb in the imperative mood. kṛpāsindhu is a Sanskrit bahuvrīhi/tatpuruṣa compound (kṛpā + sindhu).

smrutira-balire-kete-1.grammarNote: smṛtira is smṛti + -ra (genitive). bālire is bāli (sand) + -re (locative). pādacihna is a tatpuruṣa compound (pāda + cihna). paṛichi is paṛibā (to fall/be placed) in the present perfect.

v1-2.english: {0:Birth}{1: and death}{3: are indeed}{2: the play}{4: of māyā.}

words.gloss: of the power of worldly appearance

v1-2.grammarNote: Janama maraṇa is an asyndetic dvandva compound functioning in apposition to kheḷa. māyāra carries the Odia genitive suffix -ra.

v2-3.english: {0:the Guru}{1: is the favorable}{2: following}{3: wind.}
v2-3.grammarNote: Zero-copula equative sentence with Guru as subject and anukūḷa pachhuā pabana as complex predicate noun phrase.

v3-1.english: {0:A Guru}{1: is not}{2: attained}{3: in every}{4: birth;}

words.gloss: are met; are attained; are found

v3-1.grammarNote: miḷanti is an intransitive mediopassive verb taking honorific third-person agreement with Guru. na is the standard pre-verbal negator.

v3-2.english: {1:the revered Guru}{0: is attained}{2: through the Lord's}{3: grace.}

words.gloss: are met; are attained; are found
of the Lord; of the Master

v3-2.grammarNote: Verb-initial line (Miḷanti) fronted for poetic and contrastive focus. prabhuṅka is the honorific genitive singular.

words.gloss: under the sway of māyā (the delusive power of worldly appearance)

v2-4.grammarNote: 'māyābaśe' is a compound noun in locative/adverbial case ('māyā' + 'baśa' + '-e'); 'bāṭabaṇā' is a predicative adjective with copula/inchoative verb 'hue'.

v1-1.source: ଥରେ ନୁହେଁ କେତେ ଥର ଭୁଲ କରେ ବାରମ୍ବାର
v1-1.roman: thare nuheṁ kete thara bhula kare bārambāra
v1-1.grammarNote: 'thare' is noun 'thara' with locative/adverbial '-e'; 'nuheṁ' is negative copula; 'kare' is habitual present 1st person.

v3-1.source: ବାନ୍ଧିଛି ତୁମକୁ ପ୍ରାଣେ ତଥାପି ଯେ ପାପ ମନେ
v3-1.roman: bāndhichi tumaku prāṇe tathāpi ye pāpa mane
v3-1.english: {0:I hold }{1:You }{0:fast }{2:within my life-breath, }{3,4:yet }{5:sin }{6:remains in my mind.}

words.gloss: in my life-breath / within my soul

v3-1.grammarNote: First clause has transitive verb 'bāndhichi' (1st person present perfect) with object 'tumaku' and locative 'prāṇe'; second clause has locative 'mane' with subject 'pāpa' and an elided existential verb.

refrain-2.grammarNote: Vocative compound phrase 'ānanda ghana' ('compact mass of bliss') preceded by vocative marker 'he'.

v2-1.source: ଆନନ୍ଦ ସିକ୍ତ ଆକାଶେ ଗ୍ରହ ତାରା ଜନ୍ମ
v2-1.roman: ānanda sikta ākāśe graha tārā janma

words.gloss: in the sky; in space; in the ether

v2-1.grammarNote: Nominal sentence without copula. 'ānanda sikta' functions as a participial modifier to the locative noun 'ākāśe'. 'graha tārā' is a coordinate subject compound.

v2-2.source: ହୋ ଆନନ୍ଦ ସିକ୍ତ ଆକାଶେ ଗ୍ରହ ତାରା ଜନ୍ମ
v2-2.roman: ho ānanda sikta ākāśe graha tārā janma

words.gloss: in the sky; in space; in the ether

v2-2.grammarNote: Interjection 'ho' prefixed to the nominal structure of v2-1.

janena-mu-debata-ki.grammarNote: First-person singular present negative verb 'jāṇenā' formed from the verb stem 'jāṇ-' with negative suffix '-nā', followed by 1sg pronoun 'mū̃' and disjunctive interrogative particle 'ki'.

janena-mu-ishwara.english: {0,1:I do not know }{2:if the Supreme Lord,}
janena-mu-ishwara.grammarNote: Repeated 1sg negative clause structure with the Sanskrit loanword 'īśbara' (īśvara) functioning as the predicate noun of the complement clause.

bihuchuna-chakara.grammarNote: Noun adjunct 'biuchuṇā', the sung colloquial form of 'biñcaṇā' (hand-fan), qualifying the agent noun 'cākara'.

words.gloss: power of worldly appearance and entanglement
from the net; from the snare

janamara-maya-jalu.grammarNote: Genitive 'janamara' qualifying the compound 'māyā jāla', which carries the ablative inflection '-u' ('jālu').

verse-1-4.grammarNote: Nominal sentence with postpositive possessive 'mo' attached to subject 'jībana', followed by coordinate predicate adjectives 'byākula adhīra'.

words.gloss: right order, duty, or sustaining principle

dharama-karama-nija-swarthare.grammarNote: Asyndetic compound 'Dharama karama' (semi-tatsama forms of dharma and karma); 'swārthare' has locative/instrumental suffix '-re' expressing purpose/motive.

bhala-manda-kichhi-dekhibe-nahi.grammarNote: Dvandva pair 'Bhala manda' modified by indefinite pronoun 'kichi'; 'dekhibe nāhiṁ' is the standard periphrastic negative future.

papa-gantaghara-sariba-nahi.grammarNote: 'Pāpa gantāghara' is a determinative compound functioning as grammatical subject; 'sariba nāhiṁ' is negative future of intransitive 'saribā' (to be exhausted/finished).

papa-arjane-bharibe-ghara.english: {1:Through the earning }{0:of sin, }{2:they will fill }{3:their house,}
papa-arjane-bharibe-ghara.grammarNote: 'arjane' is instrumental/locative of verbal noun 'arjana' (earning/acquisition); 'bharibe' is 3rd pl. future transitive verb.

refrain-luha-bohi-jae.source: ଲୁହ ବହି ଯାଏ ତୁମ ଶ୍ରୀମୁଖ ଦରଶନେ
refrain-luha-bohi-jae.roman: luha bahi yāē tuma śrīmukha daraśanē
refrain-luha-bohi-jae.english: {0:Tears}{1,2: stream forth}{5: at the sight of}{3: your}{4: holy face}

words.gloss: at the sight of; upon beholding

refrain-luha-bohi-jae.grammarNote: Compound verb `bahi yāē` (conjunctive participle + 3rd person present auxiliary). `daraśanē` is a locative of circumstance / temporal cause (`daraśana` + `-ē`).

refrain-deha-thari-uthe.source: ଦେହ ଥରି ଉଠେ ତୁମ ପାବନ ପରଶେ
refrain-deha-thari-uthe.roman: dēha thari uṭhē tuma pābana paraśē
refrain-deha-thari-uthe.english: {0:The body}{2: starts }{1:trembling}{3: at your}{4: purifying}{5: touch}
refrain-deha-thari-uthe.grammarNote: Ingressive compound verb `thari uṭhē` (`thari` + `uṭhē` 3rd person simple present). `paraśē` is locative of cause (from `paraśa` / Sanskrit `sparśa`).

refrain-antare-jaage-je.source: ଅନ୍ତରେ ଜାଗେ ଯେ କୋହ ଶୁଣି ତୁମ ଗୀତ
refrain-antare-jaage-je.roman: antarē jāgē yē kōha śuṇi tuma gīta
refrain-antare-jaage-je.english: {0:Within,}{3: a choked sob}{1,2: awakens}{4: upon hearing}{5: your}{6: song}
refrain-antare-jaage-je.grammarNote: `śuṇi` is a non-finite conjunctive participle taking `tuma gīta` as its object. `yē` functions as an emphatic or relative connector.

refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.source: ପ୍ରାଣ ପୁଲକିତ ହୁଏ ତୁମ ସାଈ ନାମେ
refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.roman: prāṇa pulakita huē tuma sāī nāmē
refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.english: {0:The life-breath}{1,2: is thrilled}{3: by your}{4: Sai}{5: name}
refrain-prana-pulakita-hue.grammarNote: `pulakita huē` is a predicate adjective construction with copular verb `huē` (3rd person present). `nāmē` is an instrumental/locative of cause.

v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.source: ଭକତି ଯେ ବ୍ୟଥା ଦିଏ ନଥିଲି ମୁଁ ଜାଣି
v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.roman: bhakati yē byathā diē nathilī mū̃ jāṇi
v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.english: {1:That}{0: devotion}{3: gives}{2: pain,}{5: I}{4: did not}{6: know}
v1-bhakati-je-byatha-die.grammarNote: Inverted word order in main clause: negative auxiliary `nathilī` precedes subject `mū̃` and lexical participle `jāṇi` (`nathilī mū̃ jāṇi` for standard `mū̃ jāṇi nathilī`). `yē` introduces the subordinate content clause.

v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.source: ତମକୁ ଲୋଡୁଛି ମୁଁ ଯେ ପ୍ରତି ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତରେ
v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.roman: tamaku lōḍuchi mū̃ yē prati muhūrttarē
v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.english: {2:I}{1: am seeking}{0: you}{3: indeed}{4: at every}{5: moment}
v1-tamaku-loduchhi-mu-je.grammarNote: Inverted word order: Object (`tamaku`) - Verb (`lōḍuchi` 1st person present continuous) - Subject (`mū̃`) - Particle (`yē`). `muhūrttarē` is locative of time.

v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.source: ସ୍ନେହ ପ୍ରେମ ରାଗ ପ୍ରୀତି ସଉରାଗଠୁ ବେଶୀ
v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.roman: snēha prēma rāga prīti saurāgaṭhu bēśī
v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.english: {0:Affection,}{1: love,}{2: passion,}{3: fondness—}{5:more}{4: than passionate yearning}

words.gloss: than passionate yearning; beyond deep love

v1-sneha-prema-raaga-preeti.grammarNote: Asyndetic listing of four terms for love (`snēha`, `prēma`, `rāga`, `prīti`). `saurāgaṭhu` carries the ablative-comparative suffix `-ṭhu` governing `bēśī`.

v1-karunara-bhaba-jhare.english: {1:The feeling}{0: of compassion}{2: streams}{3: from your very}{4: eyes}

words.gloss: in the eyes; from the eyes

v1-karunara-bhaba-jhare.grammarNote: `jharē` is 3rd person simple present. `tumari` has the emphatic clitic `-i`. `nayanē` is a locative noun functioning with ablative/source meaning.

v2-janama-marana-die.grammarNote: Inverted word order: Object dvandva (`janama maraṇa`) - Verb (`diē` 3rd person present) - Subject (`niṣṭhura samaya`).

v2-mo-aatmare-naahi-kintu.source: ମୋ ଆତ୍ମାରେ ନାହିଁ କିନ୍ତୁ ତୁମରି ବିଲୟ
v2-mo-aatmare-naahi-kintu.roman: mō ātmārē nāhī̃ kintu tumari bilaya
v2-mo-aatmare-naahi-kintu.english: {3:But}{0,1: in my soul,}{2: there is no}{5: dissolution}{4: of you}

words.gloss: in the soul; within the self

verse-5-line-1.source: ତୁମରି ସମାଧି ନିକଟେ ଗୁରୁ ହେ ସଭିଏଁ କରନ୍ତି ଆଳି

near / beside / in the presence of (locative)

verse-5-line-1.grammarNote: 'Samādhi' is a preserved Vedantic/devotional term denoting both yogic absorption and the shrine housing the master's physical form. 'Sabhiēṃ' is an all-inclusive collective pronoun with plural verb agreement ('karanti').

refrain-2.source: ଗୋଳାଗି ଲାଗେ ମୁଁ ଚରଣେ ତୁମରି ସାଇ ମୋତେ ରକ୍ଷା କର

refrain-2.grammarNote: 'Gōḷāgi lāgē' functions as a compound verbal predicate of humble salutation. 'Tumari' has the emphatic suffix '-ri' on the second-person genitive base 'tuma'.

verse-1-line-2.source: ସବୁ ଜନମର ପାପ କାଟ ତୁମେ ନିଅ ମୋର ସାଗର ପାର
verse-1-line-2.roman: Sabu janamara pāpa kāṭā tumē nia mōra sāgara pāra
verse-1-line-2.grammarNote: 'Kāṭā' is used here as an imperative form parallel to standard 'kāṭa'. 'Nia ... pāra' is a split verbal phrase equivalent to 'pāra nia' (take across).

verse-2-line-1.source: ନ ହେଲେ ନାହିଁ ଫୁଲ ତୁମ ପାଦେ ତୁମ ପାଦେ ଧୂଳି ହୋଇ

verse-3-line-2.source: ତୁମ ଚରଣର ଧୂଳି ବୋଳି ହୋଇ ପବିତ୍ର ମୁଁ ହୋଇଯାଏ

verse-3-line-2.grammarNote: 'Bōḷi hōi' is a reflexive conjunctive participle ('having smeared upon oneself'). 'Hōiyāē' is a compound verb 'hōi yibā' (to become completely).

verse-6-line-2.source: ମୋ ବେଳକୁ କିଆଁ ଏତେ ଟାଣି ଓଟରା କଠୋର ପ୍ରାଣ ହୋଇଲ

verse-6-line-2.grammarNote: 'Mō bēḷaku' contains genitive pronoun 'mō' + noun 'bēḷa' (time) + dative marker '-ku'. 'Ṭāṇi ōṭara' is an echoic verbal compound functioning adverbially/nominally here.

har-pal-hota.source: हर पल होता जग में परिवर्तन

ha-kuthavara-vedya-ghesi-asara.grammarNote: Rhetorical interrogative clause; 'veḍyā' is vocative masculine singular; 'gheśī' is a 2nd-person singular poetic present/future form.

phir ambe mā̃ kā darśan hogā, āhõ kā inām

v2-lead-2.source: ऐसे रोने से माँ मिल जाए तो जानो सस्ता

v2-lead-2.grammarNote: 'rone' is oblique infinitive used as a gerund after postposition 'se'. 'mil jāe' is 3rd-person singular subjunctive; 'jāno' is familiar 2nd-person imperative.

v2-chorus-2.source: ऐसे रोने से माँ मिल जाए तो जानो सस्ता

v1-l4.source: ओ रह के मस्ती विच दिन-रात सदा, दुनिया तों किनारा पा लैंदा
v1-l4.roman: O rah ke mastī vic din-rāt sadā, dunīyā tõ kinārā pā laindā
v1-l4.english: {0:He, }{1,2:remaining }{3,4,6:ever in ecstasy }{5:day and night, }{9,10,11:withdraws to the shore }{7,8:from the world.}
v1-l4.grammarNote: 'rah ke' is conjunctive participle. 'kinārā pā laindā' combines 'kinārā' (bank/edge) with 'pā laiṇā' idiomatically meaning 'to attain detachment / take distance'.

v1-l4-rep.source: ओ दुनिया तों किनारा पा लैंदा, दुनिया तों किनारा पा लैंदा
v1-l4-rep.roman: O dunīyā tõ kinārā pā laindā, dunīyā tõ kinārā pā laindā

v1-l4-rep.grammarNote: Reduplicated verb phrase 'dunīyā tõ kinārā pā laindā'.

v3-l2.source: एह दिल है अमानत मैया दी, थाँ-थाँ ते लगाया नहीं जांदा

v3-l2.english: {0:This }{1:heart }{2,4,5:is Mother's }{3:sacred trust; }{8,9,10:it cannot be attached }{6,7:at every place.}
v3-l2.grammarNote: 'lagāyā nahī̃ jāndā' is passive of incapacity using the causative stem 'lagāṇā' with auxiliary 'jānā'.

v4-l4.source: इस दुनिया नू असां दिल तों भुला के, इस दिल विच माँ नू वसाना ए
v4-l4.roman: Is dunīyā nū asā̃ dil tõ bhulā ke, is dil vic mā̃ nū vasānā e
v4-l4.grammarNote: 'bhulā ke' is conjunctive participle of the causative verb bhulāṇā; 'vasānā e' is an infinitive with auxiliary forming a prescriptive statement.

v4-l4-rep.source: हो इस दिल विच माँ नू वसाना ए,
v4-l4-rep.roman: Ho is dil vic mā̃ nū vasānā e,

verse-2-ajeeb.grammarNote: Inverted predicate construction where the copula hai and predicate adjective ajīb precede the subject ye māyā.

teri-beeti-umar.source: तेरी बीती उमर हरि नाम बिना
teri-beeti-umar.roman: terī bītī umar hari nām binā

words.gloss: of Hari, a name of Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa, the Lord who removes evil and sin

teri-beeti-umar.grammarNote: bītī is a feminine past participle serving as the finite predicate agreeing with the feminine noun umar.

taise-praani.english: {0:so is }{1:a living being }{4:without }{2,3:the name of Hari.}

words.gloss: a living being; a mortal creature
of Hari, a name of Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa, the Lord who removes evil and sin

taise-praani.grammarNote: taise correlates with jaise. The predicate adjective describing emptiness/destitution is understood from hīnā in the prior line.

jaise-pandit.grammarNote: ved vihīnā is an adjectival compound/phrase (from Sanskrit veda-vihīna) serving as a predicate complement qualifying paṇḍit.

dukh-mein-sumiran.grammarNote: sab functions as a collective singular/plural subject taking the third-person present verb kare (Braj/Old Hindi).

jo-sukh-mein-sumiran.grammarNote: jo introduces the relative-conditional clause with the habitual present/subjunctive verb kare.

sumiran-kar-le.grammarNote: kar le is a compound imperative (stem kar + imperative auxiliary le denoting self-directed action). manā is the vocative of man.

kaam-krodh-mad.source: काम क्रोध मद लोभ निवारो छांडि दे अब संत जना
kaam-krodh-mad.roman: kām krodh mad lobh nivāro chā̃ḍi de ab sant janā
kaam-krodh-mad.grammarNote: kām krodh mad lobh is an asyndetic catalog of the four cardinal vices. nivāro is a 2nd person plural/honorific imperative. chā̃ḍi de is a compound imperative (conjunctive participle chā̃ḍi + auxiliary imperative de).

sumiran-kar-le-part.grammarNote: Truncated reprise of the refrain's verb phrase (sumiran kar le).

refrain-1.grammarNote: kariyo is an archaic/Braj polite precative imperative of karnā. alag functions as a predicative adjective with karnā.

refrain-2.source: चाकर हूँ तेरा जनम जनम का
refrain-2.roman: cākar hū̃ terā janam janam kā
refrain-2.grammarNote: janam janam displays lexical reduplication indicating continuous repetition across lifetimes. kā agrees with masculine singular cākar.

refrain-4.grammarNote: Ellipsis of the explicit vocative sadguru present in refrain-1.

v2-1.source: चातक हूँ तेरे कृपा सावन का
v2-1.roman: cātak hū̃ tere kṛpā sāvan kā
v2-1.english: {1:I am }{0:the cātaka bird }{4,5:of the monsoon }{2:of your }{3:grace,}
v2-1.grammarNote: kṛpā sāvan functions as an appositional/genitive compound ('monsoon of grace') modified by tere, with postposition kā linking to cātak.

rana-jiti-rama-raou-aye.grammarNote: Conjunctive participle 'jīti' modifies the main verb 'āe' (masculine plural used honorifically for Rama). 'rāmarāu' is a compound of 'rāma' + 'rāu' (king/raja).

dharani-dhenu.source: धरनि धेनु महिदेव साधु सब के सब सोच नसाए
dharani-dhenu.roman: dharani dhenu mahideva sādhu saba ke saba soca nasāe
dharani-dhenu.english: {0:of the earth, }{1:the cows, }{2:the Brahmins, }{3:and the ascetics, }{4:all }{7:anxieties }{5,6:without exception }{8:he dispelled.}
dharani-dhenu.grammarNote: Compound list of genitive dependents (dharani, dhenu, mahideva, sādhu) connected by postposition 'ke'. Reduplicated 'saba ke saba' expresses comprehensive totality.

dehi-asisa.grammarNote: 'bhūmisura' is a compound noun (bhūmi + sura); 'dehiṁ' is 3rd person plural present indicative with nasalized ending.

words.gloss: a context-dependent power or condition of worldly appearance

antara-5b.grammarNote: 'janu' introduces the utprekṣā clause. 'jīvahi' is dative/accusative singular. 'māyā' is feminine subject with 'lapaṭānī' as feminine past participle.

shankara-suvana-riddhi-siddhi-nava-nidhi.source: शंकर सुवन रिद्धि सिद्धि नव निधि दाई
shankara-suvana-riddhi-siddhi-nava-nidhi.roman: śaṅkara suvana riddhi siddhi nava nidhi dāī
shankara-suvana-riddhi-siddhi-nava-nidhi.grammarNote: suvana is the tadbhava form of sūnu/savana (son); dāī is the agentive suffix/noun (dāyī) governing the compound direct objects Ṛddhi, Siddhi, and Nava Nidhi.

words.gloss: Tānsen, the poet’s own name as signature

gaan-se-na-teri-stuti.grammarNote: Poet’s signature; 'terī stuti' is the object of 'karata' at the start of the next line.

kaato-kalesha-prathama-vandana.source: करत काटो कलेश प्रथम वंदना करत द्वंद्व मिट जाई
kaato-kalesha-prathama-vandana.roman: karata kāṭo kaleśa prathama vandanā karata dvaṁdva miṭa jāī
kaato-kalesha-prathama-vandana.english: {0:he offers: }{1:cut away }{2:distress. }{5:On offering }{3:the first }{4:salutation, }{6:conflict }{7,8:is wiped away}
kaato-kalesha-prathama-vandana.grammarNote: Compound clause pairing an imperative petition (kāṭo kaleśa) with participial phrases (karata ... karata) and the compound resultative verb miṭa jāī (stem miṭ + auxiliary jānā).

words.gloss: Panchavati (the grove of five banyan trees)

v1-panchavati.grammarNote: pañcavaṭī is a locative proper noun; parana-kuṭī is a tatpuruṣa compound (parna + kuṭī); tara functions as a postposition meaning 'under/beneath'.

words.gloss: to rear; to keep as pet

v2-paye-palibe-joga.grammarNote: pāye is a locative/conditional absolute participle ('upon obtaining'); pālibe is an oblique verbal noun/infinitive governed by joga (Sanskrit yogya).

words.gloss: loving / an intimate companion or kin

verse-1-line-2.grammarNote: Concessive clause introduced by 'jadyapi' (Sanskrit yadyapi) with elided 3sg copula and pronoun.

words.gloss: Viṣṇu's avatāra; husband of Sītā; Rāma means “pleasing” or “delightful”.
Sita; Vaidehī means “princess of Videha”, a name of Sītā.

refrain-1.grammarNote: Relative construction in Brajbhasha with dative/genitive 'jāke' marking the experiencer, paired with compound subject 'Rāma Vaidehī' and omitted copula.

words.gloss: what use is / what good is

verse-2-line-5.grammarNote: Proverbial rhetorical question with interrogative pronoun 'kahā' and relative clause 'ā̃khi jehi phūṭai' qualifying 'añjana'.

words.gloss: should I say / can I speak

verse-2-line-6.grammarNote: First person singular potential/present verb 'kahaũ' with interrogative extent phrase 'kahā̃ laũ'.

verse-3-line-1.source: तुलसी सो सब भाँति परम हित
verse-3-line-1.roman: Tulasī so saba bhā̃ti parama hita
verse-3-line-1.grammarNote: Poet signature 'Tulasī' functioning as discourse marker/speaker attribution, followed by correlative pronoun 'so' with nominal predicate 'parama hita'.

sukha-sampati-mati-sugati.grammarNote: Asyndetic list of feminine/masculine nouns in nominative, qualified by the adjective suhāī (delightful/pleasing).

refrain-jachie-girijapati.grammarNote: Jāciye is an Awadhi passive/impersonal optative/imperative formed on the root jāc- (Sanskrit yāc-). kāsī is locative by context/apposition.

nirakhi-nihala-nimisha-mahu-kinhe.english: {0:having gazed upon them, }{4:He made them }{1:fulfilled }{3:within }{2:the blink of an eye.}

words.gloss: the blink of an eye; an instant

nirakhi-nihala-nimisha-mahu-kinhe.grammarNote: Nirakhi is an absolutive/conjunctive participle. kīnhe is the 3rd person past transitive verb agreeing with the masculine plural object.

lead-tumhi-to-meri-bigdi-sanware.grammarNote: Tumhīṁ to (emphatic subject); merī bigṛī (fem. past participle of bigaṛnā functioning as substantive noun 'ruined condition'); saṁvāre (3sg present/habitual/optative of saṁvārnā 'to mend/embellish').

lead-tumhi-to-maa-mere-kaaj.source: तुम्हीं तो माँ मेरे काज सँवारे
lead-tumhi-to-maa-mere-kaaj.roman: Tumhīṁ to māṁ mere kāj saṁvāre
lead-tumhi-to-maa-mere-kaaj.grammarNote: kāj (tadbhav of kārya, masc. plural direct object); mere kāj (masc. pl. possessive + noun); saṁvāre (3sg/pl verbal form).

saagar-manthan.grammarNote: Nominal compound sāgara manthana in genitive relation to pratiphala, which takes the ablative/causal postposition sē.

koodarai-vellum-seer-govinda-undannai.english: {3:O }{2:glorious }{3:Govinda, }{1:you who conquer }{0:those who do not submit—}{4:of you yourself}

words.gloss: those who do not submit [enemies / dissenting ones]
O Govinda, finder of cattle; Kṛṣṇa, protector of cattle and living beings
you yourself, the object of the following singing

koodarai-vellum-seer-govinda-undannai.grammarNote: 'Undaṉṉai' is the 2nd person singular accusative form with reflexive-emphatic suffix (un + tannai), serving as the direct object of the following action.

soodagame-thol-valaiye.source: சூடகமே தோள் வளையே தோடே செவிப் பூவே
soodagame-thol-valaiye.grammarNote: A series of coordinate nouns marked with the coordinating clitic '-ē'. 'Tōḷ vaḷai' is a compound (tōḷ + vaḷai). 'Sevippūvē' is a compound of 'sevi' (ear) + 'pū' (flower-shaped jewel) + clitic '-ē'.

koodi-irundhu-kulirndhelor.english: {0:together} {1:we will sit} {2:cooled and refreshed—heed this,} {3:O our maiden.}

words.gloss: being cooled and refreshed; ēlōr is the refrain exhortation, rendered “heed this”
O our maiden [O young girl / our lady]

koodi-irundhu-kulirndhelor.grammarNote: Kūṭi iruntu kuḷirntu links coming together, sitting or remaining, and becoming cooled/refreshed. English supplies the first-person-plural future from the preceding promises to wear ornaments and garments. Ēlōr empāvāy is the recurring refrain exhortation.

margazhi-thingal-mathi.english: {4:On this auspicious day} {2,3:when the moon is full,} {1:in the month} {0:of Mārgaḻi,}

words.gloss: of Mārgaḻi (the ninth solar month, Dec–Jan)

margazhi-thingal-mathi.grammarNote: Mārkaḻit tiṅkaḷ names the month; the final -t is sandhi before tiṅkaḷ, not an independent genitive suffix. Mati niṟainta describes the moon as full. Nannāḷ combines nan (good or auspicious) with nāḷ (day); the whole phrase sets the auspicious occasion.

neerada-poduveer.english: {3:O maidens adorned with fine jewels,} {1:you who will go} {0:to bathe,} {2:step forth!}

words.gloss: you who intend to go / set out
O women adorned with fine jewelry

neerada-poduveer.grammarNote: nīrāṭap is an infinitive with sandhi stop doubling (-p); pōtuvīr is a participatory noun/future second-person plural form ('you who will go'); pōtumiṉō is an archaic polite plural imperative with vocative/emphatic particle -ō; nēriḻaiyīr is a vocative compound noun (nēr + iḻai + īr).

seermalgum-aaypadi-aalaap.english: {1:In the cowherd settlement} {0:overflowing with prosperity,} {2,3:ah... ah...}
seermalgum-aaypadi-aalaap.grammarNote: sīrmalkum is a relative participle compound (sīr + malkum) modifying āyppāṭi (compound of āy 'cowherd' + pāṭi 'village/settlement'); ā... represents vocal raga elongation without separate lexical meaning.

seermalgum-aaypadi-selva.english: {2:O cherished} {3:young maidens} {1:of the cowherd settlement} {0:overflowing with prosperity,}

words.gloss: of the cowherd settlement of Gokula

seermalgum-aaypadi-selva.grammarNote: āyppāṭic and celvac carry sandhi stop doubling (-c); ciṟumīrkāḷ is a double plural/honorific vocative formed from ciṟumīr (young girls) + plural vocative suffix -kāḷ.

koorvel-kodunthozhilan.english: {3:The young son} {2:of Nandagopa,} {0:the sharp-spear bearer} {1:of fierce deeds,}

words.gloss: one of fierce deeds; here the vigilant protector Nandagopa
of Nandagopa (Kṛṣṇa's foster father and chieftain)

koorvel-kodunthozhilan.grammarNote: kūrvēl is an adjectival compound (kūr + vēl); koṭuntoḻilaṉ is a masculine appellative noun (koṭu-toḻil-aṉ) in apposition to nantakōpaṉ; nantakōpaṉ stands in genitive relation to kumaraṉ.

eraandha-kanni-yasodhai.english: {3:the young} {4:lion} {2:of Yaśodā,} {1:whose eyes} {0:are full of beauty,}

words.gloss: she who has eyes; here, the beautiful-eyed mother

eraandha-kanni-yasodhai.grammarNote: ērārnta is a relative past participle (ēr 'beauty/grace' + ārnta 'filled with') modifying kaṇṇi (feminine noun 'one with eyes'); yaśōtai stands in genitive relation to the metaphoric compound iḷam siṅkam (young lion).

words.gloss: she who has eyes; here, the beautiful-eyed mother

eraandha-kanni.grammarNote: A partial-line vocal pickup repeating the adjectival phrase ērārnta kaṇṇi from line 6.

kaarmeni-sengan.english: {0:he whose body is dark as a raincloud,} {1:whose eyes are red,} {4:and whose face is} {3:like} {2:the sun and the moon,}

words.gloss: the radiant sun and the moon

kaarmeni-sengan.grammarNote: kārmēṉic is a bahuvrīhi-like adjectival compound (kār 'dark cloud' + mēṉi 'body' + sandhi -c); ceṅkaṇ (cem 'red' + kaṇ 'eye'); katirmatiyam is a dvandva compound (katir 'sun' + matiyam 'moon') governed by the comparative particle pōl; mukattāṉ is a masculine appellative noun ('he of the face').

words.gloss: Nārāyaṇa (the supreme Lord Viṣṇu) alone; Nārāyaṇa is the refuge of living beings and rests upon the primordial waters

narayanane-namakku-aalaap.grammarNote: nārāyaṇaṉē carries the emphatic clitic -ē ('Nārāyaṇa alone'); namakkē is the dative plural pronoun (namakku) with emphatic clitic -ē ('unto us alone'); ā... denotes raga alapana without lexical content.

words.gloss: Nārāyaṇa (the supreme Lord Viṣṇu) alone; Nārāyaṇa is the refuge of living beings and rests upon the primordial waters
the drum used in the vow observance

narayanane-namakke-parai.grammarNote: taruvāṉ is a third-person masculine singular future finite verb from root taru ('to give'); paṟai is an accusative direct object without overt case marker.

paror-pugazha.english: {2:Let us bathe,} {0:so that the people of the world} {1:may praise us—}{2:heed this,} {3:O our maiden.}

words.gloss: the people of this earth / the whole world
let us bathe; ēlōr is the refrain exhortation, rendered “heed this”

paror-pugazha.grammarNote: Paṭintu is the bathing/immersion participle, understood with the opening invitation. Pārōr pukaḻa gives its purpose or attendant approval. Ēlōr empāvāy is the recurring choral exhortation; here rendered “heed this, O our maiden,” rather than treating each refrain syllable as an additional event.

words.gloss: of Mārgaḻi (the ninth solar month, Dec–Jan)

margazhi-thingal-closing.grammarNote: Repetition of the opening two words of line 1 as a concluding refrain marker, showing genitive sandhi doubling (-t).

line-paluke-short.grammarNote: The noun paluku takes the emphatic particle -ē; baṅgāramāyenā is a sandhi fusion of baṅgāramu (gold), the past tense third-person neuter verb āyenu (became), and the interrogative clitic -ā.

line-kodanda-paluke.english: {0:O wielder of the bow Kodaṇḍa, }{1:have your very words }{2:become gold?}

words.gloss: one who holds the bow Kodaṇḍa in hand

line-kodanda-paluke.grammarNote: kōdaṇḍapāṇi is a bahuvrīhi compound (kōdaṇḍa + pāṇi) functioning as a direct vocative.

line-paluke-kodanda-paluke.english: {0:Have your very words }{1:become gold? }{2:O wielder of the bow Kodaṇḍa, }{3:have your very words }{4:become gold?}

words.gloss: one who holds the bow Kodaṇḍa in hand

line-paluke-kodanda-paluke.grammarNote: Compound line consisting of two identical refrain units flanking a vocative epithet.

line-pilichina.english: {0:Your very words }{1:have become gold; }{2:even when I call you, }{3:why do you not speak?}

words.gloss: even when I call you (concessive participle; speaker and addressee from context)

line-pilichina.grammarNote: baṅgāramāye is declarative past (baṅgāramu + āye); pilicinā is a concessive past verbal participle from pilucu; palukavēmi fuses the second-person singular negative habitual verb palukavu with the interrogative pronoun ēmi.

line-kalalo.source: కలలో నీ నామస్మరణ మరువ చక్కని తండ్రి పలుకే బంగారమాయెనా
line-kalalo.roman: kalalō nī nāmasmaraṇa maruva cakkani taṇḍri palukē baṅgāramāyenā
line-kalalo.english: {0:Even in dreams, }{3:I do not forget }{2:to remember }{1:your }{2:name, }{4:lovely }{5:Father; }{6:have your very words }{7:become gold?}

words.gloss: remembering the name; remembrance of the name
I do not forget (contracted first-person negative, maruvanu)

line-kalalo.grammarNote: kalalō is the locative of kala (dream); nāmasmaraṇa is a compound of nāma (name) and smaraṇa (remembrance). In this direct address, maruva is the contracted first-person negative maruvanu, “I do not forget”: Telugu permits omission of the personal termination nu. The negative participle instead ends in -ka; maruva here supplies a finite statement by the devotee.

line-iravuga.english: {4:For the devotion }{3:of the squirrel }{2:that rolled }{0:fittingly }{1:in the sand,}
line-iravuga.grammarNote: poralina is a past relative participle qualifying uḍuta; yuḍuta shows y- glide euphonic insertion before uḍuta; bhaktiki is dative singular of bhakti.

line-karuninchi-brochiti.source: కరుణించి బ్రోచితివని నెరనమ్మితిని తండ్రి పలుకే బంగారమాయెనా
line-karuninchi-brochiti.roman: karuṇiñci brōcitivani neranammitini taṇḍri palukē baṅgāramāyenā
line-karuninchi-brochiti.english: {0:you showed compassion }{1:and protected it—}{2:I fully believed }{1:this, }{3:Father; }{4:have your very words }{5:become gold?}
line-karuninchi-brochiti.grammarNote: brōcitivani is a sandhi compound of second-person singular past verb brōcitivi (you protected) and quotative particle ani; neranammitini consists of intensive prefix/adverb nera (complete/full) and first-person singular past verb nammitini (I trusted/believed).

line-enta-vedina.english: {0:However much }{1:I plead, }{2:not even a little }{3:mercy comes;}
line-enta-vedina.grammarNote: vēḍinagāni is concessive (vēḍina + gāni); suntaina combines sunta (a tiny amount) with concessive/inclusive clitic -aina; dayarādu combines noun daya with 3rd person neuter negative verb rādu (from vaccu).

line-pantamu-seya.source: పంతము సేయ నేనెంతటి వాడను తండ్రి పలుకే బంగారమాయెనా
line-pantamu-seya.roman: pantamu sēya nēnentaṭi vāḍanu taṇḍri palukē baṅgāramāyenā
line-pantamu-seya.english: {2,3:Who am I, }{4:Father, }{1:for you to }{0:be so obstinate with me? }{5:Have your very words }{6:become gold?}

words.gloss: to do; here, to persist in such contention

line-pantamu-seya.grammarNote: sēya is the infinitive of sēyu; nēnentaṭi fuses first-person pronoun nēnu with the quantitative adjective entaṭi; vāḍanu is a first-person singular pronominalized masculine noun (vāḍu + -anu).

line-sharanagata.english: {4:Do you not }{3:bear} {2:the title }{1:“Protector of }{0:those who seek refuge”}?

words.gloss: you bear; you are marked by: aṅkituḍavu

line-sharanagata.grammarNote: śaraṇāgata is a compound (śaraṇa + āgata); birudāṅkituḍavu is a second-person masculine nominalized adjective (biruda + aṅkita + -uḍavu); kāvā is the negative 2nd person singular verb kāvu with interrogative clitic -ā.

line-karuninchu-bhadrachala.source: కరుణించు భద్రాచల వర రామదాస పోష పలుకే బంగారమాయెనా
line-karuninchu-bhadrachala.roman: karuṇiñcu bhadrācala vara rāmadāsa pōṣa palukē baṅgāramāyenā
line-karuninchu-bhadrachala.english: {0:Show compassion, }{2:O supreme one }{1:of Bhadrācala, }{4:nurturer }{3:of Rāmadāsa! }{5:Have your very words }{6:become gold?}
line-karuninchu-bhadrachala.grammarNote: karuṇiñcu is a direct second-person imperative; bhadrācala vara rāmadāsa pōṣa is a vocative compound sequence ending in the agentive noun pōṣa (nourisher/protector).

v1-3.english: {1:Saying you are }{0:the thief, }{2:the women }{3:are swelling with delight!}

words.gloss: are swelling with delight; are exulting

v1-3.grammarNote: nīvani is sandhi of pronoun nīvu ('you') + quotative complementizer ani ('saying that'). poṅgucunnārā has the present continuous finite form poṅgucunnāru + lengthened metre marker -ā.

v2-3.english: {0:you, }{3:taking charge of }{1:the city of Mathurā }{2:to rule it,}

words.gloss: to govern; to rule over and protect
having taken into hand; having undertaken charge of

v2-3.grammarNote: nēla is the infinitive ēla ('to rule/protect') with n-sandhi. jēpaṭṭi is the conjunctive participle of cēpaṭṭu with c -> j softening.

words.gloss: sacred little hall of consciousness at Chidambaram

invocation-tiruchitrambalam.grammarNote: Compound proper noun / holy acclamation: tiru (sacred) + ciṟu (subtle/little) + ampalam (hall/open space).

v1-l1.source: வேயுறு தோளி பங்கன் விடமுண்ட கண்டன் மிகநல்ல வீணை தடவி
v1-l1.roman: vēyuṟu tōḷi paṅkaṉ viṭamuṇṭa kaṇṭaṉ mikanalla vīṇai taṭavi
v1-l1.english: {2:He who has as His half}{1: the woman whose shoulders}{0: resemble bamboo,}{3,4: the One whose throat swallowed poison,}{7: strumming}{5: the exceedingly sweet}{6: lute,}

words.gloss: He who shares His half with

v1-l1.grammarNote: Participial clause: vēyuṟu (vēy + uṟu), tōḷi (fem. noun), paṅkaṉ (masc. appellative noun), viṭam-uṇṭa (relative participle), kaṇṭaṉ (appellative), taṭavi (adverbial participle).

v1-l2.source: மாசறு திங்கள் கங்கை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v1-l2.roman: mācaṟu tiṅkaḷ kaṅkai muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v1-l2.english: {4:having adorned}{3: His crown with}{0: the spotless}{1: moon}{2: and Gaṅgā,}{6: entered}{4: into my}{5: heart;}{7: therefore,}
v1-l2.grammarNote: Sandhi splitting across whitespace tokens: muṭimēl split as muṭimē + laṇinteṉ (l + aṇintu + eṉ). Causal postposition ataṉāl links this entry to the following consequences within the stanza. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v1-l3.source: ஞாயிறு திங்கள் செவ்வாய் புதன் வியாழன் வெள்ளி சனி பாம்பிரண்டும் உடனே
v1-l3.roman: ñāyiṟu tiṅkaḷ cevvāy putaṉ viyāḻaṉ veḷḷi caṉi pāmpiraṇṭum uṭaṉē
v1-l3.english: {0:Sun,}{1: Moon,}{2: Mars,}{3: Mercury,}{4: Jupiter,}{5: Venus,}{6: Saturn,}{7: and both serpents}{8: together}
v1-l3.grammarNote: List of planetary deities ending in pāmpiraṇṭum (pāmpu + iraṇṭu + um) and adverbial clitic uṭaṉē.

v1-l4.source: ஆசறு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே

v1-l4.grammarNote: Reduplicated adjectives nalla nalla for superlative emphasis. Sandhi split across whitespace: aṭiyā + ravarkku (aṭiyār + avarkku, dative plural).

v2-l1.source: என்பொடு கொம்பொடாமை இவை மார்பிலங்க எருதேறி ஏழையுடனே
v2-l1.roman: eṉpoṭu kompoṭāmai ivai mārpilaṅka erutēṟi ēḻaiyuṭaṉē

v2-l1.grammarNote: kompoṭāmai = kompu + oṭu + āmai; mārpilaṅka = mārpu + ilaṅka (infinitive used adverbially); erutēṟi = erutu + ēṟi (adverbial participle).

v2-l2.source: பொன்பொதி மத்தமாலை புனல்சூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v2-l2.roman: poṉpoti mattamālai puṉalcūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v2-l2.english: {2:wearing}{1: a garland of datura flowers}{0: with gold within}{2: and the waters,}{3: He came}{5: and entered}{3: into my}{4: heart;}{6: therefore,}

words.gloss: containing gold; said of the flowers’ golden interiors

v2-l2.grammarNote: poṉpoti combines poṉ (gold) and poti (contain, enclose), describing the datura flowers. The image is gold within the flowers; pollen is not named. puṉalcūṭi = puṉal + cūṭi; vanteṉ = vantu + eṉ. The final causal phrase links to the following stanza predicate. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v2-l3.source: ஒன்பதொ டொன்றொடேழு பதினெட்டொடாறும் உடனாய நாள்க ளவைதாம்
v2-l3.roman: oṉpato ṭoṉṟoṭēḻu patiṉeṭṭoṭāṟum uṭaṉāya nāḷka ḷavaitām
v2-l3.english: {7:those}{6: asterisms}{7: themselves—}{0:the ninth,}{1: the tenth}{2: and sixteenth,}{3: the eighteenth}{4: and sixth,}{5: and those associated with them—}

words.gloss: the ninth asterism, with the following numbered ones
one: nine plus one, the tenth asterism (oṉṟu + oṭu, “with”)
seven: nine plus seven, the sixteenth asterism (ēḻu)
those accompanying or associated with them
those themselves; initial ḷ completes the preceding plural noun

v2-l3.grammarNote: The numeral construction names stellar positions, rather than a total: nine, nine plus one, nine plus seven, eighteen and six. The base nine is understood again with one and seven. uṭaṉāya describes the associated ones. nāḷkaḷ is split across nāḷka + ḷavaitām, the latter continuing with avai + tām (those themselves). The following row supplies the predicate.

v2-l4.source: அன்பொடு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v2-l4.roman: aṉpoṭu nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v2-l4.english: {0:are lovingly}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v2-l4.grammarNote: Sociative noun aṉpoṭu (aṉpu + oṭu) functioning adverbially; reduplicated adjectives nalla nalla; sandhi split aṭiyā + ravarkku.

v2-extra.grammarNote: Refrain phrase: nalla + aṭiyār-avarkku + mikavē. The performance repeats this complete phrase twice.

v3-l1.roman: uruvaḷar pavaḷamēṉi oḷinīṟaṇintu umaiyōṭum veḷḷai viṭaimēl
v3-l1.english: {1:His coral body}{0: radiant in form,}{2: smeared with glowing sacred ash,}{3: together with Umā}{4: upon the white}{5: bull,}
v3-l1.grammarNote: uruvaḷar (uru + vaḷar), pavaḷamēṉi (pavaḷam + mēṉi), oḷinīṟaṇintu (oḷi + nīṟu + aṇintu, adverbial participle), umaiyōṭum (sociative with -um), viṭaimēl (viṭai + postposition mēl).

v3-l2.grammarNote: murukalar = muruku (fragrance) + alar (blossoming); muṭimēl split across tokens as muṭimē + laṇinteṉ (l + aṇintu + eṉ).

v3-l3.source: திருமகள் கலையதூர்தி செயமாது பூமி திசை தெய்வமான பலவும்

words.gloss: she whose mount is the stag (Durgā)
being deities / the presiding deities of

v3-l3.grammarNote: kalaiyatūrti (stag as vehicle) and ceyamātu (goddess of victory) are read together as two descriptions of Durgā, not two separately introduced goddesses. teyvamāṉa = teyvam + āṉa; palavum is inclusive plural.

v3-l4.source: அருநெதி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v3-l4.roman: aruneti nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v3-l4.english: {0:like precious wealth, are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}

words.gloss: rare, precious wealth; here an image of their benefit

v3-l4.grammarNote: aruneti combines aru (rare, precious) with neti/niti (wealth, treasure), placing the preceding deities in the image of precious wealth. English makes the implied comparison explicit with ‘like’; it does not add a separate boon or another deity to the list. The repeated nalla predicates their goodness; aṭiyā + ravarkku represents aṭiyār + avarkku (for the devotees).

v4-l1.source: மதிநுதன் மங்கையோடு வடாலிருந்து மறையோதும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v4-l1.roman: matinutaṉ maṅkaiyōṭu vaṭāliruntu maṟaiyōtum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ

v4-l2.source: நதியொடு கொன்றைமாலை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்

v4-l2.grammarNote: natiyoṭu (nati + oṭu); muṭimēl split across sandhi as muṭimē + laṇinteṉ (l + aṇintu + eṉ).

v4-l3.source: கொதியுறு காலன் அங்கி நமனோடு தூதர் கொடுநோய்க ளான பலவும்

v4-l4.source: அதிகுணம் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v4-l4.roman: atikuṇam nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē

v4-l4.grammarNote: atikuṇam = ati (supreme/exceeding) + kuṇam (guṇa / beneficial quality); sandhi split aṭiyā + ravarkku.

v5-l1.source: நஞ்சணி கண்டன் எந்தை மடவாள் தனோடும் விடையேறும் எங்கள் பரமன்

v5-l1.english: {2:Our Father}{6,7: and Supreme Lord,}{1: whose throat}{0: is adorned with poison,}{5: who mounts the bull}{4: along with}{3: the gentle maiden,}
v5-l1.grammarNote: nañjaṇi = nañju + aṇi; entai = eṉ + tantai (my/our father); maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum (maṭavāḷ + taṉ + oṭu + um); viṭaiyēṟum = viṭai + ēṟum (relative participle).

v5-l2.source: துஞ்சிருள் வன்னி கொன்றை முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v5-l2.roman: tuñjiruḷ vaṉṉi koṉṟai muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v5-l2.english: {4:having adorned}{3: His crown with}{1: Indian mesquite}{2: and golden shower blossoms,}{6: entered}{4: my}{5: heart}{0: in the darkness of sleep;}{7: therefore,}

words.gloss: the darkness of sleep; here the time of His entry

v5-l2.grammarNote: tuñjiruḷ combines tuñcu (sleep) and iruḷ (darkness), read here as the time of His entry into the heart. Another possible construction relates abiding darkness to the adjacent tree; tuñcu can mean both sleep and abide. muṭimē laṇinteṉ represents muṭimēl + aṇintu + eṉ.

v5-l3.source: வெஞ்சின அவுணரோடும் உருமிடியும் மின்னும் மிகையான பூதமவையும்
v5-l3.roman: veñciṉa avuṇarōṭum urumiṭiyum miṉṉum mikaiyāṉa pūtamavaiyum

words.gloss: those elemental spirits / beings as well

v5-l3.grammarNote: avuṇarōṭum contains associative suffix -ōṭu and connective -um; urumiṭiyum, miṉṉum, and pūtamavaiyum have coordinating conjunctive -um; pūtamavaiyum combines pūtam + avai + um.

v5-l4.source: அஞ்சிடும் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v5-l4.roman: añciṭum nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē

words.gloss: will be filled with dread / will fear

v5-l4.grammarNote: añciṭum is future/habitual 3rd person neuter plural verb; aṭiyā ravarkku represents sandhi split of aṭiyār + avarkku (dative plural); nalla nalla is an aṭukku-t-toṭar (intensive reduplication).

v6-l1.source: வாள்வரி யதளதாடை வரி கோவணத்தர் மடவாள் தனோடும் உடனாய்
v6-l1.roman: vāḷvari yataḷatāṭai vari kōvaṇattar maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum uṭaṉāy
v6-l1.english: {0:Clad in radiant-striped }{1:skin as His garment, }{3:the wearer of a }{2:bound }{3:loincloth, }{6:united together }{5:with }{4:the tender woman,}

words.gloss: skin of that as His garment
the one who wears a loincloth

v6-l1.grammarNote: yataḷatāṭai contains glide y + ataḷatu (skin) + āṭai (garment); kōvaṇattar is a pronominal noun (3rd person honorific masculine); taṉōṭum contains reflexive singular taṉ + associative ōṭu + connective um.

v6-l2.source: நாண்மலர் வன்னி கொன்றை நதிசூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v6-l2.roman: nāṇmalar vaṉṉi koṉṟai naticūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v6-l2.english: {3:wearing }{0:fresh blossoms, }{1:Indian mesquite, }{2:golden shower, }{3:and the river, }{4:came }{6:and entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v6-l2.grammarNote: nāṇmalar is sandhi of nāḷ (fresh/day) + malar (flower); vanteṉ is vantu (verbal participle) + eṉ (oblique 1st person singular 'my'); ataṉāl is instrumental ablative causal connective ('on account of that').

v6-l3.source: கோளரி யுழுவையோடு கொலையானை கேழல் கொடுநாக மோடு கரடி
v6-l3.roman: kōḷari yuḻuvaiyōṭu kolaiyāṉai kēḻal koṭunāka mōṭu karaṭi
v6-l3.english: {0:the predatory lion }{1:along with the tiger, }{2:the murderous elephant, }{3:the wild boar, }{5:along with }{4:the deadly serpent, }{6:and the bear,}
v6-l3.grammarNote: yuḻuvaiyōṭu includes inserted glide y and associative suffix -ōṭu; mōṭu represents sandhi of -m (from koṭunākam) + ōṭu.

v6-l4.source: ஆளரி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v6-l4.roman: āḷari nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v6-l4.grammarNote: aṭiyā ravarkku is the split surface form of aṭiyār + avarkku (dative plural); avai is 3rd person neuter plural pronoun standing for all wild animals.

v7-l1.source: செப்பிள முலைநன்மங்கை ஒருபாக மாக விடையேறு செல்வனடைவார்
v7-l1.roman: ceppiḷa mulaiṉaṉmaṅkai orupāka māka viṭaiyēṟu celvaṉaṭaivār
v7-l1.english: With the {3:noble maiden }of {1:youthful }{0:cup-like }{2:breasts }{6:as }{4:one }{5:half, }{9:the prosperous Lord }{8:who mounts }{7:the bull}{10:—reached by}

words.gloss: reaching or settling upon Him (continuing with the waters in the next line)

v7-l1.grammarNote: The surface celvaṉaṭaivār spans celvaṉ and aṭaivu ār. The latter continues into the following line and describes the waters reaching or settling upon the Lord; it does not introduce devotees as an agent. The cup-like youthful breasts belong to the noble maiden, who is His half.

v7-l2.source: ஒப்பிள மதியும் அப்பும் முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v7-l2.roman: oppiḷa matiyum appum muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v7-l2.english: {2:the waters—}{4:wearing them, }with the {0:peerless young }{1:moon, }{3:upon His crown, }{6:entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v7-l2.grammarNote: oppiḷa = oppu (comparison/equal) + il (without) + a / iḷa (young); muṭimē laṇinteṉ represents muṭimēl (locative 'upon the crown') + aṇintu (adorned) + eṉ (my).

v7-l3.source: வெப்பொடு குளிரும் வாதம் மிகையான பித்தும் வினையான வந்து நலியா
v7-l3.roman: veppoṭu kuḷirum vātam mikaiyāṉa pittum viṉaiyāṉa vantu naliyā
v7-l3.english: {0:fever along with }{1:chills, }{2:wind-humor afflictions, }{3:excessive }{4:bile-humor afflictions, }{5:and distresses born of deeds }{7:will not }{6:come }{7:and cause harm;}

words.gloss: those born of past deeds / karmic distresses
will not afflict; will not cause harm

v7-l3.grammarNote: naliyā is a negative 3rd person neuter plural verb from root nali (to torment/crush); viṉaiyāṉa is an adjectival/pronominal appellative form referring to deeds/consequences.

v7-l4.source: அப்படி நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v7-l4.roman: appaṭi nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v7-l4.english: {0:thus they are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v7-l4.grammarNote: appaṭi functions as an adverbial connective of manner ('just so / likewise'); aṭiyā ravarkku is sandhi-split aṭiyār + avarkku.

v8-l1.source: வேள்பட விழிசெய் தன்று விடைமே லிருந்து மடவாள் தனோடும் உடனாய்
v8-l1.roman: vēḷpaṭa viḻicey taṉṟu viṭaimē liruntu maṭavāḷ taṉōṭum uṭaṉāy
v8-l1.english: {1:Having opened His eye }{2:on that day }{0:so that Kāma would perish, }{4:seated }{3:upon the bull }{7:together }{6:with }{5:the tender woman,}

words.gloss: for Kāma (the god of desire) to perish / fall

v8-l1.grammarNote: vēḷpaṭa is an infinitive of purpose/result (vēḷ + paṭa); viḻiceytaṉṟu is split into viḻicey + taṉṟu (ta- inserted before aṉṟu); viṭaimē liruntu is sandhi of viṭaimēl + iruntu.

v8-l2.source: வாண்மதி வன்னி கொன்றை மலர்சூடி வந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v8-l2.roman: vāṇmati vaṉṉi koṉṟai malarcūṭi vanteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v8-l2.english: {3:wearing }{0:the radiant moon, }{1:Indian mesquite, }{2:and golden shower }{3:blossoms, }{4:He came }{6:and entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v8-l2.grammarNote: vāṇmati combines vāḷ (bright) + mati (moon); malarcūṭi is compound of malar (flower) + cūṭi (verbal participle 'having worn').

v8-l3.source: ஏழ்கடல் சூழிலங்கை அரையன்த னோடும் இடரான வந்து நலியா
v8-l3.roman: ēḻkaṭal cūḻilaṅkai araiyaṉta ṉōṭum iṭarāṉa vantu naliyā
v8-l3.english: {2:the king }{1:of Laṅkā }{1:surrounded by }{0:seven oceans }{3:along with }{4:all distresses }{6:will not }{5:come }{6:and cause harm;}

words.gloss: will not afflict; will not cause harm

v8-l3.grammarNote: ēḻkaṭal combines ēḻu (seven) + kaṭal (sea); araiyanta ṉōṭum represents araiyan (king) + oblique -ta- + associative -ōṭu + connective -um.

v8-l4.source: ஆழ்கடல் நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v8-l4.roman: āḻkaṭal nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v8-l4.grammarNote: āḻkaṭal is a viṉait-tokai compound from āḻ (to sink/be deep) + kaṭal (ocean); aṭiyā ravarkku is sandhi-split aṭiyār + avarkku.

v9-l1.source: பலபல வேட மாகும் பரனாரி பாகன் பசுவேறும் எங்கள் பரமன்
v9-l1.roman: palapala vēṭa mākum paraṉāri pākaṉ pacuvēṟum eṅkaḷ paramaṉ
v9-l1.english: {3:The Supreme One,}{2: assuming}{0: manifold}{1: guises,}{4: having}{3: the woman}{4: as His half,}{6: our}{7: Supreme Lord}{5: who rides the bull,}

words.gloss: the Supreme One; the woman (in nāri-pākaṉ, woman-as-half)
one who has as His half

v9-l1.grammarNote: palapala is intensive reduplication of pala (many); vēṭa mākum combines vēṭam + ākum (relative participle); pacuvēṟum is pacu (bull) + ēṟum (mounting).

v9-l2.source: சலமக ளோடு எருக்கு முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v9-l2.roman: calamaka ḷōṭu erukku muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v9-l2.english: {4:wearing }{3:upon His crown }{0:the daughter of the waters }{1:along with }{2:crown flowers, }{6:entered }{4:my }{5:very heart; }{7:therefore,}
v9-l2.grammarNote: calamaka ḷōṭu represents calamakaḷ (calam 'water' + makaḷ 'daughter') + associative suffix -ōṭu; muṭimē laṇinteṉ is sandhi for muṭimēl + aṇintu + eṉ.

v9-l3.source: மலர்மிசை யோனும் மாலும் மறையோடு தேவர் வருகால மான பலவும்
v9-l3.roman: malarmicai yōṉum mālum maṟaiyōṭu tēvar varukāla māṉa palavum
v9-l3.english: {1:He }{0:upon the lotus }{1:and }{2:Viṣṇu, }{3:along with }{3:the Vedas, }{4:the gods, }{7:and all the manifold things }{6:that constitute }{5:the future,}

words.gloss: Māl, the Great One, Viṣṇu, also
all the manifold entities as well

v9-l3.grammarNote: malarmicai yōṉum is sandhi for malarmicaiyōṉ (pronominal noun: 'he who is on the flower', Brahmā) + -um; mālum has connective -um; varukāla māṉa combines varukālam + āṉa.

v9-l4.source: அலைகடல் மேரு நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v9-l4.roman: alaikaṭal mēru nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v9-l4.grammarNote: alaikaṭal is a viṉait-tokai (alai 'surge/wave' + kaṭal 'sea'); aṭiyā ravarkku represents aṭiyār + avarkku.

v9-extra.source: அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v9-extra.roman: aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v9-extra.english: {0,1:For His devotees, }they are {3:good, }{4:good—}{2:exceedingly so; }{5,6:for His devotees, }they are {8:good, }{9:good—}{7:exceedingly so; }{10,11:for His devotees—}{12:exceedingly so!}
v9-extra.grammarNote: Consists of three repeated cycles of the refrain formula aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla.

v10-l1.source: கொத்தலர் குழலி யோடு விசயற்கு நல்கு குணமாய வேட விகிர்தன்
v10-l1.roman: kottalar kuḻali yōṭu vicayaṟku nalku kuṇamāya vēṭa vikirtaṉ
v10-l1.english: {2:Along with }{1:Her of }{0:blossoming flower-cluster }{1:tresses, }{7:the Transcendent Lord of varied forms }who in {5:gracious }{6:hunter }{6:guise }{4:bestowed grace }{3:upon Arjuna,}

words.gloss: the Transcendent Lord of varied forms

v10-l1.grammarNote: kottalar is kottu (cluster) + alar (blossom); kuḻali yōṭu has inserted glide y and associative -ōṭu; vicayaṟku is dative singular of vicayaṉ (Arjuna); vikirtaṉ is derived from Sanskrit vikṛta ('one who assumes varied forms / the Transcendent').

v10-l2.source: மத்தமும் மதியும் நாகம் முடிமே லணிந்தென் உளமே புகுந்த அதனால்
v10-l2.roman: mattamum matiyum nākam muṭimē laṇinteṉ uḷamē pukunta ataṉāl
v10-l2.english: {4:wearing}{0: datura,}{1: the crescent moon,}{2: and the serpent}{3: upon His crest,}{6: entered}{4: my}{5: very heart;}{7: therefore,}
v10-l2.grammarNote: Sandhi breaks across tokens: `muṭi mēl` + `aṇintu` + `eṉ` yields surface tokens `muṭimē` and `laṇinteṉ`. Relative participle `pukunta` modifies causal instrumental pronoun `ataṉāl`. The English presents the entry as a complete clause followed by therefore; this expresses the same causal relation without treating pukunta as a finite Tamil verb.

v10-l3.source: புத்தரொ டமணை வாதில் அழிவிக்கும் அண்ணல் திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே திருநீறு செம்மை திடமே
v10-l3.roman: puttaro ṭamaṇai vātil aḻivikkum aṇṇal tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē tirunīṟu cemmai tiṭamē
v10-l3.english: {4:the exalted Lord’s }{5:sacred ash }{3:defeats }{0:Buddhists }{1:and Jains }{2:in debate—}{6:its goodness }{7:is assured; }{8:the sacred ash’s }{9:goodness }{10:is assured; }{11:the sacred ash’s }{12:goodness }{13:is assured.}

words.gloss: causes defeat; here, the sacred ash defeats opponents in debate

v10-l3.grammarNote: Aḻivikkum is a causative relative form attached to the full noun phrase aṇṇal tirunīṟu: the Lord’s sacred ash is the effective subject. Cemmai is its goodness or excellence; tiṭamē affirms that this is assured. The three performed occurrences are retained individually.

v10-l4.source: அத்தகு நல்ல நல்ல அவை நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v10-l4.roman: attaku nalla nalla avai nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v10-l4.english: {0:Such things are}{1: good,}{2: good;}{3: they are}{4: good,}{5: good—}{8:exceedingly so}{6,7: for His devotees.}
v10-l4.grammarNote: Reduplication of `nalla` emphasizes absolute auspiciousness. Sandhi split across tokens: `aṭiyār` + `avarkku` -> `aṭiyā` and `ravarkku`.

v10-extra.source: அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே நல்ல நல்ல அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே அடியா ரவர்க்கு மிகவே
v10-extra.roman: aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē nalla nalla aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē aṭiyā ravarkku mikavē
v10-extra.english: {0,1:For His devotees, }they are {3:good, }{4:good—}{2:exceedingly so; }{5,6:for His devotees—}{7:exceedingly so; }{8,9:for His devotees—}{10:exceedingly so!}
v10-extra.grammarNote: Liturgical refrain repeating the cadence of the verse's final quarter (`aṭiyāravarkku mikavē`).

v11-l1.source: தேனமர் பொழில்கொள் ஆலை விளைசெந்நெல் துன்னி வளர்செம்பொன் எங்கும் நிகழ
v11-l1.roman: tēṉamar poḻilkoḷ ālai viḷaicennel tuṉṉi vaḷarcempoṉ eṅkum nikaḻa
v11-l1.english: Amid {0:honey-rich }{1:groves, }{2:sugarcane mills, }and {3:ripening red rice }{4:clustered together, }{5:fine gold abounding }{6:everywhere }{7:in sight,}
v11-l1.grammarNote: Infinitive `nikaḻa` functions adverbially/circumstantially ('as ... shines/manifests'). Compound chain: `tēṉ-amar` (honey-settling), `poḻil-koḷ` (grove-bearing), `viḷai-cem-nel` (ripening-red-paddy), `vaḷar-cem-poṉ` (growing-fine-gold).

v11-l2.source: நான்முகன் ஆதி யாய பிரமா புரத்து மறைஞான ஞான முனிவன்
v11-l2.roman: nāṉmukaṉ āti yāya piramā purattu maṟaiñāṉa ñāṉa muṉivaṉ
v11-l2.english: {6:the wise }{7:sage, }{5:versed in Vedic knowledge, }{3,4:of Brahmapuram, }{1,2:which takes its name from }{0:the Four-faced One,}

words.gloss: origin or beginning; here, the origin of the city’s name
being or becoming; linking the origin to Brahmapuram

v11-l2.grammarNote: Nāṉmukaṉ is the Four-faced One. Āti yāya relates the origin of Brahmapuram to him; it does not say that he owns the city. Maṟaiñāṉa gives Vedic knowledge, and ñāṉa qualifies the sage as wise. The English subject is this sage, continued by spoke in the next row.

v11-l3.source: தானுறு கோளும் நாளும் அடியாரை வந்து நலியாத வண்ணம் உரைசெய்
