verse-2-put-kaput-sune.grammarNote: Coordinated sentence using adversative para; first clause has masculine plural agreement (pūta kapūta sune haĩ); second clause has feminine singular agreement (mātā sunī kumātā) with the auxiliary hai omitted after sunī.

na-suktam-napi-dhyanam.source: न सूक्तं नापि ध्यानं च न न्यासो न च वार्चनम्
na-suktam-napi-dhyanam.roman: na sūktaṁ nāpi dhyānaṁ ca na nyāso na ca vārcanam
na-suktam-napi-dhyanam.english: {0,1:nor a hymn of praise}{2,3,4: or meditation,}{5,6: the placing of mantras on the body,}{7,8,9: or worship is required.}

words.gloss: ritual placing of mantras on the body: nyāsaḥ

na-suktam-napi-dhyanam.grammarNote: Continues the list of ritual prerequisites denied in contrast with reciting the Kuñjikā alone. Do not claim these practices are prohibited.

vicce-cabhayada-nityam.english: {0:Vicce—}{2:ever}{1: giving fearlessness;}{3: homage to you}{4: whose form is the mantra.}

words.gloss: and giver of fearlessness: ca + abhayadā
O you whose form is the mantra

vicce-cabhayada-nityam.grammarNote: The line itself associates vicce with fearlessness; this is textual symbolism, not a lexical etymology.

mantra-siddhim-kurushva-me.english: {1:bring}{0: the mantra to fulfilment}{2: for me.}
mantra-siddhim-kurushva-me.grammarNote: Direct second-person request, continuing the preceding genitive: bring about the accomplishment of Goddess Saptaśatī’s mantra for me. Siddhi is effective ritual accomplishment, not a generic substitution of enlightenment.

idam-tu-kunjika-stotram.english: {0,1:This}{3: Hymn}{2: of the Little Key}{6: is for}{5: awakening}{4: the mantra.}

danshtrakaralavadane.source:
दंष्ट्राकरालवदने शिरोमालाविभूषणे।
चामुण्डे मुण्डमथने नारायणि नमोऽस्तु ते॥
danshtrakaralavadane.roman:
daṃṣṭrākarālavadane śiromālāvibhūṣaṇe |
cāmuṇḍe muṇḍamathane nārāyaṇi namo'stu te ||
danshtrakaralavadane.english: {0:Fang-}{1:fierce} {2:of face,}{5: adorned} {4:with a garland} {3:of heads,}{6: Cāmuṇḍā,}{8: crusher of} {7:Muṇḍa—}{9:Nārāyaṇī,}{10: homage}{11: to you.}

words.gloss: face: O you whose face, vocative
O Goddess named for the slaying of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa; Cāmuṇḍā
O universal Goddess related in name to Nārāyaṇa/Viṣṇu; Nārāyaṇī

danshtrakaralavadane.grammarNote: Concrete fierce imagery remains; heads are not silently changed to flowers or ornaments.

ral-ke-khushiyan-manaiyan-kamaal-ho-gaya.source: ਰਲ ਕੇ ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ੀਆਂ ਮਨਾਈਆਂ ਕਮਾਲ ਹੋ ਗਿਆ
ral-ke-khushiyan-manaiyan-kamaal-ho-gaya.roman: ral ke kẖuśīā̃ manāīā̃ kamāl ho giā

words.gloss: having; links the preceding action to the main clause
become; with giā, the event or resulting state comes about
completes ho giā: has come about or become

ral-ke-khushiyan-manaiyan-kamaal-ho-gaya.grammarNote: Ral ke is joining together; the shared celebrants are implicit, rendered as communal we. No added ownership of the joys.

o-ral-ke-khushiyan-manaiyan-kamaal-ho-ga.source: ਓ ਰਲ ਕੇ ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ੀਆਂ ਮਨਾਈਆਂ ਕਮਾਲ ਹੋ ਗਿਆ
o-ral-ke-khushiyan-manaiyan-kamaal-ho-ga.roman: o ral ke kẖuśīā̃ manāīā̃ kamāl ho giā
o-ral-ke-khushiyan-manaiyan-kamaal-ho-ga.english: {0:Oh,}{1,2: together}{4: we celebrated}{3: joys}{5,6,7:—what a marvel!}

words.gloss: having; links the preceding action to the main clause
become; with giā, the event or resulting state comes about
completes ho giā: has come about or become

o-ral-ke-khushiyan-manaiyan-kamaal-ho-ga.grammarNote: Initial o is an exclamation; communal celebrants are implicit in the together clause.

khushiyan-manaunde-saare-khushiyan-manau.grammarNote: Two full repetitions; everyone is the agent.

pooja-keeti-jagg-vi-keeta-keeta-maa-da-p.source: ਪੂਜਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਜੱਗ ਵੀ ਕੀਤਾ, ਕੀਤਾ ਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਪਾਠ ਹੈ
pooja-keeti-jagg-vi-keeta-keeta-maa-da-p.roman: pūjā kītī jagg vī kītā, kītā mā̃ dā pāṭh hai
pooja-keeti-jagg-vi-keeta-keeta-maa-da-p.english: {0:Worship}{1: was performed,}{2: a sacrifice}{3: too}{4: was performed;}{6,7: Mother’s}{8: sacred recitation}{5,9: has been performed.}

words.gloss: sacrificial rite; here ritual sacrifice, not jag, the world
Mother; the Goddess addressed as mother
recitation; reading of a sacred text
is; auxiliary of the completed action

pooja-keeti-jagg-vi-keeta-keeta-maa-da-p.grammarNote: Unstated worshippers act in completed clauses. Jagg in the ritual sequence is sacrificial worship, not a world being created. Mā̃ dā pāṭh is recitation devoted to Mother, not Mother herself reading.

words.gloss: Mother; the Goddess addressed as mother
recitation; reading of a sacred text
is; auxiliary of the completed action

keeta-maa-da-paath-hai-keeta-maa-da-paat.grammarNote: Two repetitions; unnamed worshippers perform the recitation devoted to Mother.

bhagat-lagaunde-maa-diyan-bhetan-goonj-r.source: ਭਗਤ ਲਗਾਉਂਦੇ ਮਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਭੇਟਾਂ ਗੂੰਜ ਰਹੇ ਜੈਕਾਰੇ
bhagat-lagaunde-maa-diyan-bhetan-goonj-r.roman: bhagat lagāũde mā̃ dīā̃ bheṭā̃ gūñj rahe jaikāre
bhagat-lagaunde-maa-diyan-bhetan-goonj-r.english: {0:Devotees}{1: sing}{4: offerings}{2,3: to Mother;}{7: cries of victory}{5,6: resound.}

words.gloss: Mother; the Goddess addressed as mother
offerings; here devotional songs offered to Mother

bhagat-lagaunde-maa-diyan-bhetan-goonj-r.grammarNote: Mā̃ dīā̃ bheṭā̃ in this singing context are devotional song-offerings. The devotees sing; acclamations resound. Do not reverse the two agents or make Mother the singer.

line_03.source: ये मंत्र है माँ चामुंडा का इसमें महाशक्ति समाती है
line_03.roman: ye mantra hai mā̃ cāmuṇḍā kā ismẽ mahāśakti samātī hai
line_03.english: {0:This }{2:is }{3,4,5:Mother Cāmuṇḍā’s}{1: mantra; }{7:great power}{8,9: resides}{6: within it.}

words.gloss: Mother; affectionate address for the Goddess
the Goddess named for slaying Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa

line_03.grammarNote: The Mother’s mantra is the subject of the first clause; great power is what resides in it in the second.

v010.source: बलिप्रदाने पूजायामग्निकार्ये महोत्सवे सर्वं ममैतच्चरितम् उच्चार्यं श्राव्यमेव च
v010.roman: balipradāne pūjāyāmagnikārye mahotsave sarvaṃ mamaitaccaritam uccāryaṃ śrāvyameva ca
v010.english: {1:When}{0: offerings}{1: are given,}{2: in worship,}{4: in}{3: fire}{4: rites}{6: and at}{5: great}{6: festivals,}{9: this}{7: entire}{10: account of}{8: my}{10: deeds}{11: should be recited aloud}{13: and}{12: made heard.}

words.gloss: great; mahā, vowel joined to utsava
my; mama, vowel joined to etat
should indeed be made audible: śrāvyam + eva

v010.grammarNote: Four locative settings govern the paired gerundives uccāryam and śrāvyam. Śrāvyam is causative in force: made audible, recited for others to hear.

v023.source: श्रुतं हरति पापानि तथारोग्यं प्रयच्छति रक्षां करोति भूतेभ्यो जन्मनां कीर्तनं मम
v023.roman: śrutaṃ harati pāpāni tathārogyaṃ prayacchati rakṣāṃ karoti bhūtebhyo janmanāṃ kīrtanaṃ mama
v023.english: {0,1,2:Heard, this account removes sins}{3,4: and grants health.}{9: Recounting }{10:my }{8:births}{5,6,7: gives protection from spirits.}
v023.grammarNote: Śrutam refers to the neuter Māhātmyam. Janmanāṃ kīrtanam is subject of rakṣāṃ karoti; mama modifies births/manifestations. Bhūtebhyaḥ is ablative, protection from spirits here, not protection offered to every creature.

line_06.english: {9:Here}{11: I worship}{7: Mahā}{10:sarasvatī}—{10:Sarasvatī}{8: called}{7: “Great”}—{2:arisen}{1: from}{0: Gaurī’s}{1: body,}{5,6: foundation}{4: of the}{3: three}{4: worlds,}{15: destroyer}{12: of Śumbha}{13: and the other}{14: Daityas.}

words.gloss: having as its first part; accusative feminine
Śumbha, the demon; vowel joined to ādi
Daityas, descendants of Diti; daitya, vowel joined to ardinī

line_06.grammarNote: All accusative descriptions qualify Sarasvatīm. Gaurī-deha-samudbhavām specifies arising from Gaurī’s body; tri-jagatām is genitive, of the three worlds. Mahā-pūrvām specifies that Mahā precedes the name Sarasvatī, yielding Mahāsarasvatī; it does not mean primordial here. Atra means here; anubhaje is first-person singular reverent worship. Śumbhādi includes Śumbha and the other Daityas.

v1-a.source: न मन्त्रं नो यन्त्रं तदपि च न जाने स्तुतिमहो
v1-a.roman: na mantraṃ no yantraṃ tadapi ca na jāne stutimaho

words.gloss: mantra, a sacred formula for recitation
yantra, a sacred diagram used in worship

v1-a.grammarNote: Mantram, yantram and stutim are the objects of jāne, first person singular. Tad api: even that.

v6-b.english: {2:a pauper, }{0:free of }{1:dread, }{3:roams }{4:long }{3:at his ease }{6:amid gold }{5:by the ten million—}

words.gloss: takes his pleasure; moves at ease

v6-b.grammarNote: Viharati: moves about at ease. Kanakaiḥ is an instrumental plural.

words.gloss: O Aparṇā, who in her austerity took not even a leaf

v6-c.grammarNote: Manu-varṇe viśati is a locative absolute: when a syllable of the mantra enters. Aparṇe, karṇe and varṇe rhyme.

v3-b.source: परं तेषां मध्ये विरलतरलोऽहं तव सुतः ।
v3-b.roman: paraṃ teṣāṃ madhye viralataralo'haṃ tava sutaḥ
v3-b.grammarNote: Virala-taralaḥ … sutaḥ is the predicate of aham: I am your son, rare and wavering.

words.gloss: O dark one; Śyāmā, the Goddess
an orphan; one with no protector

v9-c.grammarNote: Anātha, without a protector, is also the word for an orphan. The verb dhatse follows in the next line.

v9-d.grammarNote: Ucitam stands as a predicate with tava eva: fitting of you alone.
